Overall, the “table” functions as a **navigation map** for the manual section describing how to interact with the graphical interface (menus, editing/cutting operations, selection mechanisms, and categories of commands). It organizes sections and subsections of a **SOFiSTiK AG “Manual, Service Pack 2025-4 Build 146”** for the software suite related to **graphical representation of finite elements and beam structures**. The content is copyright-protected and includes a standard foreword-style disclaimer.

## Structure and fields (implied columns)
While no explicit column headers are shown, each entry follows a consistent pattern equivalent to two logical fields:

1. **Section/command identifier** (left):  
   Examples include “3.1 Input Language”, “3.3 CTRL”, “3.4 DB”, and many subsequent short codes such as “SIZE”, “AND”, “SCHH”, “GRID”, “PERS”, etc.
2. **Topic title** + **page reference** (right):  
   Each item ends with a page number like **3-1, 3-6, 3-9, …**, indicating where the detailed documentation for that identifier begins.

This makes the table effectively a **mapping from internal keyword/code → description topic → manual page**.

## Key content areas covered
The snippet is concentrated in the **“Input and Output Description”** part of the manual, under **Chapter 3**. It begins with:

- **3.1 Input Language** (page 3-1)
- **3.2 Program parameters** (3-1)
- **3.3 CTRL – General Control Parameters** (3-6)
- **3.4 DB – Change of the Database** (3-9)
- **3.5 SIZE – Scale and Paper Size** (3-10)
- Then a long list of graphical/output-related parameters and directives.

Major themes include:

- **Text and labeling**: `SCHH`, `SCH2`, `SCH3`, `GRID`, `LEGO`, `PERS`, etc.  
- **Colors and styling**: `PALE` (color palette), `COL0`, `COL1`, `COLB` (background), `FILL` (fill patterns), `COLO`-style entries for line/text/marker types.  
- **Selection and views**: `SELE`, `GRP`, `BOX`, `SEL`, `VIEW`, including different ways to specify what is displayed or processed.
- **Visibility and deformation**: `VIST`, `DEFO` (deformed structure).
- **Geometric/graphic drawing operations**: `MOVE`, `DRAW`, `TEXT`, `POST` (position marking), `NIVE` (level symbol), `CURV` (axes), `AXIS`.
- **Special structural/engineering representations**: `DSIR` (SIR sections), `CUTP` (cutting pattern areas), `LC` (load case selection), `DSGN` (representation specification), `ARR0` (vector layout).
- **Output/list handling**: `LIST – Lists properties` (3-100) and `STRU – Representation of structure values` (3-102).

## Cross-links to output sections
Earlier in the same snippet, the manual’s **Output Description** includes named outputs such as:
- **LOAD – Load Pictures**, **NODE – Results in Nodes**, **BEAM – Beam Element Results**, **QUAD**, **ISOL**, **SECT**, **BRIC**, **INTE**, each with its own page range indicator.

## Overall purpose of the “table”
The dataset functions as a **navigational index** for RAG retrieval: users can search a keyword/code (e.g., “CTRL”, “SELE”, “COL0”, “BEAM”) and jump to the relevant manual section and page, covering both **input directives** and **output visualization/results representations** for finite element/beam structures.

 GRAPHIC is a graphical program for the finite element and framework analysis modules of SOFiSTiK with a CDBASE database (e.g. FEABENCH, TALPA, ASE, STAR2, MAXIMA, BE- MESS, AQB, DYNA, HASE or HYDRA). The program allows the representation of almost all information saved in the database. These ones are in particular:
 Structures: Elements and nodes with or without numbers
 Support conditions
 Elastic foundations
 Cross sections and cross section values
 Material values
 Local coordinate systems
 Results: Principal stresses or principal moments as well as normal
 stresses
 (for plane structures according to magnitude and direction)
 Nodal and element loads
 Reinforcements in areas (contour lines)
 Non–linear stresses, strains and crack widths
 Vectors of velocities
 Potential values
 Deformed structure
 Bending forms of structure
 Internal forces and deformations for frame and girder systems
 Influence lines Beam loads Beam stiffnesses Maximum stresses Reinforcements
 The graphical representation can occur according to the result type in different manner:
 – Single lines or arrows with defined (scaled) length
 – Numerical values
 – Designations
 – Line representations for frame and girder systems or for
 – Cuts in plane structures
 – Isolines
 – Hatch or fill patterns

An interactive surface (GMEN) exists for the operating WINDOWS systems.
 An arbitrary input file can be read, graphical modifications can occur and an input file can be output again with this interactive version. In this case the interactive processing can be omitted for a new calculation of a known system.
 The drawings are arranged into graphics, pictures and layers. Every layer contains drawing elements (vectors, lines, text,...). A picture can consist of one or several layers which can lie over each other. A graphics is divided in one or several pictures which are positioned side by side.
 The WINDOWS version allows the direct layout of a representation with an immediate check of the result. The parameters can be changed or a new drawing can be requested if a picture is not liked.
 Two variants of the representation of result types are possible with the program GRAPHIC:
 1. the Edit box
 2. the result tree
 The working with the result tree is suitable for the fast generation of the desired pictures with- out user–specific definitions. The processing with the Edit box is recommended, if specific definitions become desired or necessary.

 The dialogue area at the lower picture border corresponds to a normal text screen. The inputs of the user with the keyboard, error estimates and requests are represented here. In this case the lines are shifted upward.
 The position of the pointer is symbolized in the graphical window via the so–called cursor. The form of the cursor can change according to the task. A pickbox is represented fundamentally, if a point or a line should be picked.

Subsequently the process of the GRAPHIC initialization is shown. In this case all settings are defined for the next layer to be generated after the start of the program.
 • Fixed values defined in the program are set directly after the start of the program.
 • Then the environment variables (GRAFSIZE,...,GRAFD000...) are searched for in the sys- tem environment or the file SOFISTIK.DEF. This environment variables are set, if they are available.
 • Then a predefinition file WINGRAF.DEF is searched for. This file contains the predefinitions as inputs in the CADINP format. The file WINGRAF.DEF is searched for according to the following rules:
 – first in the local working directory
 – then in the SOFiSTiK path, in all directories which are defined in the SOFiSTiK environ- ment variable
 – then in the directory in which the program (WINGRAF.EXE) is
 – If there are still no search results, the environment variables are evaluated in the order of CDBASETMP and TEMP.
 The file WINGRAF.DEF is stored manually, not automatically. This file contains the definitions of the interactive buttons, which are saved with the help of the INTE records.
 Furthermore the most important defaults can be defined in this file for a new graphic (SIZE, SCHH, COLO ...). The size of the saved data can be defined with the command predefinitions of drawing in the menu options.

The image is a diagrammatic UI/graphics manual figure titled “Figure 2.3: Cursor types” that illustrates different mouse cursor representations used for object selection and drawing operations in a coordinate-based CAD-like program. The background shows a 2D grid of blue dashed lines on white, with thicker black axes/screen borders near the center and lower areas, emphasizing a “picture plane” or viewport. The overall layout is split visually into regions marked with letter labels (a–e), each near a corresponding cursor glyph.

At the top-left region labeled **(a)**, a cursor graphic appears as a **target cross**: two short perpendicular line segments intersect, forming a small crosshair. This indicates the cursor type for **precise target** snapping (intersection of two short lines).

Near the center-right area labeled **(b)**, a larger cursor crosshair is shown. It consists of **two long perpendicular lines** crossing at a center point, producing a longer cross indicating **intersection of two long lines**.

On the right side, the region near the **(c)** label shows a cursor preview resembling a **rubber-band line**: a straight line segment extends from a start point (near the left of that small region) toward the current point being chosen, indicating dynamic feedback for operations like **cutting/line definitions** between two points.

Around the lower center-right, labeled **(d)**, there is a cursor depiction of a **window/rectangle selection**. A rectangular outline is drawn at a **diagonal orientation** (one corner at the starting point, opposite corner at the current point), illustrating a **window rectangle** used to define a box/selection area.

At the lower-left region labeled **(e)**, the figure shows a small **pickbox**—a compact square/box outline. The box is sized to represent the **snap radius** for object snaps (e.g., point snap). A small red/orange marker near the pickbox suggests a reference point being snapped to.

Several cursors appear at different heights, but all are plotted over the same grid to clarify snapping geometry. The diagram supports the accompanying text about how mouse clicks return coordinates, how keyboard mode interrupts/ends with ESC/RETURN, and how cursor appearance changes depending on the active command mode (target intersection, rubber line, window rectangle, or pick mode).

If the left mouse button is pressed in the graphic area, the corresponding coordinates of the picture plane are returned to GRAPHIC. The program changes to the keyboard, if a key on the keyboard is pressed. If the ESC–key or the RETURN key are used, the keyboard mode is interrupted or ended. It is changed to the mouse.

 target cross intersection of two short lines

Frequently numerical values are necessary. These values are input via the keyboard in GRAPHIC. In this case the request in the dialogue area can show the values proposed by the program in peaked clips (e.g. < 0>). If the user has the same opinion, then he confirms it with return. Otherwise one or more values can be input separately with comma. Two commas following immediately or missing values do not change the corresponding value. The request is repeated, if the values are no numbers or if too much numbers are input. Numerical values has to be closed with RETURN of the keyboard (and not with the mouse button RETURN).

Texts are expected via the keyboard. If a standard text is planned, it is shown in peaked clips. This text can be accepted with return, or a new text is input. The return key deletes the input text and escape interrupts the request. The text input is ended automatically, if the maximum number of the signs is reached. Also texts have to be closed with RETURN of the keyboard (and not with the mouse button RETURN). Frequently also numbers are necessary within the text inputs.

The cursor can be moved to an arbitrary position in the graphical window. The coordinates are delivered from the picture plane to GRAPHIC with a click of the left mouse button. The missing third coordinate results from the current representation specification.
 The coordinates can be input also via the keyboard separately with comma. In this case the coordinates can be outside of the screen. If no Z coordinate is defined, it is calculated from the equation of the picture plane and the available coordinates.
 GRAPHIC allows like the program AutoCAD also the definition of local screen coordinate sys- tems as well as polar or relative coordinates.
 The polar coordinates are input with a < between the first value (radius) and the second value (angle). The relative coordinates to the previous point are defined with a prepositioned @.

The menu File contains the basic commands for the file management. Some commands of
 this menu are available also as toolbar buttons. The commands are described subsequently:
 New
 The just processed data file is saved as SOFiSTiK metafile. Then this file can be considered, stimulated, printed with the program REPORT BROWSER. On the other hand other graphic formats (e.g. DXF) can be generated.
 The values used for the representation are written as a list in a LST–file. The name results from the current document or from the database name, if no document name exists yet. The output can be limited to the current layer or the picture or the graphics in a dialogue box. Else the values of all graphics are written. Then this file can be considered and printed with the program WINTED.
 The input which led to the values is recorded as a batch input (as for the GRA file) in the so generated LST file. The lists can be formed differently. However, there is always a reference number (in general the element number or the number set in an intern way) and at least one result value (1st value). Also a 2nd and a 3rd value (for the main reinforcement, the transverse reinforcement or for the support components in the X, Y and Z direction) is available for the representation of some components (e.g. area reinforcement or support components). The section value at the beam axis is printed in addition to the results at line elements. The global insertion point or the group number is printed also for some results.
 Occurred changes can be taken back command–wise and produced also again.

The image is a technical diagram illustrating coordinate systems in 3D space, comparing/connecting Cartesian (orthogonal) axes to cylindrical coordinate concepts. A rectangular, box-like 3D frame is drawn in perspective, representing a spatial region. Three labeled axes are shown: the positive **X** axis is indicated by an arrow on the right side of the box labeled “X”; the positive **Y** axis is indicated by an arrow on the left side labeled “Y”; and the **Z** axis is indicated by a vertical arrow downward from the center area of the box labeled “Z”. The arrows suggest that X and Y extend horizontally in the plane of the box, while Z extends vertically.

Inside the box, a cylindrical-coordinate interpretation is depicted. There is a central vertical line passing through the figure, aligned with the Z direction. Around this central line, a curved arc or circular sector is drawn in a horizontal plane to indicate an angular parameter. The angle is labeled with the Greek letter **φ (phi)** near the arc.  Dialog box: Properties of the next SIR cut

The cutting pattern lines at the membrane structures are defined with the commands of the submenu Cutting pattern. Therefrom the geodetic isolines are determined. The resultant cut- ting pattern areas are transmitted to the program TEXTILE. The menu Cutting pattern contains the following commands:
 it is possible to allocate BRIC cuts, which should be generated, to an own group num- ber. Thus BRIC cuts with different directions can get for example different group numbers. BRIC cuts can be also deleted via their group number (see Delete BRIC cuts).
 A straight BRIC cut or a BRIC cut as polygon can be generated via
 The start point and the end point of the line are input interactively with the mouse or via the keyboard. If the user wants to input the relative coordinates with the keyboard, a @ must be input at first as in AutoCAD. BRIC cuts with several segments (polygon) retain their direction. The direction of single cuts is aligned.
 The deletion of cuts can be done via
 The selection of BRIC cuts in the active groups is done via an input in the dialogue area. The input for each single cut is Y = Yes (deleting) or N = No (not deleting). The input for all cuts is A. The selection is accepted with ENTER and is canceled with ESC. If only the BRIC cuts of a specific group number are supposed to be selected, the group numbers of the remaining BRIC cuts have to be switched off via the Group definition .
 Note:
 For a better result representation it is possible to define the representation of the BRIC structure or BRIC surface at Group definition .

Additional drawing elements, for instance Lines, Texts, Positioning symbols, Level sym- bols, Dimensional lines as well as Axes, can be inserted into the drawing.
 Subsequently the commands are described:
 With the command Insert position symbol it is possible to insert positions with and without a line. If only a click is done at a point, no line is printed. If a line is drawn in the graphic, then this line is printed too. The text for the position symbol is input in the dialogue area below. The size of the position symbol can be changed interactively before the end (after one return).
 It is possible to define multiple dimensional lines with this command. The text has then the default, the distance between the start and end point.
 The submenus contain the commands for the drawing and the deletion of these additional elements and for the definition of specific properties.
 Additional elements (no axes or cuts) are created with system coordinates if they are positioned inside the structure (SBOX). Therefore it is possible to check these elements if they are outside the structure, when the BOX or GROUP selection are be changed. This check can be switched on / off.
 All active Additional elements (no axes or cuts) can be deleted at once.

The menu View contains the basic commands for the layout definition and for the view. Some commands of this menu are available also as toolbar buttons. Subsequently the commands are described:
 This command switches on or off the indication of the global coordinate system.
 rotates the Text about 90 degrees
 beam ends can be plotted.)
 In an analog mode options for the other representation types are available for the user.
 Each selection is removed with the command Show all. All elements are be visible.
 A selection includes all selections via box, group or single selection. A selection in- cludes a view (line of vision) too. The properties of all defined selections can be edited with the command Selection manager in a tabular form.
 A new selection is defined with the with the command Define new selection. This se- lection includes the current box, group and single selection in addition with the current line of vision. A description of the selection can be defined here. This description is shown in the first line of picture description.
 Normally the selection is used for all layers of the current picture. But sometimes it makes sense to use only the current layer, eg if the first layer shall include the whole structure and the second layer shall have a selection of a result. After setting Selection by Layer the next selections are used on the current layer till the command is be reseted again.

This menu includes the commands for geometric selection of elements via the location of their nodes.
 After the definition of a group selection all elements are represented with this command.
 ie
 Individual elements or element types (e.g. beam elements, area elements) can be cho- sen with the group selection for the representation. The group number of an element is equal to the integer part of the term element number/group divisor.
 Group divisor can be redefined temporary in GRAPHIC, if the elements were defined with a fixed group divisor (divisor>0) during the system generation. Groups can be divided or combined on this way.
 But the better way is to define Secondary groups with program SOFIMSHA. These secondary groups are available for the most programs, not only for GRAPHIC.

This menu includes the commands for selection of specific node types.
 Free nodes are not part of any element. Therefore group selection can not act on these nodes. All free nodes can be switched on / off with this command.
 Nodal sequences (EDGE) have no group number. Therefore group selection can not act on these nodes. All nodal sequences can be switched on / off with this command.
 Normally BRIC inner nodes are not visible. Only the nodes on the BRIC surface are visible. All inner nodes can be switched on with this command so that all results (extremal values) on this nodes are visible.
 Sometimes invalid nodes are created during an invalid system generation. In this case these nodes can be switched on here.
 The nodes of a domain composition can be switched with this command.

This menu includes the commands for visibility of BRIC surfaces.
 Front sides
 The front sides are visible depending on the line of vision.
 All BRIC outer sides are visible.
 Inner BRIC group border sides are visible too.
 No BRIC surfaces are displayed. This makes sense if BRIC cut areas were defined.
 All BRIC elements are displayed, the inner ones too.

The menu Extras contains the commands to change the units, the submenu Macros for the additional informations and for the start of other SOFiSTiK programs (ANIMATOR, REPORT BROWSER, TEDDY).
 The distance between 2 points can be measured.
 The distance is output in the global components.
 An angle between 3 three–dimensional points can be measured.
 A node or element may be searched via its number. Some properties, e.g. node coor- dinates and node support, are shown additionally.
 the current statics input file (.DAT) is used.

 Sets units of output to the default from file WINGRAF.DEF.

Always recurring manipulations and settings can occur via the request of a CADINP–based macro. Macros is a submenu of the menu Extras.
 Only the input values of the current layer, picture or graphics are changed with the first drawing request (records STRU, NODE, BEAM or QUAD). If more drawing requests are defined, then the layers arising newly are placed behind the current layer.

 The selected macro is copied into the clipboard. Then the use in the layer tree is possi- ble (with the command Replace).

The menu Options contains transparent and non–transparent commands of general kind. Transparent means that this command can be requested at any time even within a command sequence. In this case the current menu does not have to be left or the command or the command sequence do not have to be interrupted. Some of these commands are directly accessible also in other menus.

WING processes input **blockwise**: a single input block ends with the literal **`END`**, and all records inside are handled sequentially.

A central distinction is made between **attribute records** and **drawing orders**. Most records are **attribute records** whose values are stored during parsing and **become visible only in the next drawing output**. Drawing orders trigger creation/reuse of drawings and determine *what kind of result data is plotted*. Additionally, there is a special mechanism: if the drawing order argument literal **`DSGN`** is entered for **`TYPE`** in drawing orders, then **only the attributes are set** (no new result plot is produced). - **`STRU`**: plot of structural elements, system values, input items, numbering and designations; also deformed structures for displacements, eigenmode shapes, or stress areas.
- **`LOAD`**: loads in vector form, line representations, or area blocks.
- **`NODE`**: node results such as displacements, support reactions, boundary forces (vector or numeric representation).
- **`QUAD`**: scalar variables, vectors, tensors, or derived values for quadrilateral elements; includes options for numeric or fill-pattern representation.
- **`BEAM`**: line representation for frame/girder systems (e.g., bending moments) with numerical designation.
- **`ISOL`**: isolines for QUAD elements.
- **`SECT`**: results along cuts through the structure.
- **`BRIC`**: results at volume elements.

A further rule is that the **structure plot** is repeated as a contour for the orders **`LOAD`, `NODE`, `QUAD`, `BEAM`, `ISOL`, `SECT`, and `BRIC`**. Actual output plots are produced only for records **`STRU`** and those drawing orders; all other input records are attributes.

## Item: OPT

Its unit is shown as **LIT/-**, and the default entry is **0** (with the Description indicating that the practical default option is “DEFA” for structure behavior). The table’s **Description** enumerates supported OPT keywords and explains their purpose and typical effect:

- **NOHE**: Inserts the next **HEAD** line without deleting previous HEAD lines. Example context: to change a “ZTVK” head but continue with the 5th HEAD line, the user can use `CTRL NOHE 5`.
- **GSTR**: Controls the *default structure type* used to draw results. Different structure presets are possible (DEFA, NO, CONT, FULL, MESH, AX). The description indicates “complete structure” is typically used for numbering structures (e.g., `STRU NUME ENO`) while contour/other modes apply otherwise.
- **DEF**: Selects the “level of defaults” that this input is based on (i.e., which predefined defaults file or mode is used).
- **EMPT**: Defines behavior for blank or invalid sheets/pictures/layers; it controls whether invalid pages/layers are generated and how validity is checked.
- **MEAS**: Controls measurability of distributions; may also temporarily select another representation.
- **AXIS**: Selects how axis lines are represented (e.g., full axis lines for structure representation, otherwise as hints; includes modes like CURR/FULL).
- **CUT**: Controls use of stored vs generated cuts for area elements from the database (SOFIPLUS), including deletion/replacement logic.
- **WARN**: Allows warnings to be switched off; the number of warning instances is governed by **VAL** and **V2**.
- **REPR**: Enables correction of an invalid or inconsistent representation (YES means correct; OFF/NO means do not correct and subsequent behavior may be governed by CTRL EMPT).
- **EDGE**: Controls how opposite spring directions are unified when representing results along **EDGE** (NO/YES/FULL), including a note that sign of results can change in FULL mode due to coupling springs.

The column lists **Default = DEFA** inside the OPT description area, reflecting that **GSTR-like default behavior** (structure drawing defaults) is typically “DEFA”.

**VAL** is “Value of the option” with unit **\*** (generic numeric). The Default is **!** (unspecified/indicator). In the surrounding context, **VAL** is used primarily with **WARN** to define which warning number(s) may be switched off.

## Item: V2
**V2** is the “Second value of the option” with unit **\*** and Default **-**. In context, **V2** is used with **WARN** to define the number of times a warning may occur before it is suppressed.

This table defines the configuration record `SIZE`, which controls paper selection, scaling, and layout framing for generating plots/pictures (and, depending on format, legends and headers) for the “GRAPHIC / REPORT BROWSER” system.

### Columns
- **Item**: parameter name used in the input record.
- **Description**: meaning and allowed values/interpretation.
- **Unit**: measurement unit for numeric entries.
- **Default**: the default value when the record is not explicitly set.

### Parameters and semantics

1. **TYPE** (paper size / format selection)  
   - **Meaning**: selects the paper format implicitly.  
   - **Values**: `- / LIT` indicates a numeric format code; `WIN` is the default meaning “current GRAPHIC printer format” (the printer last used in an interactive session).  
   - **Orientation**: positive values imply landscape; a **minus sign** selects portrait orientation.

2. **SC** (scale)  
   - **Meaning**: the drawing scale used for reproduction.  
   - **Special meanings**:
     - `0` → choose the *largest possible drawing*, i.e., format filling regardless of engineering scale constraints.
     - `-` (unspecified) → the program may automatically choose an engineering-style best fit.
     - `*` (star) → “use this scale” (force usage rather than auto-choosing).
   - **Default**: `-` (unspecified).

3. **W** (paper width)  
   - **Meaning**: explicit paper width in **cm**; can be provided instead of using `TYPE`.  
   - **Interaction**: if one of `W` or `H` is set to zero, the other dimension can drive automatic paper/scale selection.
   - **Default**: `-` (not fixed).

4. **H** (paper height)  
   - **Meaning**: explicit paper height in **cm**, analogous to `W`.  
   - **Interaction**: if only one of `W`/`H` is zero, the scale definition may change depending on the other dimension.
   - **Default**: `-` (not fixed).

5. **MARG** (border/margin behavior)  
   - **Unit**: `LIT` indicates a literal/enum value.  
   - **Default**: `FULL`.  
   - **Values**:
     - `OFF`: no border drawn.
     - `NO`: draws an **inner border + scale area**; `W` and `H` define the drawable area for single-sheet plotters/laser printers.
     - `YES`: creates a **free border** around the drawing area using a margin of **2 cm** (otherwise **0.5 cm**).
     - `FULL`: draws an additional outer border aligned to the **outer paper limits** (typical for drum plotters).

6. **FORM** (form/frame type)  
   - **Meaning**: selects the border frame style.  
   - **Default**: `URS`.  
   - **Values**:
     - `STAN`: standard frame for pictures only.
     - `ZTVK`: ZTVK-88 frame for pictures only.
     - `URS`: `REPORT BROWSER` frame, used for tables and pictures.

7. **HLEG** (legend field under the plot)  
   - **Meaning**: reserved horizontal/vertical field (height) **in cm** under the plot for legend placement.  
   - **Default**: `1.0`.

8. **WLEG** (right-side legend field)  
   - **Meaning**: reserved field width **in cm** for an additional legend to the right of the plot.  
   - **Default**: `0.0`.

### Notes on related layout behavior (context)
- The system also supports header bands and legend sizing via other records (e.g., `SCHH`, `SLEG`, `HEAD` lines).  
- Plot positioning relative to title bands depends on the format height (bands between plot for ~27–30 cm, otherwise bands may appear beside/right for larger formats).  
- Borders/margins impact where the drawable area and coordinate/dimension lines can be placed.

Overall, this table is the authoritative schema for choosing **paper format (TYPE or W/H)**, **scaling (SC)**, and **frame/margin strategy (MARG + FORM)**, with dedicated reserved spaces (**HLEG/WLEG**) for legends.

The table describes the **SIZE** / **SIZ2** parameter set used by a GRAPHIC plotting system to define **paper size, orientation, margins, title bands, legend sizing, and multi-plot layout**, as well as related coordinate-dimensioning behavior. It also introduces supporting records (e.g., **SCHH**, **COLO**, **LEGO**, **AND**, **VIEW**, **SCAL**) that affect text heights, legends, and coordinate presentation.

### 1) Inputs defining paper format and orientation
Paper size can be selected in two main ways:

1. **Implicit format via TYPE** (numeric DIN/other codes):
   - **0..6** correspond to DIN sizes, with optional **American formats** and **special HP plotter formats**.
   - A **leading minus sign** selects **portrait** orientation; otherwise landscape is default.
   - Explicit examples listed:
     - **URS / –URS**: “drawing paper without an external margin” (special no-margin mode).
     - **WIN / –WIN**: uses the current GRAPHIC printer format from the last interactive session; without it, **WINDOWS default printer** is used.
     - **9..9**: “Free format with W and H”.
     - **ANSI A–D**: A (11×8.5"), B (17×11"), C (22×17"), D (34×22").
     - **HP formats**: HP A–D and numbered HP1–HP4, with specific mm dimensions.

2. **Explicit dimensions via W and H**:
   - The user can set paper **width W** and **height H**, while **scale SC** may be computed automatically if not provided.
   - Setting **SC=0** forces the **largest possible drawing** regardless of engineering scale constraints (scale mentions 1:1, 1:2, 1:5, …).

### 2) Scale and automatic selection behavior
The table explains two interacting strategies:
- If the user selects the paper format via **TYPE**, the system chooses/adjusts **scale automatically** unless **SC** is explicitly given (and only when technically feasible).
- If the user specifies scale via **W and/or H**, then setting one of **W or H to zero** triggers automatic selection of an appropriate paper size. If only one is zero, scale definition can “drop” because it is inferred from the remaining dimension.

### 3) Margins: external/inner and control via SIZ2
- For most formats, the paper includes both:
  - **external margin**: defines the drawable paper limit (“margin”).
  - **inner margin**: offset from the external margin (often ~0.5 cm; may consider file margin).
- **URS / –URS** removes the external margin; later margin handling can be added during “REPORT BROWSER” reading (PLB stage).
- Print margins to release can be explicitly configured by **DRUL, DRUU, DRUL/DRUR** within **record SIZ2**, but otherwise defaults are used on a new SIZE call.

### 4) Title/header bands and placement rules
- Title bands are used to print designation/head lines.
- Band sizes are controlled by **HLEG**.
- **HEAD** line placement relative to margins depends on **FORM**:
  - With **FORM=STAN**, the inner margin is shifted so **HEAD lines appear between inner and external margins**.
- The system registers “user name” and “GRAPHIC name/version” within a small fixed margin area.
- For larger formats, title bands may appear at the **right side** of the plot; for medium formats (stated: heights **27–30 cm**), the plot is positioned **between** bands.

### 5) Legend sizing and text constraints
- Each picture gets its **own legend**.
- Legend height is controlled by **SLEG**.
- The table notes that legends are limited in number of lines; more lines may be possible with:
  - smaller text height via **SCHH** (including H1) for HEAD lines,
  - or enlarged legend height **HLEG**.

### 6) Multi-plot partitioning and explicit positioning
- The paper can contain multiple plots; partitioning may involve both height and width.
- Control literal format: **height x width** (e.g., digits **1–9** or letters **A–G** mapping to **10–16**).
- Plots are produced in boxes from left of beginning, then “above/below” logic; **AND** can jump to a specific position or define explicit sheet positions.
- A new paper is used when SIZE/SIZ2 is called again.

### 7) Coordinate axes, dimensioning, and related records
- Coordinate axes, scale (including reduction factors via **SCAL**), result designation, and a **1 cm sample line** are placed except for header lines.
- Dimensional lines of picture coordinates are placed within the inner border below and at the right side.
- The global coordinate origin is fixed at **(0.00, 0.00)**.
- Grid scaling matches geometry scaling.

Additionally, the table describes dimensioning two selected coordinates instead of picture coordinates for condensed diagrams. This requires selecting an observer viewpoint via **VIEW** so the desired **reduction scale** is achievable. Graphic decides which coordinate axis is horizontal/vertical based on the largest vertical component.

Overall, the table provides a comprehensive specification of how **paper format (TYPE/W/H), scale (SC), margins (SIZ2), header/legend sizing (HLEG, SLEG, SCHH), and plot partitioning (height×width via AND)** together determine the final plotted layout and coordinate presentation.

This table defines parameters related to how a drawing’s content is laid out on a paper/page, and how legends for individual pictures are sized.

**Columns and meaning**
- **Item**: the name/identifier of the parameter used in the system.
- **Description**: what the parameter controls and any sub-options.
- **Unit**: the measurement unit for the parameter (where applicable).
- **Default**: the default value used if the user does not override it.

---

## Row 1: **SPLI**
**Parameter meaning:** Controls **partitioning of the paper** into multiple sub-areas (“pictures”), i.e., how the available page area is subdivided into a grid or a single drawing region.

**Description details:**
- The value specifies a pattern of **height × width**.
- Two notation/behavior variations are described:
  1. **`heigthxwidth`**: “create pictures column by column”
  2. **`height*width`**: “create pictures line by line”
  
Here, **height** and **width** are not numeric measurements in cm/inches; they represent **partition counts/labels** (consistent with the surrounding context that partition digits/letters map to 1–9 and A–G ≈ 10–16). The key functional impact is the **render order** of the produced sub-pictures:
- **Column-by-column** for one form of the literal
- **Line-by-line** for the other form

**Unit:** **LIT** (literal / code-like configuration value rather than physical measurement)

**Default:** **`1*1`**
- Means no effective subdivision: the paper is treated as a single picture region (1 partition in height and 1 in width).

---

## Row 2: **SLEG**
**Parameter meaning:** Sets the **height of the partial legend**.

**Description details:**
- Specifies the vertical size of the legend associated with each picture (the system context states that “every picture gets an own legend” and that its height is defined by **SLEG**).

**Unit:** **cm**

**Default:** **1.5**

---

### Practical interpretation (for layout/RAG extraction)
- Use **SPLI** to decide whether one or multiple sub-plots are placed on the same paper page, and in which traversal order they fill the partition grid.
- Use **SLEG** to control the legend’s vertical footprint per sub-plot; increasing it allocates more space to legend text/bands, potentially affecting overall spacing on the page.

This table documents configuration “Items” related to how structure legends, borders, spacing, and picture/legend rendering behave in generated sheets and browser views. It is organized into columns: **Item** (parameter keyword), **Description** (meaning and allowed values), **Unit** (measurement type or literal type), and **Default** (default behavior when not specified).

### Core legend and border layout parameters
- **UMBR** (*Line feed in the picture legend*, Unit: **LIT**, Default: **YES**)  
  Controls automatic line wrapping (“line feed”) in the picture legend text. Allowed modes:
  - **NO**: never wrap lines  
  - **YES**: wrap if the line is too long  
  - **SUPP**: shorten an overly long line by moving the remainder to the next blank  
  - **SHOR**: shorten within a word (i.e., breaks/shortens to fit rather than moving whole words)

- **DRUU**, **DRUR**, **DRUL**, **DRUD** (*Upper/Right/Left/Lower print border*, Unit: **cm**, Default: **0.5**)  
  Define page/sheet frame margins (in centimeters) around the printed content:
  - **DRUU**: upper border  
  - **DRUR**: right border  
  - **DRUL**: left border  
  - **DRUD**: lower border

- **LEGW** (*Width of the legend if placed in the picture*, Unit: **cm**, Default: **\*** )  
  Sets the legend width constraint when the legend is integrated into the picture. The default is marked **\***, meaning the actual default may be system-dependent or calculated.

- **FREE** (*Region to be left free around the structure*, Unit: **cm**, Default: **0.2**)  
  Reserves whitespace around the structure to prevent overlap with legend/labels. Semantics:
  - **>= 0.0**: take axis/additional elements into account  
  - **< 0.0**: only this value is used (simpler behavior)

- **FAKH** (*Distance of legend lines as a factor of text height H*, Unit: **—**, Default: **0.5**)  
  Determines vertical spacing between legend lines by scaling the reference text height (noted as **SCHH H10** in the surrounding context).

### Representation of structure identifiers in legends
- **SHAE** (*Representation of the HEAD lines*, Unit: **LIT**, Default: **YES**)  
  Controls whether/how the “HEAD” line of the structure is printed in legends and how database-path context is included. Values:
  - **NO**: no representation  
  - **YES**: include the line of the structure in the sheet legend; if databases differ, include the representation in the picture legend including the complete path, or use a literal combination of up to four characters controlling what is written.

  Additional control logic (from the provided context) states that the output string may use a literal combination (max 4) where:
  - **A**, **R** are mutually exclusive  
  - **P**: always write the structure line or path into the picture  
  - **C**: structure line and (if requested) path placed on different lines or together if space allows  
  - **H**: only write the structure line  
  - **A**: write complete database path  
  - **R**: write relative path (relative to the input file position)  
  - **N**: write only database filename  
  (And again: **A**, **R**, **N** are mutually exclusive.)

### Date printing
- **DATE** (*Print of the date within the sheet frame*, Unit: **LIT**, Default: **YES**)  
  Enables or disables printing a date inside the sheet frame:
  - **NO**: do not print date  
  - **YES**: print date

### Picture/list placement behavior in browser reports
- **SPLI** (*Definition of the picture-positioning in the REPORT BROWSER*, Unit: **LIT**, Default: **\*** )  
  Determines how pictures are stored/placed when producing outputs for **REPORT BROWSER**, specifically relating to mixing pictures and lists:
  - With **SIZ2 SPLI PICT**: creates **single pictures**; the browser places these pictures on the sheet. Picture size is fixed based on **SIZE SPLI**, and inputs from the **record AND** for picture sizing are ignored.
  - With **SIZ2 SPLI PAGE**: stores the **complete page** including all pictures; pictures may have varying sizes and placements, and list lengths are limited by the size of the picture.

Overall, the table specifies fine-grained rendering controls for legend content formatting (wrapping, spacing), sheet framing margins, reserved clearances, inclusion of structure “HEAD” information (with controlled path/line formatting), optional date printing, and the mechanism for picture placement when generating browser-based report layouts.

 The item SHAE controls the output of the line of the structure defined with the program SOFiMSHA. The line of the structure is printed as a default in the sheet legend, if the same database is used at this sheet. In case of different databases the line of the structure is placed in the picture legend with the complete path of the database file. This can be controlled with a literal combination of the following characters (maximal 4). In this case ”A” and ”R” exclude each other:
 P The line of the structure or the path are written always into the picture (also if the database is available).
 C The line of the structure and the path (if it is requested) are placed in different lines, else, if the place is sufficient, together in one line.
 H Only the line of the structure is written.
 A Only the complete path for the database file is written.
 R Only the relative path with reference to the position of the input file is writ- ten.
 N Only the database file name is written.
 The parameter ”A”, ””R” and ”N” are mutually exclusive.
 The picture-positioning in the browser REPORT BROWSER is defined with the item SPLI. With the input SIZ2 SPLI PICT (default if the browser REPORT BROWSER is supported) single pictures are created. The browser REPORT BROWSER is placing this pictures on the sheet. This is the correct way to mixing pictures and lists. Pictures have a fixed defined size depending on SIZE SPLI. The input values to pictures size in the record AND are ignored. With the input SIZ2 SPLI PAGE (default if the browser REPORT BROWSER is supported) always the complete page including all pictures is stored. Pictures may have varying sizes and placements. The length of lists are limited on the size of the picture.

content:
This table defines parameters for the placement and scaling of a “picture” (a drawing output) on a sheet, including how multiple drawing layers can be composed within the same picture. It is structured with columns **Item**, **Description**, **Unit**, and **Default**, indicating both the meaning of each parameter and typical starting values.

### 1) Picture positioning within the sheet graphic area
- **POSI**: Selects a picture by **index** within the current picture list (**unit: “–”**).  
  - **Default: \***.  
  - It refers to the “Number in the current picture list”, allowing jumps to a specific defined picture position on the current sheet. The **current position** is the default reference for POSI.

- **POSL** (left border of picture): Defines the **left-hand picture border** as a percentage of the available graphic area (**unit: %**, **default: 0**).
- **POSR** (right border of picture): Defines the **right-hand picture border** as a percentage (**unit: %**, **default: 100**).
- **POSD** (lower picture border): Defines the **lower picture border** as a percentage (**unit: %**, **default: 0**).
- **POSU** (upper picture border): Defines the **upper picture border** as a percentage (**unit: %**, **default: 100**).

**Interpretation:** Together, POSL/POSR/POSD/POSU form a rectangular placement region. The table context specifies that placement can be chosen freely within the graphic area, but the picture must not be smaller than **1×1 cm**. The **picture size is defined by the first drawing** of that picture and must then remain fixed (subsequent layers cannot change it).

### 2) Picture scale applicable to all layers
- **SC**: Sets or requests the **scale of the picture**, valid for **all layers** within that picture (**unit: “–/LIT”**, **default: DEFA**).
  - If a numeric/explicit **value** is given, the system attempts to use it.  
  - If that fails, it chooses the **best possible scale** for filling the picture area.
  - If the given **value** is “multiplied with 1E+10”, the scale check is omitted (i.e., the system does not validate the scale under that condition).
  - The special preset **DEFA** means “Engineering scale, best possible for filling the picture”.

**Relationship to other controls:** In combination with the scale-determination method (**MSCA**), SC behavior determines whether the system tries to fit content into the defined picture borders.

### 3) Scale determination method (MSCA)
- **MSCA**: Controls how the drawing extents are analyzed to compute an appropriate scale (**unit: LIT**, **default: FULL**).
  - **MSCA NO** (*No / LIT*: used label “NO”): Scale is based on the **system box of the 1st layer**.
    - Additionally: only relevant outside-box representations of that 1st layer are considered, improving speed.
  - **MSCA ALL**: Scale uses **system boxes of all layers**.
  - **MSCA FULL**: Scale uses system boxes of all layers **and also includes representations outside those boxes**, providing stronger prevention against clipping (but requiring more scanning/work).

### Overall operational context (layering and sheets)
The surrounding text explains that pictures can be arranged across sheets, and the **AND** input determines whether the next drawing is placed as a **new layer within the same picture** (same sheet/picture context) or starts a new picture on a new sheet. Once multiple layers belong to one picture, the table parameters above—especially **SC**, **POS***—govern the entire picture consistently, while **MSCA** defines how layer extents influence the computed scale.

 AND
 If AND is not input, the next drawing is represented always at a new sheet. If several pictures are at one sheet, the next drawing is printed in the next picture position.
 An input for AND represents the next drawing order (layer) in the same picture. If no further inputs for AND occur, this layer is assigned to the at last processed picture. The scale remains unchanged.
 It is changed to the new picture or a picture not defined yet is generated, if the record AND contains further inputs.
 The current sheet obtains the list of the defined pictures from the previous sheet, that is their positioning at the sheet. One can jump to a picture of this list with POSI. The current position
 is the default for POSI. Maximal 64 pictures per sheet are possible.
 The position of a picture at a sheet can be defined freely within a graphic area with inputs for POSL, POSR, POSD and POSU. However, the picture should not be selected smaller than 1x1 cm. The size of the picture is defined in the first drawing. Then it can not be changed anymore.
 The scale which is calculated for the picture depends on the size of the structure box (system box) and the width of the borders around this box. The calculation is fastest, if the first layer of a picture with its structure is considered only in each case (MSCA NO). MSCA FULL should be input to prevent that representations are outside the picture. The entire picture is scanned to representations outside the picture and then the scale is adapted before the real drawing.

The table is a parameter specification list for **SCHH**, i.e., settings that control **text, legend, dimensions, scales, and the handling of numeric values and overlapping designations** in a SOFiSTiK graph/plot output. Each row defines an *Item* (parameter name), its *Description* (function and allowed modes), its *Unit* for the input value, and a *Default* value used when not specified.

**Global behavior and formatting context (applies across the table):**  
- Numeric **decimal places** in the **graph, legend, and list output** are uniformly derived from **ND**. Depending on whether NDIM or NMAX is used, the precision depends on unit settings or the *magnitude* of values.  
- Values that are too small for the chosen decimal resolution are shown as **‘0.0’** (including sign if needed).  
- Very large values (greater than the threshold **INTE SET 9 PAR1**, default **1.E+7**) are displayed in **E/exponent format**.  
- Overlap of lettering/designations can be managed by dividing the paper into a **grid** (0.7 mm spacing). Each lettering claims grid elements; the system checks whether they were already occupied by previous lettering. The overlap tolerance is controlled via **REVI** / **TREV**.

**Row-by-row meaning of items:**
- **H1 (cm, default `*`) – Legend:** Controls legend definition mode.  
  - `> 0`: explicit definition.  
  - `< 0`: adaptation to legend width (auto-sizing).
- **H2 (cm, default `0.25`) – Text in standard border above:** Sets the size/height for the “above” text in the standard border.  
- **H3, H4, H7, HS, MS, MINH, MINW (unit omitted / likely inherited; marked “obsolete”):** These parameters are deprecated and should not be used.
- **H5 (cm, default `0.2`) – Dimensional lines:** Controls dimensional line size/thickness scale for the plot.
- **H6 (cm, default `0.16`) – Results:** Scale for “results” text/graphics.
- **H8 (cm, default `0.2`) – FILL scale:** Controls the left-side fill scale size (dimensioning/scale display).
- **HS (cm, default `0.35`) – Symbol sizes for springs in side view:** Spring symbol scaling for side-view depiction.
- **FACW (unit `–`, default `0.7`) – Text width for results as text height factor:** Defines the width of result text relative to its height.
- **REVI (% , default `EXTR`) – Allowed overlapping for texts:** Selects how much previously placed lettering may be overwritten.  
  - `NO`: no overlap check.  
  - `YES`: 40%  
  - `FULL`: 25%  
  - `EXTR`: 5%  
  - `0...100`: an explicit percent value.
- **H10 (cm, default `H1`) – Text height of partial legend:** Height for text in a partial legend (defaults to H1).
- **FACS (–, default `0.8`) – Text width of partial legend:** Width scaling for partial legend text.
- **TREV (LIT, default `AMAX`) – Type of check for text overlap mappings:** Defines which values are chosen during overlap resolution (i.e., precedence rules). The table continues with selection modes:
  - `FIRS`: ignore following values  
  - `MINV`: use smaller values  
  - `MAXV`: use larger values  
  - `AMIN`: use absolute smaller values  
  - `AMAX`: use absolute larger values (explicitly emphasized in the provided context).

**Additional geometry/scale context included with the table:**  
- If a text size is entered as **zero**, the corresponding designation is omitted (useful for inner border dimension lines and the left fill scale).  
- Dimensional lines use SOFiSTiK unit **1001** and refer to the **3D optical-plane representation** perpendicular to the viewing direction (the “optical plane” concept).

Overall, the table provides a structured set of visualization parameters that determine **sizes (in cm), legend behavior, and output formatting**, plus **robust collision handling for labels** using REVI/TREV grid-based overlap logic and numeric formatting rules driven by ND.

The table entry describes an input/output parameter set associated with a graphical legend and value representation for designations (text, dimension lines, and scale-related markings) in a SOFiSTiK-based plotting context. It also defines how numerical values are selected, displayed, rounded, and how textual designations behave to avoid overlap.

Key concept: **value selection for maxima/minima and sign handling**. The notes distinguish between selecting absolute extrema and direction- or foreground-specific extrema. Specifically, **“AMAX uses the absolute larger values”**, while **“MAXZ uses the values in foreground”** (i.e., the Z/front-side context rather than an absolute comparison over all items). The line “imum values (if MINV, AMIN) per direction and unit” indicates that minimum-related options (MINV/AMIN) likewise compute per direction and unit, implying that extrema computation can be parameterized by direction and unit system.

Next, the table specifies **display semantics for numeric sign and visibility**:
- A condition **“> 0 showing always”** indicates that positive values are always shown (or always included in display logic).
- **“= 0 no showing”** indicates zero values suppress the corresponding display/designation.
- **“< 0 showing if sign is changed”** means negative values are only shown if the sign changed relative to some prior/reference state (e.g., whether the legend indicates a sign change event). This is consistent with legend behavior that depends on sign transitions.

Then, **text size handling** is specified: if an entered text size is **zero**, the corresponding designation is omitted. This is described as particularly useful for:
- dimensional lines of the **inner border**, and
- the **FILL scale** of the border on the left-hand side.
The dimensional lines are defined using **SOFiSTiK unit 1001**, and the indicated scale and dimension lines refer to the **3D representation of a line in an optical plane perpendicular to the viewing direction** (i.e., the drawing’s perspective/optical plane affects the final appearance).

Numeric formatting rules are also part of the table description:
- Decimal places in the **graph, legend, and list output** are uniformly determined by the input parameter **ND**.
- With **ND NDIM**, the number of decimal places depends on the SOFiSTiK unit settings.

- Values that are too small to represent at the required precision are displayed as **“0.0”**, possibly with sign.
- Very large values above **INTE SET 9 PAR1 (default 1.E+7)** are shown in **E (exponential) format**.

Finally, the table addresses **mutual overwriting (text collisions)** prevention:
- Inputs **REVI** and **TREV** control overlap avoidance for lettering.
- The paper is conceptually divided into a grid (0.7 mm spacing). Each lettering occupies grid elements; the system checks whether those elements were already occupied by prior lettering.
- The parameter specifies the allowed percentage overlap/retyping, i.e., how much of a lettering may overwrite grid elements from previous text.
- If the overlap condition is not met, the designation is selected or deleted based on **TREV**.
- This collision check increases runtime when performed more accurately.
- **REVI does not affect additional element designations** such as **CURV, TEXT, NIVE, POST, AXIS**.

Overall, the table section defines how extrema are chosen (absolute vs foreground), when numeric annotations are shown or suppressed (positive/zero/sign change logic), how text size and dimensional lines are rendered in a 3D optical plane, how numeric rounding/formatting is standardized using ND and INTE SET parameters, and how text overlaps are managed with a grid-based collision algorithm.

The table documents command/input parameters for controlling numeric **designation/label output** in a graph/legend context (and related maximum/minimum value displays), including rounding, formatting, and overlap-avoidance behavior. It has four columns: **Item** (parameter name), **Description** (what the parameter controls, often with literals/sub-options), **Unit** (expected unit type or symbol), and **Default** (system default).

**ND** sets the **number of decimal places after the comma** for values shown in the graph, legend, and list output. Its behavior depends on the value:

**REVX** and **RELVY** control overlap resolution by specifying a **distance of the edge for text overlapping**, expressed as a factor **relative to the text size**. Both have defaults of **0.33** and use **no unit** (unit column shows “–”).

**RMIN** and **RMAX** define bounds for how much spacing is allowed during text overlap checking:  
- **RMIN** (default **0.0 cm**) is the minimum distance.

**RMOD** selects the behavior mode for overlap handling and accepts literals under a **LIT** type:

For maximum/minimum value checks, the table introduces two parameter families:

**MAXX** defines the **type of check for maximum values** (also including literal-like parameters such as **TREV**). It also specifies the sub-option **DEFA**, described as using text-overlap mode corresponding to the **current TREV setting**. The parameter type is **LIT**, default **MAXV**.

**MMOD** defines parameters for the **maximum values** behavior with additional literals (LIT type), default **RIC**. Sub-options include:

- **MAXN** default **1**: number of **maximum** values. If **MAXV/AMAX** is used, it shows maxima; if minima variant is used, it affects that case accordingly. **0 = no showing**.  
- The next row begins **MINN** (default **-1** shown partially in the image): it is the number of **minimum values** when maximum-mode parameters like **MINV/AMIN** are active, with **-1 indicating the default behavior pattern** for minimum display count.

Overall, the table’s parameters tightly govern: (1) **decimal formatting** (ND), (2) **label overlap avoidance** through distance factors and tolerance (REVX/RE VY, RMIN/RMAX/RMOD/RTOL), and (3) **whether/how many extreme-value labels** are included and how their overlap rules interact with the max/min logic (MAXX/MMOD/MAXN/MINN). The input table defines several parameters controlling how result labels (“text”) are placed and formatted in a graphical output. Each row represents one configurable item, with an associated meaning, unit/type, and default behavior.

## MARK (Text insertion point marking)
- **Item:** `MARK`
- **Description:** Controls whether the insertion/effect point of the text is additionally marked (shown as a marker).
- **Unit:** `LIT`
- **Default:** `YES`
- **Possible values:**
  - `NO`: no marking.
  - `YES`: marking only for **QUAD** or **BRIC** results and for text representation (e.g., `QUAD REPR DTXT`).
  - `FULL`: marking always for text representation.
  - `EXTR`: marking always.

This setting is specifically about whether a marker cross/crosshair is drawn at the text insertion point, and under which result/text modes.

## MHEI (Height of marker cross)
- **Item:** `MHEI`
- **Description:** Defines the height of the marker cross.
- **Unit:** `-/cm` (effectively length in cm or a scaling mode)
- **Default:** `-1.0`
- **Interpretation rules:**
  - `> 0`: value is taken in **cm**.
  - `< 0`: absolute value acts as a **text height factor**, referencing `SCHH H6`.

So negative values convert the marker height into a proportion of the current text height.

## MFAC (Underscore length factor)
- **Item:** `MFAC`
- **Description:** Defines the length of an underscore as a factor of the marker cross height `MHEI`.
- **Unit:** `-`
- **Default:** `2.0`

## PREF (Prefixed text)
- **Item:** `PREF`
- **Description:** Adds a prefix (typically **load** or **design case number**) to the label text.
- **Unit:** `LIT`
- **Default:** `NO`
- **Possible values:**
  - `NO`: no prefix.
  - `YES`: prefix only for **area loads**.
  - `FULL`: prefix for **all loads**.
  - `EXTR`: prefix for **all results**.

This governs whether labels include identifying case/load information and how broadly it applies.

## PROP (Font properties)
- **Item:** `PROP`
- **Description:** Sets font style properties. The input can be either:
  - `DEFA`: “normal font”
  - or a **combination** of characters:
    - `B` = bold
    - `I` = italic
    - `U` = underscore
- **Unit:** `LIT`
- **Default:** `DEFA`

## MAX1 / MAX2 / MAX3 (Maximum text offset distances per direction)
- **Items:** `MAX1`, `MAX2`, `MAX3`
- **Description:** Define the **maximum value** for the text distance (used in the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd text direction).
- **Unit:** `LIT`
- **Default:** `DEFA` for each (i.e., default is applied unless overridden)

### Context for these “maximum value” parameters
The surrounding text explains how minimum/maximum thresholds and defaulting behave:
- Literal `DEFA` means the tool falls back to the corresponding default defined elsewhere.
- For “distance/displacement” style parameters, the unit of minimum/maximum values corresponds to the **results to be drawn currently**, and the valid selection can depend on whether `MIN`/`MAX` are set as ranges (with combinations like “min only”, “max only”, or “min+max range”).

Although this specific excerpt table only shows `MAX1–MAX3`, it fits into the same overall mechanism: the user can constrain how far/how (in up to three directions) the text is drawn, with `DEFA` meaning “use standard program behavior,” otherwise applying explicit limits.

Overall, this table segment focuses on **(1) whether and how an insertion-point marker is drawn**, **(2) how label text is prefixed**, **(3) font styling**, and **(4) direction-dependent maximum constraints for label placement**.

 The unit of the minimum and maximum values refers to the results to just be drawn currently. Following combinations are possible:
 MIN DEFA and MAX DEFA :

 If the literal DEFA is input for BACX, BACY, BMIN, BMAX, FMVX, FMVY, MMIN or MMAX, the corresponding default specified here is set.
 The result description is placed at a corresponding background area. This area can be bor- dered or the background can be deleted. The size of this area is controlled with BACX, BACY, BMIN or BMAX. In this case X is the writing direction and Y is the direction of the height.
 The result description is placed with the program control. However, an other offset can be also defined with OFFS, e.g. centrically at the corresponding place or next to that. It results the following orders:
 +2 +3 +4
 -1 0 +1
 -4 -3 -2
 The texts are drawn centrically at the insertion point with OFFS 0, with OFFS -4 to the left–hand side under that, with reference to the writing direction.
 The distance of the descriptions from the insertion point is defined with FMVX, FMVY, MMIN and MMAX. X and Y are here again the local writing directions.
 Usually the insertion point is displaced relatively to its original position a little bit, so that the descriptions in different direction (e.g. principal and transverse reinforcement of a plate) in the same node do not overwrite themselves. In this case the direction and the maximum value of the displacement (e.g. for QUAD elements the half element thickness) were determined already with GRAPHIC. However, the user can still change this with DTYP, DVAR, DX, DY and DZ.

 DX, DY and DZ are only analysed in the case of DTYP CM. Otherwise the direction defaulted by the program is used. The following literals are planned for DX:
 local x direction in the element
 X
 Y local y direction in the element
 Z local z direction in the element
 XX global X direction in the system
 YY global Y direction in the system
 ZZ global Z direction in the system
 EG global dead load direction

 BX horizontal
 BY vertical
