The table defines the parameter specification for a **selection command** (keyword set “SEL”), which controls which geometric/structural elements are processed or represented for output/graphics. It is organized into columns **Item**, **Description**, **Unit**, and **Default**.

### Columns
- **Item**: Name of the parameter/field that appears in the selection record.
- **Description**: Human-readable meaning of that parameter. For this snippet, it focuses on **ETYP**.
- **Unit**: Measurement unit for the parameter when applicable (here shown as italic/blank for ETYP since it is a categorical code).
- **Default**: Default value if the parameter is not provided (for ETYP, the table indicates “-”, meaning no inherent default category).

### Main parameter: `ETYP`
- **ETYP** = **Element type**.
- It accepts a code (`LIT` in the default font style is shown as the implicit default category label; in practice, it represents “all elements” unless narrowed).
- The description lists the supported **element type categories**, grouped as structural/meshing entities and “additional” non-structural graphical objects.

#### Element type options shown
- **All elements / general**
  - `LIT`: all elements
- **Structural element types**
  - `BEAM`: beam elements
  - `SPRI`: spring elements
  - `BUN O` (shown as `Boun` in the list): boundary elements (code displayed as **BOUT** in the snippet text description)
  - `TRUS`: truss elements
  - `CABL`: cable elements
  - `TUBE`: tube elements
  - `QUAD`: plane elements
  - `BRIC`: volume elements
  - `KINE`: kinematic constraints
  - `EDG E` / `EDGE`: nodal sequences
  - `SIR`: external beam sections
  - `DSLN`: design elements
  - `QTEN`: quad tendons
  - `BTEN`: beam tendons
- **Structural topology entities**
  - `GVO`: structural volumes
  - `GAR`: structural areas
  - `GLN`: structural lines
  - `GPT`: structural points
  - `NODE`: nodes
  - `QSEC`: cutting lines
  - `BSEC`: cutting areas
  - `CUT`: cutting pattern
  - `FIXL`: fixed cutting pattern
- **Additional graphical elements**
  - `ADD I`: all additional element types (code displayed as **ADDI**)
  - `LINE`: additional lines
  - `AREA`: additional areas
  - `TEXT`: additional texts
  - `POST`: position markers
  - `NIVE`: level symbols

### How this ties to the overall SEL behavior (context)
The surrounding text explains that **SEL** can be used to manage selection states:
- A **default behavior** exists where elements are processed unless filtered.
- Special selection logic depends on **TYPE** and additional fields (**VAL1–VAL3**, **TOL**, **REF**, **MODE**).
- **ETYP** acts as an element-type filter; when used, it can switch on only addressed element types.
- The selection can include **additional elements** (LINE/TEXT/QSEC etc.) and supports grouping via **SGRP** and boolean operators (**OPER**, default behavior described as OR within groups and AND across groups).

In RAG terms, this table should be indexed as: *“SEL parameter ETYP enumerates all supported element-type codes for selection/filtering.”* It is categorical (no unit), and it is central to narrowing what kinds of elements the selection affects.

The input table defines **SEL** (selection) functionality for controlling which geometry/graphics elements are processed and represented. It is a structured command table where a “record” (row) contains fields that describe **what to select**, **which values to use for matching**, and **how selection behavior should be interpreted**.

### Main purpose
- The command **SEL** enables selection of **specific elements** for representation.
- By default, **all elements are processed**, but selection behavior can deactivate/reactivate elements depending on the record contents and the chosen options.

### Columns / fields
- **SEL**  
  Identifies the selection command/keyword context for the table.

- **CURV Geometry axes**  
  Indicates that the system may include or refer to curved geometry axes as part of the selection/representation context.

- **Item**  
  A high-level label for the record entry; likely used to identify the specific selection instruction within the command set.

- **TYPE**  
  Determines the **kind of property/target** used for selection matching. The semantics of VAL1/VAL2/VAL3 depend on TYPE.
  Mentioned types include:
  - `NO`, `MAT`, `CROS`, `LENG [m]`, `GLN`, `GAR`, `GVO`, `TEND`, `NODE`, `T [m]`
  - Additional types referenced elsewhere: `LINE`, `TEXT`, `QSEC`, plus direction-related `DIRX`, `DIRY`, `DIRZ`.

- **VAL1, VAL2, VAL3**  
  Provide selection criteria values whose meaning varies with TYPE:
  - For many numeric-like types (`NO`, `MAT`, `CROS`, `LENG [m]`, `GLN`, `GAR`, `GVO`, `TEND`, `NODE`, `T [m]`), the values support:
    - **Only VAL1** → search for the single value
    - **VAL1 and VAL2** → search within a **range VAL1 to VAL2**
    - **VAL1/VAL2/VAL3** → range search with **increment** (from/to/increment)
  - For **direction-based selection**, VAL1–VAL3 represent components of a **global direction vector**; `TOL` is then interpreted as an **angular tolerance (in degrees)**.
  - For most types (except `TYPE NO`), VAL1–VAL3 may alternatively be derived from a **reference element number** using **REF**.

- **TOL**  
  Used as a **tolerance**:
  - For value matching: numerical tolerance for matching VAL1/VAL2/VAL3
  - For direction matching (`DIRX/DIRY/DIRZ` and direction-vector cases): angular tolerance in degrees.

- **REF**  
  Optional reference element number to determine VAL1–VAL3 automatically (except for `TYPE NO`).

- **MODE**  
  Controls special matching and selection behavior. Max **4 characters**.
  Examples described:
  - For searching titles (`TYPE MAT`, `CROS`, `GLN`, `GAR`, `GVO` with `TITL`):
    - `C` = case sensitive (default case insensitive)
    - `W` = whole word (default not whole word)
  - For direction types:
    - `P` = only positive direction (default all directions)
    - `N` = only negative direction (default all directions)

### Selection control logic (behavior described in the table text)
- **Special selection modes depend on TYPE.**
- Input `SEL` with the **first record** can deactivate structure elements initially; selection then mainly applies to **additional elements** (notably `LINE`, `TEXT`, `QSEC`) when explicitly defined.
- An **empty** `SEL` record (no values) turns selection **off**.
- If `SEL` uses only an **ETYP**-style input (type-based targeting), only those element types are represented; multiple criteria can be combined.
- Combining **SEL, BOX, GRP** is supported for more complex spatial or grouped filtering.

### Grouping and boolean operations
- Up to **100** individual selection inputs can be defined.
- **SGRP** divides selections into groups.
- Within a group, selections are combined with `OPER` (default is **OR**).
- Groups themselves are combined using `OPER`, with the first group defaulting to **AND**.

Overall, the table is a specification for building a configurable selection filter: it uses **TYPE** to choose the interpretation of **VAL1–VAL3** and **TOL**, optional **REF** to derive criteria, **MODE** to refine matching (case/word/direction), and **grouping/boolean logic** (SGRP/OPER) to combine many selection rules.

The input table documents a “SEL” record schema for selecting which model elements should be processed or represented. Each row defines one field in the selection command, how the field is interpreted, and what defaults apply. The table is designed to be generic: the meaning of numeric inputs (VAL1–VAL3 and TOL) changes depending on the selected TYPE.

**Columns:**  
- **Item / Field name**: the parameter used in the record (e.g., TYPE, VAL1).  
- **Description**: semantics of that parameter.  
- **Unit**: physical/meaning units when applicable; for most fields this is “–” or “*” (implementation dependent).  
- **Default**: the default behavior/value when the field is omitted.

### TYPE
**TYPE** specifies the “kind of selection via” and controls which property is used for matching. It accepts the following keywords:  
- **“all” / “–”**: select all elements of element type ETYP.  
- **EXCE**: select all elements except those of type ETYP.  
- **NO**: select by **element numbers**.  
- **MAT**: select by **materials** (ETYP QUAD, BRIC).  
- **CROS**: select by **cross sections** (ETYP BEAM, TRUS, CABL, TUBE, SIR).  
- **LENG**: select by **element length** (applicable to BEAM, SPRl, TRUS, CABL, TUBE, BOUN, QSEC, LINE, CUT, FIXL, SIR, QTEN, BTEN, EDGE).  
- **DIRX / DIRY / DIRZ**: select by local direction components in x/y/z for element types listed (e.g., BEAM, QUAD, BOUN, NODE, BRIC, GPT, GLN, GAR, SIR, KINE, SPRl, EDGE).  
- **GLN**: structural line numbers (BEAM, TRUS, CABL, BOUN).  
- **GAR**: structural area numbers (QUAD).  
- **GVO**: structural volume numbers (BRIC).  
- **GVO** selection is for volume membership; **GLN/GAR/GVO** act as higher-level grouping identifiers.  
- **GVO**, **TEND**, **NODE**, **T**:  
  - **TEND**: tendon properties (ETYP BEAM, QUAD).  
  - **NODE**: node numbers.  
  - **T**: thickness for QUAD.

The **Default** column for TYPE is “-”, meaning no special restriction beyond the element type ETYP unless TYPE is provided.

### VAL1, VAL2, VAL3
These fields provide numeric values used for TYPE-dependent matching. The table indicates they are “Selection via values depending on TYPE” and are effectively **wildcarded** in the unit/default columns (shown as “*”). Their semantics follow additional rules from the context:
- For many TYPEs, you may define **only VAL1** (search for that value), or **VAL1 + VAL2** (search a **range** “from…to”).  
- If **VAL1, VAL2, and VAL3** are all provided, the selection uses an **incremental search** “from, to, increment”.  
- For **direction-related TYPEs** (DIRX/DIRY/DIRZ), VAL1–VAL3 represent **components of a global direction vector**, and **TOL** is given in **degrees**.

### TOL (Tolerance)
TOL defines the allowed tolerance for matching. The context further clarifies two regimes:
- **TOL > 0**: interpreted in the **unit of TYPE**.  
- **TOL < 0**: interpreted as a **percent of (VAL2 − VAL1)**.  
For direction selection (except TYPE NO), the tolerance is typically treated as an angular tolerance in degrees.

### REF (Reference element number)
**REF** allows VAL1–VAL3 (except TYPE NO) to be derived from another “reference element number”. Instead of explicitly entering target values, the selection can compute them from the referenced element’s attributes.

### MODE
The table excerpt indicates MODE is “Special selection modes depending on TYPE” (units/default shown as “*” for this field). From the provided context, MODE is a **maximum of 4 characters** and includes modifiers such as:
- **For title-based searches** (MAT/CROS/GLN/GAR/GVO):  
  - **C** = case sensitive (default is case insensitive)  
  - **W** = whole word (default is substring matching)  
- **For direction TYPEs (DIRX/DIRY/DIRZ)**:  
  - **P** = only positive direction (default: both signs)  
  - **N** = only negative direction (default: both signs)

### Overall purpose and behavior (context summary)
Selection records are intended to be combined with a broader selection mechanism: individual elements can be explicitly deactivated/activated. As described in the context, an initial SEL record turns off elements except structural ones; subsequent SEL inputs mainly affect **additional elements** (LINE, TEXT, QSEC) when defined explicitly. An **empty SEL record** switches selection off. Selection can also be organized using **SGRP** and combined with logical **OPER** between entries and groups. Records **SEL**, **BOX**, and **GRP** can be used together.

The table defines a command/keyword-based selection mechanism under the **`SEL`** (special selection) feature. It is organized as a structured list with the following columns: **`Item`**, **`TYPE`**, **`VAL1`**, **`VAL2`**, **`VAL3`**, **`TOL`**, **`REF`**, and **`MODE`**. The header also indicates related concepts elsewhere in the specification (see also **SELE, BOX, GRP**), implying that **SEL** works in combination with additional selection constructs (e.g., bounding boxes and grouping).

### Columns and purpose
- **Item**: The named target/field for the selection request.
- **TYPE**: Determines what kind of entity/attribute is used for selection and how the values are interpreted. The table notes that the selection meaning of **VAL1/VAL2/VAL3/TOL** depends on **TYPE**. Examples include:
  - **`NO`**, **`MAT`**, **`CROS`**, **`LENG [m]`**, **`GLN`**, **`GAR`**, **`GVO`**, **`TEND`**, **`NODE`**, **`T`** (and **`TYPE DIRX, DIRY, DIRZ`** for direction components).
- **VAL1, VAL2, VAL3**: Numeric/string parameters whose semantics vary by TYPE. The table states multiple input modes:
  - If **only VAL1** is given → search for that single value.
  - If **VAL1 and VAL2** are given → search for a range **from VAL1 to VAL2**.
  - If **VAL1, VAL2, VAL3** are used → interpreted as an increment-based search **(from, to, increment)**.
  - For **direction-vector-based** selections (except `TYPE NO`), **VAL1–VAL3 represent global direction vector components**, while **TOL** is a tolerance in **degrees**.
- **TOL**: A tolerance parameter whose meaning depends on TYPE:
  - For scalar searches it is a numeric tolerance.
  - For direction selections it is given in degrees.
- **REF**: A reference element number from which **VAL1/VAL2/VAL3 can be derived** (explicitly mentioned “Except of TYPE NO … may be determined from a reference element number REF”).
- **MODE**: A constrained string (max **4 characters**) modifying the search/selection behavior, especially for text/title-based searches and direction handling:
  - For **TYPE MAT, CROS, GLN, GAR, GVO**: search the title **`TITL`** with options:
    - **`C`** = case sensitive (default is case insensitive)
    - **`W`** = whole word (default is not whole word)
  - For direction selections using **`TYPE DIRX/DIRY/DIRZ`**:
    - **`P`** = only positive direction (default: all directions)
    - **`N`** = only negative direction (default: all directions)

### Selection behavior and defaults
The accompanying context explains the operational rules of **SEL**:
- “Individual elements can be selected … with `SEL`.” As a default, **all elements are processed**.
- When the first **`SEL`** record is provided, **all structure elements are deactivated** (not additional elements). Selection therefore primarily affects **additional elements** (e.g., **LINE, TEXT, QSEC**) **only if explicitly defined**.
- An empty `SEL` record (with no values) switches selection **off**.
- If `SEL` includes **`ETYP`** only, then **only addressed element types** are represented.
- For `SEL ETYP ... TYPE EXCE` (and related combinations), all elements except certain types are turned on, but only elements with selected nodes are switched on if **`MODE B`** is added.

### Grouping and combination with other selection constructs
- Up to **100 individual** selection inputs can be defined.
- **`SGRP`** is used to divide selections into groups:
  - Within a group selections are combined using **`OPER`** (default: **“OR”**).
  - Groups themselves are connected using **`OPER`** as well; the first group uses **default “AND”**.
- The table indicates that **`SEL`** can be used together with **`BOX`** and **`GRP`**, supporting combined selection criteria.

The input table describes additional fields used by the **SELI/SEL** (“special selection”) mechanism to control how geometric/model entities are filtered and represented. It is organized as a schema with columns **Item**, **Description**, **Unit**, and **Default**. The table segment shown focuses on linkage logic for partial selections, grouping, and title-based selection for specific element types.

## Columns
- **Item**: Name of the input parameter/field.
- **Description**: How the parameter affects selection behavior.
- **Unit**: Measurement unit where applicable (mostly “—” here).
- **Default**: Default value when the field is not explicitly provided.

## Fields in the table

### 1) O PER (Linkage operator for partial selections)
- **Purpose**: Defines how multiple partial selections are combined.
- **Unit/Default**: Unit is **LIT**; the **default is “*”** (asterisk indicates the implicit behavior used when no explicit operator is specified).
- **Allowed behaviors**:
  - **NO**: *Does not use* the partial selection linkage operator.
  - **AND**: Activates only elements that are activated by **all** combined partial selections.
  - **OR**: Activates elements that are activated by **at least one** of the combined partial selections.
  - **–AND**: “Inverted AND”: elements are treated as active only in the sense that **all elements activated by the partial selection are deactivated** (i.e., the partial-selected elements become deactivated in the overall context).
  - **–OR**: Similar to OR but using an inverted logic: **elements activated in the partial selections are excluded/inverted** relative to the OR behavior.

This field therefore governs boolean-like composition rules between multiple **SEL** inputs that form “partial selections” within the selection framework.

### 2) SGRP (Group number of the partial selection)
- **Purpose**: Assigns a partial selection to a **group** so that multiple selections can be combined hierarchically.
- **Range**: **1…32**
- **Unit/Default**: Unit is **—**; **default is 1**.
- **Interaction with operators** (from surrounding context): Groups are connected using an operator as well (default described elsewhere as **AND** for the first group), and within a group selections are connected using **OPER** (default operator is **“OR”**).

So, **SGRP** enables up to 32 logical groups, allowing combinations like (Group1 AND Group2 OR Group3), depending on configured operators and inversion options.

### 3) TITL (Selection via designation / title)
- **Purpose**: Performs selection based on an entity’s **designation/title**, i.e., textual matching.
- **Applies to**: Only element types **MAT, CROS, GLN, GAR, GVO** and also certain explicit type selections such as **ETYP GPT, GLN, GAR, GVO**.
- **Unit/Default**: Unit is **LIT**; **default is “-”** (no title criterion unless provided).
- **Behavior**: The title string is used as the search criterion, which is further controlled by a **MODE** field elsewhere (e.g., case sensitivity and whole-word matching).

In practice, **TITL** turns “special selection” into a textual filter for the above element types, typically used together with **MODE** and **TYPE**-specific rules for matching.

## Overall interpretation
Collectively, the table defines the mechanisms for:
1) combining multiple selection criteria (**OPER**),  
2) organizing those criteria into up to **32 groups** (**SGRP**), and  
3) selecting entities by **textual designation** (**TITL**) for particular element categories.

## Table description: `VIEW` (3D parallel projection & orientation specification)

This table defines the **3D view specification** for rendering a structure in a **parallel projection**, including how the observer’s line of sight and the drawing orientation are established on the sheet. It is also connected to a possible **perspective variant** via a reference context (“PERS”), where the parallel observer position may be expanded to a perspective-like observer behavior.

### Core concept: mapping of observer direction to a view on the sheet
The table determines how the observer looks at the coordinate system using inputs **X, Y, Z**, and optionally an **AXIS** selector indicating which coordinate direction points **to the bottom of the picture**.

The observer is effectively placed at an infinite distance (parallel projection). Therefore, the values **X/Y/Z** represent the components of a **direction vector** that locates a point “behind” the origin (for line of vision) or “in front” (for standing at a point in front of the origin).

### Field meanings and relevant enumerations
- **TYPE (Direction definition)**: selects how X/Y/Z are interpreted.
  - `DIRE` or `STAN`: X, Y, Z are **direction components** of the observer’s line of vision.
  - `ANGL`: X/Y/Z are **angles** describing axis orientations relative to the horizontal.
  - (The table also mentions `SCAL`, `TRAN`, `DEFA` as related operations for scaling or transformation behavior, though those appear primarily in the extended “Direction/Transformation Definition” context.)
- **X, Y, Z**: parameters whose meaning depends on `TYPE`.
- **AXIS (orientation on the sheet)**: specifies which axis points downward on the sheet.
  - Default shown: `NEGZ` = “negative z axis downwards”.
  - Additionally, the table defines orientation literals like `POSX`, `NEGX`, `POSY`, `NEGY`, `POSZ`, `NEGZ` with the semantics “positive/negative x/y/z axis downwards”.

### Supported TYPE behaviors
1. **TYPE = DIRE or STAN**
   - **X/Y/Z** define the vector in the direction the observer looks.
   - `DIRE`: observer looks at the origin from behind it.
   - `STAN`: observer stands in front of the origin.

2. **TYPE = ANGL**
   - **X/Y/Z** are angles (x,y,z) for corresponding axes.
   - The table warns that certain angle combinations can lead to **degenerate graphics** (e.g., two orientations vertical to each other or parallel), producing ambiguous or non-univocal projections.

### Scale and transformation notes (as described in the same specification context)
- **VIEW can be used to generate reductions of axes** for condensed diagrams.
- If **three reduction values** are given, they are scaled directly for x/y/z axes.
- If **two reduction values** are given, the missing third is inferred using normalization conventions (quartic/ quadratic normalization described in the text).
- Positive vs negative reduction orientation convention: **positive values** orient axes away from the observer; **negative values** orient them toward the observer.
- A **3×3 transformation matrix** (with possible distortions) can be defined via `VIEW` by selecting which matrix row/column is controlled using **AXIS** literals such as `(POSX, NEGX)`, `(POSY, NEGY)`, or “all other AXIS literals”.

### Interaction with local element transformations
If an element type is defined with **item X**, then the view uses a **local element transformation** (referenced via item Y) instead of the global transformation. Example: `VIEW XY QUAD 3` makes the vision direction equal to the normalization vector of element type **3** (and negative Y selects from the nth element).

### Reference orientation types (enums for “orientation by reference”)
The table lists possible **reference types** that can supply orientation vectors:
- `QUAD`, `BEAM`, `DSLN`, `GPT`, `GLN`, `GAR`
- “Design elements” are mentioned as a further category.

These references allow `VIEW` to align the observer orientation to specific structural regions/elements rather than only to the global coordinate system.

The input table defines parameters for generating the *picture orientation/transformation* used by the `VIEW` mechanism in the representation. It is structured as an “Item / Description / Unit / Default” schema.

## Columns
- **Item**: Identifier of the parameter within the view specification. In the shown excerpt, the only visible item is **ROTA**.
- **Description**: Natural-language meaning of the parameter.
- **Unit**: Measurement unit used by the parameter.
- **Default**: Default value applied when the parameter is not explicitly set.

## Visible row: `ROTA`
- **Item**: `ROTA`
- **Description**: “Additional rotation of the picture in the clockwise direction.”
  - This indicates that `ROTA` applies an *extra* rotation to the rendered picture beyond the base orientation defined by `VIEW` (e.g., based on `TYPE = DIRE/STAN/ANGL` or axis reductions/transformation logic).
  - The rotation direction is explicitly **clockwise**.
  - It is described as “additional,” meaning it is composed with (not replacing) the orientation derived from the main view definition inputs (X/Y/Z, AXIS, scaling/reduction, and potential perspective handling via `PERS`).
- **Unit**: `degree`
- **Default**: `0`
  - A default of 0 degrees means no additional rotation is applied unless the user specifies otherwise.

The input table defines a set of perspective/projection parameters used to control how 3D results are mapped to a 2D illustration. It is organized into four columns: **Item** (parameter name), **Description** (what the parameter does), **Unit** (measurement or flag type), and **Default** (the system’s initial value).

---

## Parameters controlling observer distance and projection mode (`A`)

**Item: `A`** — “Set perspective value”
- **Meaning:** Controls the **distance of the observer from the focal point** (i.e., how strong the perspective effect is).
- **Unit:** `LIT/m` (a length unit per meter, indicating the value is expressed in a length-related scale).
- **Values / modes (enumeration):**
  - `value` — Use a numeric distance (enables perspective geometry according to the observer–focal point setup).
  - `OFF` — Eliminates perspective (effectively disabling perspective distortions and behaving like a parallel projection).
  - `ON` — Enables perspective using the **previous settings** (toggles perspective without resetting focal/angle related parameters).
  - `INF` — Uses **infinite distance** (explicitly described as **parallel projection**). This corresponds to the case where perspective projection converges to length/angle-precise projection, as noted in the context: the default parallel projection is length- and angle-precise and suitable for complete 3D representation.
- **Default:** `!` (unspecified/placeholder meaning; the table does not provide a numeric default, suggesting this parameter must be set/controlled by the user or by higher-level logic).

**Context tie-in:** The surrounding text explains that parallel projection is length- and angle-precise (all coordinates preserved without limit), while central perspective depends on observer distance and relative positioning, which can distort moment diagrams.

---

## Parameters defining the focal point (`BX`, `BY`, `BZ`)

The focal point is the point used as the reference for the optical geometry. The table provides three coordinate entries:

- **Item `BX`** — **x-coordinate of the focal point**
  - **Unit:** `m`
  - **Default:** `0.0`
- **Item `BY`** — **y-coordinate of the focal point**
  - **Unit:** `m`
  - **Default:** `0.0`
- **Item `BZ`** — **z-coordinate of the focal point**
  - **Unit:** `m`
  - **Default:** `0.0`

These default to the origin, meaning that if the focal point is not explicitly configured, the projection center is assumed at (0, 0, 0). The context further clarifies that the focal point lies in both the **optical plane** and the **optical axis** and that representation is length- and angle-precise at the focal point for central perspective.

---

## Parameters controlling the field of view and specialized projections (`ANGL`, `CYL`, `CYLD`, `SPH`, `SPHD`)

**Item: `ANGL`** — “Visual angle for perspective”
- **Meaning:** Defines the observer’s **visual angle** (a tangential limit for what points around the optical axis remain visible in the perspective representation).
- **Unit:** `LIT/-` (unitless ratio/angle measure in this system’s convention).
- **Default:** `99`
- **Context tie-in:** The text describes that points exactly next to the observer project to infinity, so the visual angle must be introduced. It also provides example mappings:  
  - `0.643` → 28 mm (wide angle)  
  - `0.360` → 50 mm (normal)  
  - `0.144` → 125 mm (tele)  
  This implies `ANGL` behaves like a lens-equivalent field-of-view parameter: larger values correspond to wide-angle perspective, smaller values to telephoto-like narrow viewing.

### Projection mode selection flags / templates
The table also includes mode specifiers that alter the type of projection and how the optical plane is constructed:

- **`CYL`** — “cylinder projection”
- **`CYLD`** — “developed cylinder view”
- **`SPH`** — “spherical projection”
- **`SPHD`** — “developed spherical view”

**Units:** Not explicitly shown for these items in the provided table section (they are listed under the same unit column), suggesting they are **mode keywords** rather than numeric parameters. Their inclusion indicates that, in addition to central perspective (finite observer distance), the system supports alternative mappings such as cylindrical or spherical projection, including “developed” views that unfold the surface (turning curved projection surfaces into planar representations). The context states that for cylinder projection, the optical plane is a developed view of a cylinder with vertical axis and radius `A`, with the observer standing at the cylinder axis; this can reduce hidden-line inaccuracies because lines are drawn as straight segments in the unfolded view.

--- 

Overall, the table is a configuration interface for selecting and parameterizing perspective projection: **`A`** governs perspective strength or mode (including parallel when `INF`), **`BX/BY/BZ`** set the focal point coordinates, and **`ANGL`** constrains the visual field; **`CYL/CYLD/SPH/SPHD`** switch between central perspective and specialized cylindrical/spherical projection variants.

The input table describes configuration options for **visibility handling in 3D representations**, specifically **hidden-line omission** and **depth-of-focus limits**. It is organized into columns: **Item** (parameter name), **Description** (option meaning and allowed values), **Unit** (measurement unit or data type), and **Default** (system default setting).

### Parameters related to hidden lines
1. **HIDD** – *Omission of hidden lines*  
   - **Default:** `NO`  
   - **Behavior:** Controls whether hidden lines are suppressed in the 3D output.  
   - **Allowed values (as listed in the table):**
     - `NO`: Prints also hidden lines (i.e., hidden lines are not omitted).  
     - `NODE`: Uses a **node-dependent** hidden-line method. The algorithm checks all nodes, determines which nodes are visible (e.g., not covered by other geometry), and then draws only elements/results whose nodes are visible.  
       - Noted in the context: this method is **very fast**, but it **cannot realize partial not visible or hidden lines**.  
     - `LINE`: Uses a **line-dependent** classical hidden-line method. It operates **edge/edge-related** and therefore cannot determine whether an element area is actually covered (it is edge-oriented rather than area-coverage oriented).  
       - Context notes: it will represent results in all elements that are considered visible according to the `NODE` method, but because it cannot distinguish area coverage, its behavior may differ from the node-based approach.

### Parameters related to depth of focus (clipping in view direction)
2. **DMAX** – *Depth of focus, maximum*  
   - **Unit:** `m` (meters)  
   - **Default:** `-` (not explicitly fixed in the table; context states a default of **+1.E12**)  
   - **Meaning:** Limits the represented region **behind** the optical plane from the observer perspective.  
   - **Special value:** `OFF` = not used (i.e., the depth limit is not applied).  
   - **Direction convention from context:**  
     - **Positive values** refer to area **behind the optical plane**.  
     - **Negative values** refer to area **in front of** the optical plane (even if the parameter name suggests “behind”).

3. **DMIN** – *Depth of focus, minimum*  
   - **Unit:** `m` (meters)  
   - **Default:** `-` (not fixed in the table; context provides a default depending on projection type)  
   - **Meaning:** Limits the represented region **in front of** the optical plane (minimum depth bound in the view direction).  
   - **Special value:** `OFF` = not used.  
   - **Default convention from context:**
     - For **perspective** representation: default equals the **negative distance of the observer from the picture point**.  
     - For **parallel** projection: default is **-1.E12**.  

   - **User override:** Both `DMIN` and `DMAX` can be set arbitrarily (even values behind the observer). The sign convention remains: positive = behind optical plane; negative = in front.

### Additional control over depth input mode
4. **DREL** – *Input of depth*  
   - **Unit:** `LIT` (logical/boolean-like enumerated option type)  
   - **Default:** `YES`  
   - **Allowed values:**
     - `YES`: Depth of focus values are interpreted **relatively to the current observer standpoint**.  
     - `NO`: Depth of focus values are interpreted in **absolute coordinates**.

### Overall implication for rendering
Taken together, the table configures (a) whether hidden-line removal is performed and how it is computed (**HIDD: NODE vs LINE vs no omission**) and (b) how far geometry is rendered along the viewing direction relative to the optical plane (**DMAX/DMIN**) with an optional choice of coordinate interpretation (**DREL**). This directly affects which portions of a 3D model are drawn normally and which are clipped or suppressed in the final representation.

### Table: DEFO – Representation settings for deformed structures and derived result visualizations

This table defines the **DEFO** drawing/visualization record, which controls how subsequent graphics are rendered in place of the original (undeformed) structure. When **DEFO** is enabled, the system computes **modified node coordinates** by adding a **scaled offset** to the undeformed structure according to one of several deformation “sources” (displacements, potentials, or internal force/moment quantities). The resulting deformation representation is then used by **following drawing records** (e.g., a record like **STRU** must follow DEFO when internal forces are requested). If **DEFO is not active** (value **NO**), the original structure is shown.

#### Columns / field meaning (as described in the surrounding text)

- **Item Description**: indicates the meaning of each DEFO option.
- **TYPE**: categorizes how the value is interpreted:
  - **number of a calculated load case** or literal tokens used to select the deformation source/type.
  - **NO / YES** are explicit boolean-like options.
  - **LC (load case)** variants define which load case drives the deformation.
- **DEFO**: main control record enabling deformation representation.
- **NO / YES**:
  - **NO**: no deformed structure is represented.
  - **YES**: enables **nodal displacements** for the load case(s) specified in connection with **LC**.
- **LC / lc–no** (load case of the deformed structure):
  - Specifies the load case index (**lc–no**) whose deformation or results are used.
- **POT (HYDRA potential-based deformation)**:
  - Uses **potential values** from the HYDRA program state defined by **LC** instead of the original **z coordinates**.
- **FREE (free surface)**:
  - Generates a **free surface of potential values** from the BRIC structure.
  - Intended when results are available in **BRIC elements**.
- **FRGL (FREE with additional potential peaks)**:
  - As FREE, but additionally accounts for potential peaks using the FRGL.. option set.
- **Internal forces and moments (plate/shell rendering areas)**:
  - **MXX, MYY, MZZ, VXX, VYY, NXX, NXY** (and related **SH0, SH1, SH2, SH3, SH5, SH10, SH15, SH20, SH30**) represent internal force/moment or stiffness categories.  
  - The record **STRU** then draws the resulting **areas** of those internal quantities (i.e., DEFO defines the data projection/displacement; STRU performs the visualization).
  - **Important rule**: if you only specify DEFO with internal-force/moment literals but **do not provide a subsequent record like STRU**, the expected internal-force area representation will not appear.
- **GAR / GARB (projection onto GARB structural area)**:
  - Uses **FAKV** to project coordinates to a **GARB structural area**.
  - If **FAKV is positive**, selection context (SEL/BOX) remains unchanged.
  - If **FAKV is negative**, it creates a **single selection** including relevant QUAD elements belonging to the area.
- **GVO / GVOB (3D view of structural volume)**:
  - Uses **FAKV** to define a structural volume view.
  - If **FAKV is positive**, existing selection (SEL/BOX) remains.
  - If **FAKV is negative**, it selects all **BRIC elements** belonging to that volume.
  - **GVOB** creates a surrounding BOX; it overwrites prior SEL/BOX if provided afterward.
- **FAK V / FAKV (factor for magnification / selection geometry)**:
  - Drives scaling and/or geometric interpretation for area/volume projection.
- **SMOV** (system movement):
  - Uses a **system movement load case** (e.g., incremental launching).
  - Displacements from this SMOV load case are added to node coordinates.
- **CURR / CURR time step / current load case selection**:
  - When **CURR** is used, the effective load case is determined in order:
    1) Load case of the deformed structure  
    2) Load case of the current load/result  
    3) Load case of group control depending on a load case
  - Additionally, **CURR time step** can be used when representing hydraulic free surfaces/potentials.
- **Time / Units**:
  - The table text includes unit defaults in the form of **−/LT, DEFA −/LT, CURR sec/LT** and indicates:
    - **DEFA** is a program default factor value (mentioned as **1/10 of maximum structure length** in context),
    - **CURR sec/LT** relates to time-step representation for hydraulic free surfaces/potentials.
- **Legend output**:
  - The load case, magnification, and eigenvalue frequency (when eigenmodes are used) are printed in the legend.

#### Key behavior rules (requirements and interactions)

- **DEFO** modifies what is drawn after it; it does not itself guarantee that internal-force areas are displayed.
- For internal forces/moments visualization based on added quantities, **a drawing record such as STRU must follow DEFO**.
- **Free surface behavior**:
  - When FREE/FRGL is used, intersecting surfaces between the free surface and BRIC surface create **holes**; nodes are displaced according to **potential** at those intersections.

Overall, the table specifies a flexible set of **deformation visualization modes** (displacement-based, potential/free-surface-based, and internal force/moment area-based) plus **selection/projection controls** (GAR/GVO/GVOB/GARB) and **special dynamic/system-movement handling** (SMOV, CURR).

The table defines two input items used by the **DEFO** (deformed shape) and related result representation workflow. It has four columns: **Item**, **Description**, **Unit**, and **Default**. Together, the entries specify how geometric transformations and load-case/time selection affect the plotted representation.

### 1) Item: **EXPO**
- **Meaning (Description):** “Explosion factor for the representation of two-dimensional cutting pattern areas (record **STRU**, **NUM ZS2…**) or for distances of bore profiles.”
- **Purpose in the workflow:** EXPO controls an *expansion/scaling* effect (“explosion”) applied when visualizing 2D cutting pattern areas produced by the **STRU** record (with numeric pattern indices like **ZS2…**) and also when representing *bore profile distances*. In practice, higher values separate or offset those pattern/bore elements for clarity.
- **Unit:** shown as “—” (dimensionless).
- **Default:** **0.0**, meaning no explosion/offset is applied unless the user specifies a value.

### 2) Item: **SMOV**
- **Meaning (Description):** “System movement (e.g. incremental launching of bridges).”
- **Purpose in the workflow:** SMOV selects whether a **system movement load case** is used to update nodal coordinates prior to displaying the deformed/result state. This is relevant for staged construction processes (e.g., incremental bridge launching) where the structural system itself changes over time/loading history.
- **Allowed values (enumeration in the table):**
  - **NO**: “Do not show” system movement (i.e., do not apply that transformation).
  - **CURR**: “Use current load case” as the basis for the system movement.
  - **> 0**: “Use this load case” (numeric selection).
- **Unit:** “—” (selection/mode).
- **Default:** **\*** (asterisk), indicating a program-controlled default (not explicitly fixed in the table).

### Cross-context with DEFO (from the provided documentation)
This table complements the DEFO record behavior described in the context text: **DEFO** generates deformed coordinates from the undeformed structure using a scaled offset (“shift rule”). When **SMOV** is used, the displacements from the chosen system movement load case are added to node coordinates. The documentation also explains that when **CURR** is used, the load case is determined following a priority order: primarily the load case of the deformed structure, then the load case of the current load/result, then group control depending on a load case.

In summary, **EXPO** is a visualization scaling factor (explosion/offset) for specific STRU-derived 2D patterns or bore profile distances, while **SMOV** is a selector controlling whether system movement displacements are applied during the DEFO-based deformed representation.

sections: 3.27 MOVE – Starting Point and Properties of Additional Elements

content:
The input table is a technical specification excerpt (appears to document CAD/geometry text and cutting-pattern placement options). It contains multiple “Item” entries, each describing a parameter, its meaning, unit type, and default behavior. The table is primarily organized into two parameter blocks: **MOVE** and **ADJU**, and it also includes lists of possible symbol/geometry placement types and axis references from a database.

## Block 1: MOVE (text insertion offset behavior)
- **Item:** `MOVE`
- **Description (parameter meaning):** Controls **“maximum distance of the text insertion point from the cm/% OFF boundary”** of a system box. The system box is defined via `GRP / BOX ON`.
- **Key rule:** The **initial text insertion point is shortened to the system box boundaries** when it would exceed those boundaries.
- **Value interpretation:**  
  - If **> 0 distance** in **cm**, it is applied as a positive offset limit.  
  - If **≤ 0 distance** in **%**, then the behavior corresponds to “text insertion points are OFF not changed.”  
  - The text insertion point behavior is stated as: **“picture area: the text insertion points are OFF not changed.”**
- **Unit/Default column:** shows **`cm/%`** with default meaning described by the boundary logic (positive moves within allowed boundary; non-positive / OFF leaves unchanged depending on unit).
- **Related parameter:** a note says: **“Check always, independent of UNIT”** for the boundary/off decision logic.

## Block 2: GRNO / DTYP / LT (element identification)
Under the MOVE area, there are additional selector fields that define an **additional element** being positioned or generated:
- **`GRNO`**: *Group number* that the additional element pertains to. Default indicates **0**.
- **`DTYP`**: *Type of additional element* with an internal set of enumerated options. Default shown as `LT` with a dash indicating “not specified / all types” depending on context.
- **Enumerated DTYP options** include:
  - `LINE` (additional line)
  - `AREA` (additional area)
  - `QSEC` (cutting line through plane elements)
  - `BSEC` (cutting area through volume elements)
  - `CUT` (cutting pattern line)
  - `FIXL` (fixed cutting pattern line)
  - `TEXT` (additional text)
  - `POST` (positioning symbol)
  - `NIVE` (level symbol)
  - `CURV` (geometry axis)
  - `SIR` (external beam sections)
  - `DIML` (dimensional lines)
  - `AXIS` (system axis)

## Axis placement mappings (read from database)
Two kinds of axis-related placement values are listed as database-driven:
- **Axis reading from database: `AXST`** and various bridge/tendon/general axes:
  - `AXLA` central lane of bridge
  - `AXGE` additional lane of bridge
  - `ASEC` secondary axis
  - `AXTE` tendon geometry
  - `AINT` internal axis (SOFIMSHC mentioned)
  - `AXUN` general axis
  - plus: `AXST` structural axis
- **Placements reading from database:**
  - `PXLA` at central lane of bridge
  - `PSEC` at secondary axis
- **`DISZ`**: distance of multiline texts (`TEXT`), with a continuation marker (`− 1.3 >0.0`) implying a default of **1.3** and a rule that only applies when **> 0.0**.

## Block 3: ADJU (adjustment/coupling of cutting lines)
- **Item:** `ADJU`
- **Description:** Controls **adjustment of cutting lines** specifically for plane/“cuts” and defines whether cuts are coupled or treated as singletons, and how global direction alignment is determined.
- **Core default:** `DEFA` (default behavior: **“Cuts will not connected”**).
- **Adjustment modes and meanings (enumerated):**
  - `DEFA`: for polygonal cuts use `SERI`; for single cuts use `GLOB`
  - `SERI`: **polygonal cuts are coupled to each other** (“SERI Cuts are coupled…”)
  - `SEPA`: **polygonal cuts are separated** and saved as single cuts
  - `GLOB`: cuts adjusted using a **global direction**
  - `NO`: **no adjustment**; direction is defined by the **order of point input**
  - `POLY`: only polygonal cuts are coupled; single cuts are not adjusted
  - `SING`: only single cuts are adjusted at a global direction; polygonal cuts are not adjusted
  - `CONN`: like `DEFA`, but cuts **may be connected**
  - `CSRI`: like `SERI`, but cuts **may be connected**
  - `CGLB`: like `GLOB`, but cuts **may be connected**
  - `CNO`: like `NO`, but cuts **may be connected**
  - `CPOL`: like `POLY`, but cuts **may be connected**
  - `CSNG`: like `SING`, but cuts **may be connected**
  - `+X...–Z` / `+GX..–GZ`: global direction variants (direction explicitly spans coordinate components)
  - `+EX...–EZ like SING, global direction`: another variant indicating single-cut-like behavior with global direction

The table is effectively a configuration reference: it defines how text insertion points are constrained relative to a system box and how different “additional element” types and axis references are selected, then it defines how cutting lines are adjusted—coupled vs separated, and whether direction is global, local, or determined by point entry order.

It uses a consistent schema with four columns: **Item** (parameter code), **Description** (what the parameter affects and how it behaves), **Unit** (measurement unit or dimension rule), and **Default** (the system default value).

### Parameters shown in the table

1. **DIST — Distance of dimensional lines (DIML) to the measured line**
   - **Unit:** `cm`
   - **Default:** `0.6`
   - **Meaning of sign:**
     - `> 0` : dimensional lines are placed to the **right** side of the measured line
     - `< 0` : dimensional lines are placed to the **left** side of the measured line  
   This parameter therefore supports direction control via positive/negative values in centimeters.

2. **DASH — Size of dash at dimensional lines (DIML)**
   - **Unit:** `−/cm` (dash size is expressed in centimeters, but the “-” indicates a special sign convention)
   - **Default:** `0.4`
   - **Rules:**
     - `> 0` : interpreted as a **dash length** in `cm`
     - `< 0` : interpreted as a **factor of text height** (the dash size becomes `(+MAR G?)`-related per text height; the table states “Factor of text height (+MARG)”)
   This parameter allows either absolute dash sizing or relative sizing tied to the text height.

3. **PICT — Maximum distance of the text insertion point from picture boundaries**
   - **Unit:** `cm/%`
   - **Default:** `0.2`
   - **Interpretation:**
     - `= 0` : the element is shown **only if it lies inside the picture** area
     - `ON` : the initial text insertion point is **shortened/clamped** to the picture boundaries
     - `> 0` : distance is in **centimeters**
     - `≤ 0` : distance is given as a **percentage of picture area**
     - `OFF` : text insertion points are **not checked/unchanged**  
   This parameter governs how far text may be placed outside the visible picture region and whether the system clamps or ignores boundary checking.

4. **SBOX — Check for visibility inside the structural box**
   - **Unit:** `m/—` (the table indicates a special categorical behavior)
   - **Default:** `0.0`
   - **Modes:**
     - `OFF` : no visibility check
     - `ON` : behaves like input `"0.0"`
     - `≤ 0` : check only for elements with `UNIT WC`
     - The table text also mentions: “Check always, independent of UNIT” (the row likely continues beyond the visible capture, implying a condition such as `> 0` or another threshold to enforce always-on checking)  
   This parameter controls whether graphic elements are validated for visibility within a structural framing box, with optional restrictions based on element unit/type.

### Overall table role (for RAG use)
Collectively, these **Item** definitions specify numeric and categorical options that affect **visual correctness** (boundary/visibility enforcement) and **styling** (dash length). They are designed for parameter-driven rendering: each item has a default, supports sign-based semantics for direction/relative sizing, and includes boundary-check modes to prevent text or dimension elements from being placed outside the intended visible areas.

The table defines input parameters for an **SIR cross-section configuration** (i.e., properties used to place and orient reference sections along a continuous beam). It is organized into four columns: **Item** (parameter name), **Description** (what the parameter controls), **Unit** (measurement unit or “–” for none), and **Default** (the value assumed when the item is not explicitly provided).

### Key section identification and orientation
- **NO** (*Section number*): Identifies the section. **Default: 1**.
- **NX, NY, NZ** (*Components of the section normal*): These specify the direction of the section’s normal vector (no physical unit). Defaults are **NX = 1**, **NY = 0**, **NZ = 0**, meaning the normal initially aligns with the X-axis direction used by the section definition system.
- **LDIR** (*Kind of local direction = line of vision*): Selects how the section’s local y/z direction is interpreted relative to the “line of vision” set elsewhere (record VIEW referenced in the context). Unit is **LIT** (logical type). **Default: DEFA**. Allowed modes listed:
  - **DEFA** (default behavior)
  - **Y**: positive local y direction
  - **–Y**: negative local y direction
  - **Z**: positive local z direction
  - **–Z**: negative local z direction  
  This directly relates to the context note that “positive local z direction” and “negative local z direction” correspond to DSIR-controlled changes of point properties along the continuous beam.

### Spatial extents of the section “box/window”
These parameters define the geometry of a **section box** and the active “window” plane relative to a reference point:
- **XMIN** (*Depth of the section box for the support*), **XMAX** (*reactions*): Depth limits along the local X axis. **Units: m**. Defaults:  
  - **XMIN = -0.001 m**  
  - **XMAX = +0.001 m**
  These small default values suggest a minimal box depth unless the user provides meaningful limits.
- **YMIN, YMAX** (*Local coordinates of the active window of the section plane with reference to the reference point*): Define the active interval in Y. **Units: m**. Defaults:
  - **YMIN = -999 m**
  - **YMAX = +999 m**
  This effectively creates an “unbounded” window by default.
- **ZMIN, ZMAX** (*Local coordinates of the active window … with reference to the reference point*): Define the active interval in Z. **Units: m**. Defaults:
  - **ZMIN = -999 m**
  - **ZMAX = +999 m**

### Cross-section selection and linkage
- **SNO** (*Cross section number of the section*): Links to a cross-section definition (e.g., in a database of section shapes/properties). **Default: 1**.

The provided description context explains that continuous beam polygons are created by **MOVE** (start at **XS=0.0**) and subsequent **DRAW** records define points, with **XS calculated automatically**. The table’s section items (especially orientation-related ones like **NX/NY/NZ** and **LDIR**) correspond to **SIR record SECT items XM, YM, ZM** and are applied consistently across all layers for the referenced database. The **DSIR** record changes properties for the “last defined point” or defines properties for the “next point,” affecting how the section is oriented along the beam.

---

## Row: **CUT**

## Row: **GRP**
- **Meaning (parameter):** Controls whether *group limits* are applied when generating additional cutting pattern lines.
- **Unit:** `LIT`
- **Default:** `NO`
- **Behavior:**
  - **YES:** Consider group membership; if group limits apply, **additional cutting pattern lines** are generated.
  - **NO:** No group limit consideration (no additional cutting pattern lines driven by group constraints).
- **Interpretation:** Enables/disable constraint logic tied to grouping (likely affecting line generation density/extent based on membership rules).

## Row: **SELE**
- **Meaning (parameter):** Controls whether cutting patterns are generated only from the currently selected/visible finite elements.
- **Unit:** `LIT`
- **Default:** `NO`
- **Behavior:**
  - **YES:** Only the **currently visible QUAD elements** are used.
  - **NO:** All **available QUAD elements** in the system are used, including those switched off with **BOX** and **GRP selection**.
- **Interpretation:** This setting determines the element scope: “visible subset only” vs “entire available system.”

The table defines how to select and filter which stored analysis results are used when generating drawings/output. It is structured with columns **Item**, **Description**, **Unit**, and **Default**. Each *Item* is a parameter name that can be set in the input; the behavior is described in the corresponding *Description* and is further constrained by the “default” selection rules.

### Rows / Parameters

**NO**
- Purpose: Selects a **load case** (LC) for the representation in subsequent drawings.
- Unit: shown as **−/LIT** (either a load-case index/list token or a special list identifier).
- Default: **DEFA**
  - **DEFA = FIRS**
  - **FIRS** selects the *first* load case from the load case list.
- Selection semantics:
  - If **NO ≥ 0**, the specified load case number is used.
  - If **NO < 0**, the load case is taken using the mapping “with NO from the load case list” (i.e., it is interpreted as a reverse/indexed selection relative to the list rather than a direct absolute LC number).
  - Special keyword options are supported:
    - **LAST**: use the last load case from the list
    - **NEXT**: use the next load case
    - **PREV**: use the previous load case
    - **NAME**: search for the load case number via **TITL** (with a warning if the designation is found not exactly)
    - **FIND**: search like NAME but **without** the warning

**T**
- Purpose: Time value for **transient results** (referenced to transient calculations, e.g., stored by time step interpolation).
- Unit: **sec/LIT**
- Default: **LAST**
- Interpretation rule: the input (except for **NAME/FIND**) is treated as **equivalent to NO**, meaning it uses the same selection logic as the load-case selector but applied to time values.

**DESI**
- Purpose: Selects the **design case** (e.g., reinforcement or design stresses).
- Unit: **−/LIT**
- Default: **DEFA**
  - **DEFA = FIRS**
- Semantics: the input (except **NAME/FIND**) is equivalent to **NO**, i.e., it uses the same indexing/list-based selection logic, but for design cases instead of load cases.
- Example context: the surrounding text indicates that design-case-related results (reinforcements/design stresses) are represented using the design load case, whereas other LC-stored results are addressed by **NO**.

**MAT**
- Purpose: Selects the **material** to be represented in the case of **composite materials** (materials available under the same LC/design case).
- Unit: **−/LIT**
- Default: **DEFA**
- Semantics:
  - The input (except **NAME/FIND**) is equivalent to **NO**.
  - If MAT is not provided, the **first found** material is used.
  - If selection fields like averages/extremes/summation are requested across materials (mentioned in the context), then multiple/all materials may be combined.
  - The broader context also notes that literals/stress points from beam output (e.g., AQUA stress output) can be used in some cases, tying MAT selection to specific material representations.

Overall, the table documents a consistent “selector” pattern: **NO**, **T**, **DESI**, and **MAT** all accept numeric indices or symbolic keywords (**FIRS/LAST/NEXT/PREV/NAME/FIND**), with defaults routed through **DEFA → FIRS** unless overridden. This enables selecting the correct LC/design/time/material records that subsequent result extraction and plotting will visualize.

content:
### Table Description: AQUA Output Selection for Beam Results (LC/Material/Direction/Factors)

This table defines the input fields used to select and post-process output results produced by the program **AQUA** for **beam-related quantities**. The main purpose is to specify **which load case(s)** (LC) and **which material or direction components** to extract, as well as how to compute **envelope extremes** and **differences** (including the application of safety factors).

#### 1) Load case / scope of results
- **Item `LC`**: identifies the **load case number** (or design load case) whose results are used for the output at beams.
- The description clarifies that selecting a specific **LC or design load case** affects all results stored relative to that same reference load case.
- Reinforcement design stresses (from **BEMESS**) and beam stresses (from **AQB**) are treated specially: they are represented using the **design load case** input. Other load-case-wise stored results are addressed by **`NO`** (explicitly stated as *equivalently to NO* depending on context).

#### 2) Material selection for composite beams / multiple materials
- **Item `MAT` (Reference material, equivalent to MAT)**: selects a specific **material** among multiple materials available for the same LC/design case (typical for composite beams).
- If **`MAT` is not provided**, the **first material found** is used.
- If the table uses special material tokens:
  - `_MID` average
  - `_MAX` maximum
  - `_MIN` minimum
  - `_AMX` absolute maximum
  - `_AMN` absolute minimum
  - `_LST` last
  - `_SUM` sum (noted for **beam bond force only**)
  then results across materials can be aggregated using the indicated operator.
- If **`REF`** (reference material) is provided, only materials of the **same type/classification** are used for combination/selection.

#### 3) Factors and directional differences (up to 3 directions)
The table provides mechanisms to modify values using:
- **Items `FAC1`, `FAC2`, `FAC3`**: numeric **factors** applied to numerical values in up to **three directions** (X, Y, Z). Defaults are indicated as **1** for factors.
- **Items `DIF1`, `DIF2`, `DIF3`**: **difference values** computed/added to generate additional outputs showing deviations (e.g., exceedance against limits). Defaults shown as **0**.

#### 4) Direction component selection
- **Item `DIRE`** selects which directions are represented:
  - `X_` / `1` = first direction (X)
  - `Y_` / `2` = second direction (Y)
  - `Z_` / `3` = third direction (Z)
  - `XY` / `1+2`, `XZ` / `1+3`, `YZ` / `2+3`, or `XYZ` / `ALL` for all.
- This aligns with the note that some results exist in **multiple direction components (maximum 3)** and may be filtered if not all directions are needed.

#### 5) Material law selection for nonlinear material laws
- For nonlinear results from **TALPA/ASE** (area/volume elements), a separate material-law selector exists:
  - **`NMAT`** chooses a specific **nonlinear material law**.
  - If `NMAT` is omitted, the **first law found** is used.
- The table lists many literal material law identifiers (e.g., `EC_C`, `EC2 Light weight`, `EC_CE`, `DN_C`, `OELB`, etc.), representing standard codes and variants (elastic no tension, deformation A/B, lightweight, prestressing, etc.).

#### 6) Beam stress location parameters
Beam-related positional and identification inputs are included:
- **`ENO`**: beam number for area stresses (from **AQB**). It is stated to be equivalent to **NO** (contextually meaning the same input index naming).
- **`X`**: beam abscissa coordinate for area stresses (also from **AQB**), equivalent to **NO** per the note.

#### 7) Additional semantics (difference generation, legends, and kind comparisons)
- Safety-factor handling: “results from the database can be modified to consider requested safety factors subsequently” and “used factors are written into the legend.”
- Differences vs database: differences can be generated additionally using `DIF1..DIF3`, and “used difference values are written into the legend.”
- Conditional comparison capability: the table references a **`KIND`** option to compare two load/design cases using numeric operations for real-valued results (not available for system values/loads/texts). It requires two LC records and supports directed component logic (e.g., vector difference uses global direction components; multiplication uses scalar product; division uses quotient and direction derived from norms).

**Overall**, this table is a configuration schema for extracting and post-processing beam output in AQUA, combining: (1) load case selection, (2) material/material-law selection, (3) directional filtering (X/Y/Z), and (4) optional scaling and differential exceedance computations via factors and difference values.

This table snippet defines the parameters for selecting and post-processing *beam/output results* produced by programs such as **AQUA** (beam-related output), and it also controls how **load cases (LC)** / **design cases** are mapped to displayed values and legends. It is organized conceptually as a list of selectable items (fields) with defaults, units, and cross-references to how values are interpreted.

### Key selection fields
- **LC**: identifies the load case (or range, when used with *KIND*). The input (except for certain text selectors like **NAME/FIND**, not shown here) is used to select the stored results tied to that load case. It also determines which results are shown for all referenced program outputs.
- **FIRS** / **ENO** / **X**: define a beam location context for “area stresses” from program **AQB**:
  - **ENO**: beam number (equivalently to **NO**), used to choose which beam.
  - **X**: beam abscissa position (equivalently to **NO** per the text’s phrasing), defining where along the beam the result is taken.
  - **FIRS** appears as an indicator/label related to that same AQB area-stress selection block (also described as “equivalently to NO” in the provided text).  
  All three are about mapping the result to the correct beam and position.

### Beam/stress direction handling
Some results are vector/tensor-like and can be resolved into multiple directions (up to 3).
- **DIRE** selects which direction components are represented:
  - **X_ / 1** = first direction
  - **Y_ / 2** = second direction
  - **Z_ / 3** = third direction
  - **XY / 1+2**, **XZ / 1+3**, **YZ / 2+3**, **XYZ / ALL**
  This affects which directional components are plotted/printed for values that exist in multiple directions.

### Material selection (linear and nonlinear)
The table supports selecting among multiple materials or material laws stored under the same LC.
- **MAT** (reference to “material law to be represented” in nonlinear cases is stated as equivalent to MAT for material choice):  
  Selection literals enable choosing a specific concrete/material among those present for composite beams. If **MAT** is not provided, the “first found” material is used. If **_MID/_MAX/_MIN/_AMX/_AMN/_LST/_SUM** are given, then *all materials* are used.
- **REF**: a reference material additional to **MAT**. If **REF** is input, only materials of the same **type and classification** are considered (i.e., filtering comparable material sets).
- **NMAT** (nonlinear material laws): for nonlinear material laws from **TALPA/ASE**, results for different laws share the same LC. **NMAT** selects the law; if missing, the first found is used.

#### Material/law literal list
A large set of concrete/material law literals is provided (e.g., **EC_C, ECLC, ECCE, ECDA, DN_C, DNLC, OE_B, SA_C, BSLC, AIHC, JILC, GBHC, ISLC, SN_C, BA_B, B0_C**, etc.). This list is intended for direct input of the material law name/literal to drive **MAT/NMAT**-type selection.

### Value aggregation vs extremum/summary
The table defines how to derive displayed values over materials or over LC ranges:
- **Use suffix-style selectors** (shown as: `_MID`, `_MAX`, `_MIN`, `_AMX`, `_AMN`, `_LST`, `_SUM`):
  - `_MID` average value
  - `_MAX` maximum, `_MIN` minimum
  - `_AMX` absolute maximum, `_AMN` absolute minimum
  - `_LST` last value
  - `_SUM` sum (explicitly noted: “beam bond force only”)
- **Factors for numerical values**: **FAC1, FAC2, FAC3** apply up to three multiplicative factors to numerical values (designed for combinations).
- **DIF1, DIF2, DIF3** represent “Differences for numerical in a maximum of 3 directions,” enabling generation of additional difference results relative to limits/secondary references. Used difference values are written into the legend.

### Load-case comparisons and safety factors
- A design/safety-factor system is referenced: “results from the database can be modified to consider requested safety factors subsequently,” and the used factors appear in the legend.
- **KIND** enables comparison/envelope operations between two LC/design cases when the values are real numbers. It is **not available** for system values, loads, and texts.
  - The comparison uses global direction components for directed operations like addition/difference/multiplication.
  - For multiplication, the scalar product is used; for division, the raw value is used; the new direction is obtained from the normed scalar product.
  - Example given shows using **KIND TMAX/TMIN** with LC ranges (e.g., 1001–1010) and directional selection to build positive/negative extrema for an envelope.

### Relevance to other result categories (context)
The snippet includes “See also: LOAD, NODE, BEAM, QUAD, ISOL, SECT” indicating that this table is part of a larger result-representation system, where LOAD/NODE/BEAM/SECT likely provide location and entity scoping, while QUAD/ISOL relate to area/solid element output.

Overall, the table is a configuration schema that controls **which load case**, **which beam entity and position**, **which direction components**, and **which material/material law** (including nonlinear laws) are used, plus how **extrema, sums, factors, and differences** are computed and reported in legends.

The table defines metadata for two configuration “Items” used when selecting and presenting structural analysis/design results from load cases (LC). It has columns **Item**, **Description**, **Unit**, and **Default**.

## Table structure
- **Item**: keyword identifying the parameter to be set by the user.
- **Description**: textual explanation of what the keyword does.
- **Unit**: unit type expected/used for the item (here shown as **LIT** for both entries, meaning it is a literal/configuration selector rather than a physical quantity).
- **Default**: default value if the item is omitted (shown as “-” for KIND and “*” for TITL).

## Row 1: KIND
- **Item**: `KIND`
- **Description**: “Kind of comparison of results.”
- **Unit**: `LIT`
- **Default**: `-` (no default behavior stated in the table; implies KIND must be specified to activate a comparison mode)
- **Behavior**: selects how values from **two** load cases/design cases or from an **LC range** are combined for the output. The supported modes are:
  - **No comparison** (`No comparison`)
  - **AMX**: absolute maximum of two LCs
  - **MAX**: maximum of two LCs
  - **MIN**: minimum of two LCs
  - **DIF**: difference between two LCs
  - **DIV**: division of two LCs
  - **ADD**: addition of two LCs
  - **TAMX**: absolute maximum over an LC range
  - **TMAX**: maximum over an LC range
  - **TMIN**: minimum over an LC range
  - **TADD**: addition over an LC range

From the surrounding context, these operations can be direction-aware for vector quantities: for example, comparisons involving directions can use global direction components, where differences of displacement vectors are performed component-wise, and for multiplication a scalar product is used; for division the scalar value is used. The table itself focuses on the selection keywords.

## Row 2: TITL
- **Item**: `TITL`
- **Description**: “Designation of the load case in the legend (default as in the database)”
- **Unit**: `LIT24`
- **Default**: `*`
- **Meaning**: provides the **legend label** shown in the output for the selected LC/result representation. If not provided, the legend uses the database title (as noted in the description). This affects visualization/labeling rather than numerical result calculation.

Overall, this table documents how to (1) choose the computational relationship between load-case results via **KIND**, and (2) optionally rename how the results appear in legends via **TITL**.

The provided table excerpt documents **DSGN** as an input item describing the **“type” and geometry/orientation of a graphical representation** used in results visualization. The table is primarily about configuring how a representation is drawn for structural elements and related quantities, including its **direction**, **length**, and **coordinate reference**.

## Core field: `DSGN`
- **Item**: `DSGN`
- **Description**: “Item Description Unit Default”
- **Meaning**: `DSGN` sets the *representation* behavior. It is closely tied to the concept of **vector/line/area graphics** and their orientation in local/global coordinate systems.
- **Context linkage**: The “See also” list (ARRO, STRU, LOAD, NODE, BEAM, QUAD, ISOL, SECT) suggests DSGN is part of a broader graphics/result-definition framework across multiple element types.

## Main control: `DTYP` (Type of the representation)
- **Item**: `DTYP`
- **Unit/Default**: not explicitly given; default behavior described qualitatively.
- **Purpose**: Specifies which **representation category** is valid for the first *LT* ALL input.
- **Accepted values**:
  - `ALL`: All types of representation
  - `SING`: Only single/vector representation
  - `LINE`: Only line-shaped representations
  - `AREA`: Only area-shaped representations

- **Related directional options**: The table indicates direction codes that depend on whether a line-shaped representation is used and how “perpendicular” is defined.

## Direction control: `URIC` (direction of representation) / default direction
- **Item**: `URIC`
- **Purpose**: Selects the **direction** the representation uses.
- **Direction keywords**:
  - `X`, `Y`, `Z`: Local element x/y/z directions (`URIC X/ Y/ Z`)
  - `XX`, `YY`, `ZZ`: Global system X/Y/Z directions (`URIC XX/YY/ZZ`)
  - `EG`: gravity load direction (`URIC EG`)
- **Picture-based direction qualifiers**:
  - `BX`: horizontally at the picture
  - `BY`: vertically at the picture
- **Line-specific perpendicular/relative directions** (for line-like elements):
  - `PP`: horizontally perpendicular to the line direction (right-hand side)
  - `PQ`: perpendicular to `PP`
  - `EP`: perpendicular to the line direction upwards
  - `EQ`: perpendicular to `EP`
  - `NM`: perpendicular to `PP,` else `BX` (conditional defaulting behavior)

- **Coordination logic statement**: “A useful representation (mostly the action direction) direction is available in a pre–defined form for each result. This can be changed with DTYP.” This indicates that default direction choices may come from the result type, but can be overridden via the direction configuration.

## Length control: `LENG`, `LMAX`, `LMIN`
The table explains representation scaling and clipping protection:
- **`LENG`**: “Fixed defined length of the representation” (example given: cm * coordinate systems).
  - Effect: If `LENG` is defined, **all representations get exactly this uniform length**, regardless of result size.
- **`LMAX`**: “Maximum length of the representation”
  - Purpose: prevents large representations from exceeding the picture boundary.
  - It also notes that at such points representations are marked with an alternative line type `LFRB`.
- **`LMIN`**: “Minimum length of the representation” (example shown with `cm 10.` and `cm 0.`)
  - Purpose: ensures very small representations remain visible/legible.

## Distance placement control: `DIST`, `DISX`, `DISY`, plus `DVAR` context
- **`DIST`**
  - Meaning: “Distance at the beginning from the starting point on the structure element”
  - Unit: `cm/−` (the table indicates a scaling with sign/option)
  - Default: shown as `−/` with a negative value-like placeholder (excerpt shows “− 0.”)
  - Additional note: applies “as for record SCH2”
- **`DISX`, `DISY`**
  - Meaning: Direction for the distance at the beginning as a **three-dimensional vector** or literal, “as for the item DTYP”
  - The table further indicates `DISX` and `DISY` correspond to distance direction variants based on record SCH2 DX/DY/DZ.
  - This suggests that the start offset can be oriented using explicit local/global or vector direction logic.

## Overall intent
Collectively, this table excerpt defines a **visual representation directive**:
- Choose **which representation types** to show (`DTYP`).
- Determine **orientation** via local/global or semantic direction keywords (`URIC`).
- Control **where** the representation begins along the element (`DIST`, directional components `DISX`/`DISY`).
- Control **how long** the representation appears (`LENG`, bounded by `LMAX` and `LMIN`), including protective behavior (`LFRB` marking) and visibility constraints for small values.

If you want, paste the continuation page(s) to capture missing defaults or any additional fields tied to `SCH2`, `DVAR`, or `LT ALL`.

The table defines input parameters that control the graphical “load arrow” representation used in a visualization system. It focuses on how arrow heads (and related transverse lines) are styled and positioned for different result directions and representation types.

**Item / Description / Unit / Default** structure:  
- **Item** names the input field.  
- **Description** explains the meaning and rules for the field, including valid contexts.  
- **Unit** indicates either a direct unit (centimeters) or a dimensionless factor (when values are negative).  
- **Default** provides a default behavior/value for the parameter.

### Fields captured in the table
**1) TYPE**  
Specifies which representation category the settings apply to. Allowed values are:  
- **ALL**: applies to all representations  
- **SING**: only single/vector representations  
- **LINE**: only line-shaped representations  
- **AREA**: only area-shaped representations  
Default is **ALL**. Unit shown is **LIT** (logical/integer literal type).

**2) KIND**  
Controls the **kind of arrow head in the view**. Two modes:  
- **STAN**: uses a system default depending on the current result type (explicitly “different for each case”).  
- Otherwise, a **literal with four alphabetic characters** defines the arrow head style. In these four characters:  
  - **1st character** selects the arrow head type (e.g., no head, transverse line, open/closed/filled arrows, half-page variants on left/right, etc.).  
  - **2nd character** selects multiple heads count (single/double/threefold/fourfold).  
  - **3rd character** selects additional transverse lines (none or 1–3 behind the arrow head, or certain “end transverse line” variants).  
  - **4th character** encodes additional properties via a bit-pattern using symbols: digits **0–9** for bit patterns 0–9, or letters **A–Z** for bit patterns 10–37. This bit pattern governs insertion point placement (beginning/end/central), rotated direction, both-sides arrow heads, special handling for positive vs negative values, etc.  
Unit is **LIT**. Default is **STAN**.

**3) KIN2 and KIN3**  
Define arrow head kinds for the **2nd and 3rd direction** respectively, using the same concept as **KIND** (a literal or STAN).  
- **KIN2** default: **KIN D** (i.e., inherits/uses KIND)  
- **KIN3** default: **KIND**  
Unit: **LIT**.

**4) LENG** (Length of the arrow head)  
Controls arrow head size/length. Value interpretation:  
- **> 0**: given in **cm**  
- **< 0**: treated as a **factor**  
Special rule:  
- For **TYPE SING / AREA**, LENG is the length of the vector itself.  
- Otherwise, it uses the distance between **direction vectors** (FDIC).  
Default values shown in the table: **-0.2**.

**5) WIDE** (Width of the arrow head)  
Controls arrow head width using the same numeric interpretation rules:  
- **> 0**: **cm**  
- **< 0**: **factor**  
Special rule:  
- For **TYPE SING / AREA**, WIDE relates to vector length.  
- Otherwise, it uses the distance between direction vectors (FDIC).  
Default values shown in the table: **-0.15**.

**6) DOUB** (Distance of the next head for multiple arrow heads)  
Controls spacing between arrow heads when multiple heads are rendered.  
- **> 0**: **cm**  
- **< 0**: **factor of the arrow length (LENG)**  
Default: **-0.33** (cm/– in unit column indicates “cm or factor”).

**7) CROS** (Distance of additional transverse lines)  
Controls spacing for added transverse lines related to the arrow head style.  
- **> 0**: **cm**  
- **< 0**: **factor** (implied by table pattern as a cm/– type field)  
Default: **-0.25**.

### Overall meaning
This table parameterizes arrow-head geometry and behavior (style, multiplicity, transverse-line details, insertion-point/bits, and geometric scaling). It also supports direction-dependent styling (KIN2/KIN3) and restricts applicability by representation type (TYPE). The literals (KIND/KIN2/KIN3) are four-character codes where each character or bit-region encodes a specific visual property.

This table section specifies how **load/moment arrow graphics** are rendered in a structural representation, focusing on several related configuration parameters (e.g., **arrow head style**, **top-view symbol style**, and **line/area fill behavior**). It also references arrow geometry scaling by defining distances using **factors** of other lengths.

## Arrow head sizing and distance factors
The parameters **>0 in cm** and **<0 as factor of the arrow length LENG** describe a distance/offset value (e.g., spacing or placement distance).  
- If the value is **positive**, it is interpreted directly in **centimeters**.

  - **D** design elements

  - **P** pile elements
  - **C** truss and cable elements
  - **I** external beam sections (stored only by **SIR** or **AQB**

#### 3) Literal options for BEAM TYPE (what can be selected)
A large enumerated list follows, mapping **TYPE literals** to physical quantities and units. Each literal corresponds to a result that can be drawn along the beam element:
- **Hinge reactions / displacements / rotations / performance indices**
  - Examples: **HNS** (hinge reaction N), **HVYS** (Vy), **HVZS** (Vz), **HMTS** (Mt), **HMYS** (My), **HMZS** (Mz)
  - **HNT** nonlinear hinge displacement (tension direction mentioned)
  - Performance-index variants: **HMZ2**, **HMY3**, **HMZ3**, **HMY4**, etc.
