  - **SPY**, **SPZ** (spring force components), **SPM** (spring moments)
  - Area-related representations: **ASP**, **ASPV**, **ASPX**, **ASP Y**
- **Tendon design stresses for QUAD elements** (when STYP has no effect)
  - **SGMA** (maximum), **SGMI** (minimum), **SGPM** (permanent), **SGSW** (stress range)
- **Cross-section forces and stress measures**
  - Internal forces: **EN** (axial force N), **EVY** (shear Vy)
  - **BOND** bond force; **BNDO** dowel shear; stress point min/max/others: **SDPT**, **SZPT**, **STPT**, **SVPT**, **SPCP**
- **Utilisation and decisive checks**
  - **CSCL / CPCL / CECL** (cross-section class variants)
  - **CCHK** check/utilisation level
  - **TCF**, **SCCB**, **SCBN**, **ULN/ULVY/ULVZ/ULMT/ULMY/ULMZ/ULMB/ULM2** (decisive results and utilization of N/V/M/torsion bending/warping/secondary torsion)

- Stirrup layers: **ASU9**, **ASUA** (layer 10), **ASUF** (layer 15) etc., plus torsional reinforcement: **AST**, **AST0**, **AST9**, **ASTA**.

- Some diagrams compute **maximum values internally** using cubic/parabolic engineering-line fitting from known shear/moment or displacement/rotation derivatives.
  - These maxima are **not saved**, and **cannot be used for superposition/design calculations**.
- Stress definitions distinguish **uniaxial stresses (SIGU/SIGL)** vs **min/max total section stresses (SIGD/SIGZ)**; truss/cable normal stresses map to **SIGU**.
- **BOND** is computed from longitudinal force differences between beam sections; composite materials may require **LC MAT** selection.

- **CSGC**: Utilisation level of common materials (except concrete) → **Dim.: –**
- **CSGT**: Longitudinal tension → **Dim.: –**
- **CSHE**: τ Shear stress → **Dim.: –**
- **CSGV**: σ–v Von Mises stress → **Dim.: –**
Overall, these appear to be **utilisation/performance measures**, not raw stresses with conventional force units (hence the dimensionless “–”).

### Shear wall design quantities (reinforcement and geometry)
These are mainly reinforcement-related wall design outputs with explicit units:
- **SWVT**: Vertical reinforcement (total) → **cm²**
- **SWST**: Shear reinforcement (total) → **cm²/m**
- **SWL1**: Vertical reinforcement in mid zone → **cm²**
- **SWL2**: Vertical reinforcement in edge zone A (+Z) → **cm²**
- **SWL3**: Vertical reinforcement in edge zone B (−Z) → **cm²**
- **SWS1**: Shear reinforcement in wall → **cm²/m**
- **SWS2**: Shear reinforcement in edge zone A (+Z) → **cm²/m**
- **SWS3**: Shear reinforcement in edge zone B (−Z) → **cm²/m**
- **SWWA**: Width of edge zone A (+Z) → **m**
- **SWWB**: Width of edge zone B (−Z) → **m**

The sign conventions (+Z / −Z) indicate how edge zones are referenced relative to the local/global Z direction used by the program’s representation rules.

### General reinforcement layers and stirrups
These entries provide reinforcement area by layer and stirrup reinforcement:
- **AS**: Total reinforcement → **cm²**
- **ASØ**: Reinforcement layer 0 → **cm²**
- **AS1**: Reinforcement layer 1 (below) → **cm²**
- **AS2**: Reinforcement layer 2 (above) → **cm²**
- **AS9**: Reinforcement layer 9 → **cm²**
- **ASU**: Maximum stirrup reinforcement (including torsional stirrups) → **cm²/m**
- **ASUØ**: Stirrup reinforcement layer 0 (per cut part) → **cm²/m**
- The excerpt ends with a continuation marker (e.g., “ASU9 …”), implying further layer-specific stirrup quantities follow with the same unit pattern (**cm²/m**).

## Relationship to BEAM record behaviour
In the broader BEAM context, these literals are used to select what results are drawn/represented. Only one **element type** (via **TYPE/STYP/DSGN**) can be edited at a time, and availability depends on the earlier **D/B/P/C/I** availability flags. These wall/reinforcement literals are therefore intended for diagrams/status lines where reinforcement and shear-wall design outputs are available for the selected element types.

The table documents **BEAM representation output/instruction options**. Its schema contains four columns:

1. **D B P C T I** (availability selector/sign mask): indicates for which element categories/program contexts the corresponding result is available. Asterisks and dashes represent availability in different combinations:
   - `*` = generally available for the indicated context(s)
   - `-` = not available
   - The mask columns encode whether values exist for **Design elements (D)**, **Beam elements (B)**, **Pile elements (P)**, **Truss/Cable elements (C)**, and additional context fields **T** and **I** (the source text explains broader sign semantics for stored vs. not-stored values and special program-only storage, e.g., STAR2/AQB/ASE/COMPOSITE).
2. **Literal**: the internal code name used in the BEAM-type configuration.
3. **Meaning**: human-readable description of the represented quantity.
4. **Dim.**: the physical dimension/unit of the quantity (or `-` if dimensionless / not specified).

 The stresses SIGU and SIGL are uniaxial stresses (e.g. for prestressed concrete) according to the ratio M/W for the external fibres which were determined by the program AQB. On the other hand SIGD and SIGZ are minimum and maximum stresses in the total cross section. The normal stresses for truss elements and cables are represented with SIGU.
 The bond force BOND is calculated from the difference of longitudinal forces per material be- tween the beam sections. If more than one material exists the total can be calculated (LC MAT _SUM REF...).
 ENER and PIEZ are drawn in the global Z direction with reference to the minimum Z coordinate. In this cases the geometric scale is the default for UNIT.
 Representation
 Representation
 Logical defaults are prescribed for the representation directions of all values. The usual values are represented along the local y or z axis. Influence lines are drawn with their components in the global coordinate directions. In special cases (for example the line of vision is equal to a local axis, but also for moment diagram in USA) all other types of representation can be selected by using DTYP.

The usual values are represented along the local y or z axis. Influence lines are drawn with their components in the global coordinate directions. In special cases (for example the line of vision is equal to a local axis, but also for moment diagram in USA) all other types of representation can be selected by using DTYP..
 The values are represented always with their real dimension also in the skew directions.
 Additional designations are represented at the status lines, if SCHH is not zero. The amount of the designations can be controlled with STAT. No designations occur, if the distance of the beam sections becomes smaller than the text height and the check of the text is not activated (record SCHH REVI).
 If shear forces (derivatives of moments) are known in beam sections, a cubic parabola is drawn to create an engineering line. In this case maximum values may be calculated. The user has to check these maximum values if the loads include line moments, because high-order moment lines are generated then. Or more nodes or beam sections have to be defined. A warning is printed.
 Attention: These (maximum) values are generated internally in GRAPHIC/WING. They are not saved in the database and are not provided for superpositioning and design calculation.
 Beam displacements
 If rotations (derivatives of displacements) are known in beam sections, a cubic parabola is drawn to create an engineering line. In this case maximum values may be calculated. The user has to check these maximum values because these cubic parabola results from the displacements formulation of Finite Elements Method (solution of minimum of deformations energy) and each loading (e.g. line loads) requires a high-order line. Or more nodes or beam sections have to be defined. A warning is printed.
 Attention: These (maximum) values are generated internally in GRAPHIC/WING. They are not saved in the database and are not provided for superpositioning and design calculation.
 Beam loading
 The loading is represented with its defined distribution considering the load factors, the gravity loading, the moments due to the eccentric loading and the generated loads.
 Point loads are drawn as vectors with UNI2.
 Composite cross sections
 A material number (record LC MAT) for SIGU to SIGV must be specified for composite cross sections. The results can be saved in the database also with a stress point defined in the program AQUA. Then the designation (literal) of this stress point can be input for MAT.

Point loads are drawn as vectors with UNI2.. Composite cross sections. A material number (record LC MAT) for SIGU to SIGV must be specified for composite cross sections. The results can be saved in the database also with a stress point defined in the program AQUA. Then the designation (literal) of this stress point can be input for MAT..

 The internal forces and moments of inherent stresses of the cross section from creep and shrinkage are added to the internal forces and moments N...MT1, if they are available in this load case.

The table defines the **“QUAD” representation** settings for a graphical output system (SOFiSTiK/WING/GRAPHIC context). It provides a schema for how **quadrilateral (QUAD) element results** are converted into drawing primitives (status lines, vectors, isolines, cut representations, tensor/vector arrows, and fill areas), including scaling, text size, element selection, and especially the choice of **TYPE** (the physical quantity) and **STYP** (where the quantity is evaluated on/around the element).

Key fields and their meaning:
- **Item / Description / TYPE**: **TYPE** identifies the physical result to be represented (e.g., stresses, shear forces, displacements, bedding stresses, principal stresses, reinforcement design values). The note “DSGN does set only the input values, does not draw anything” indicates TYPE=**DSGN** behaves as a design data container rather than a visual result.
- **UNIT**: scaling description for length of representations; units vary per TYPE (e.g., kN/m, kN/m², m, cm²/m, N/mm², mm).
- **STRU**: structure-related plotting parameters (e.g., text height via SCHH; thickness plotted with STRU for area element structure values).
- **SCHH / SCH2 MIN / MINT**: text height and obsolete minimum-threshold controls. **MIN**-type entries define an input minimum value that is compared against support reactions for certain drawings (e.g., isolines/cuts).
- **STYP (element value location / sampling)**: how values are sampled:
  - **NODE**: nodal values of QUAD elements
  - **QUAD**: centre of QUAD elements
  - **GAUS**: Gauss points (four near corners + one middle for QUAD)
  - **FULL NODE + QUAD E2N / G2N**: averaged nodal values derived from element centres or Gauss points (E2N, G2N)
  - **ERIN**: error estimates in element centre
  - **EE2N**: averaged values read from error estimates
  - **BRIC / BRIK**: centre and nodes for BRIC volume elements
- **ND**: number of decimal points after comma (via SCHH ND).
- **FILL / DIST / REVI**: fill-related appearance options; some items are obsolete and replaced by SCHH entries.
- **ELEM/ Centre identifiers**: **E2N/G2N** are used specifically to move/smooth distributions for isolines/cuts.
- **REPR modes**: The table’s content heavily links STYP/TYPE with drawing representation modes:
  - **Representation as Tensor / Vector (REPR DVEC, DARE, DREP, DTXT)**: certain TYPES are drawn as vectors/lines in projected or effective directions; negative values can be shown with short limit lines.
  - **Vector flow velocity**: TYPE FL, PA, Q draw as projected-direction vectors.
  - **All other single values**: drawn in effective direction; isolines, cuts, fill area are also possible.
  - **Error estimate printing**: STYP ERIN is available for a specified set of TYPES if requested during calculation.
  - **Representation at Isolines (REPR DISO)**: isolines are computed element-by-element from nodal values using hyperbolas; labels are readable “uphill”, optional explicit designation via SCHH if many isolines are active, and interval labeling via DTXT.
  - **Representation at Cuts (REPR DCUT)**: QUAD elements intersecting active DRAW elements define cuts; results become status lines along cuts and may be converted to marked areas. Cut coordinates define directions **N** (cut line) and **T** (perpendicular in element plane). Weld seam stresses are approximated using plate assumptions.

Computation/interpretation rules embedded in the table:
- QUAD elements use **5 Gauss points**: four near corners and one middle; the middle corresponds to STYP **QUAD**. For some nonlinear results, corner Gauss point values may be output (STYP **GAUS**).
- Smoothed nodal distributions for cuts/isolines can be obtained by averaging: **G2N** (average of Gauss points at nodes) vs **E2N** (shift centre value to nodes then average).
- Error estimates may not exist at nodes from the solver; WING can derive them similarly via **EE2N**.
- Isoline generation uses **nodal values**; STYP controls whether nodal values are used directly or derived from element centres.
- For weld seam outputs after a cut definition, geometric weld seam thickness is approximated by cut plate thickness, and stresses are mapped from slab/plate stress components (σ⊥, τ∥, τ⊥) derived from N/A ± M/W assumptions.

Overall, the table acts as a **controlled vocabulary and mapping specification**: choose **TYPE** (quantity and solver-dependent literal sets), choose **STYP** (location/averaging source), then use the configured representation mode (tensor/vector, isolines, cuts) to produce graphical outputs with correct units, scaling, and thresholding behavior.

sections: 3.44 QUAD – Single Results of QUAD Elements

content:
The input table defines the configuration fields for graphical output (primarily line and text related) for a 2D element/plate visualization context (SOFiSTiK GRAPHIC). It enumerates “Item” keys with human-readable “Description”, specifies the associated “Unit” (where applicable), and provides a “Default” value. Several entries are marked obsolete and redirect to newer records.

**Columns**
- **Item**: Parameter identifier used in the input.
- **Description**: Meaning/behavior of that parameter (often including allowed values).
- **Unit**: Measurement unit for numeric inputs.
- **Default**: Default behavior if the parameter is not explicitly set.

**Row-by-row description**
- **DANG (obsolete)**: Deprecated parameter; behavior removed. Default shown as `*` indicates wildcard/unspecified replacement in the original schema.
- **LEGX (obsolete)**: Deprecated; replaced by record reference **SCH2 FMVX**.
- **LEGY (obsolete)**: Deprecated; replaced by record reference **SCH2 FMVY**.

- **REPR**: Sets the **type of representation**.  
  - **Description**: “see record STRU REPR” (the specific representation mode is resolved via another record).
  - **Unit**: `LIT` (list/keyword type).
  - **Default**: `DARE` (i.e., the default representation style is “DARE”, consistent with the surrounding context where `REPR` typically selects between diagram, vectors, isolines, cuts, etc.).

- **AVER**: Controls averaging of results for **group boundaries** (contour lines) that are described via **STRU WCON**. Some result values can exist in boundary element nodes, and the switch determines whether those nodal values are averaged across the boundary.
  - **Allowed**:
    - **NO**: do not average; result jump remains (discontinuity preserved).
    - **YES**: average results (smoothing across nodes).
  - **Unit**: `LIT`
  - **Default**: `NO`

- **TOTA**: Defines the **sum of the line representation** for cuts/line displays.
  - **Description**: “see record NODE TOTA” (resolved through that record).
  - **Unit**: `LIT`
  - **Default**: `-` (no default sum behavior specified)

- **OFFZ**: Offset of the **designations** for the line representations; equivalent conceptually to **BEAM OFFZ**.
  - **Unit**: `LIT`
  - **Default**: `MIDD` (default designation placement strategy is “middle”)

- **CDIS**: Distance between designation labels for area representations.
  - **Unit**: `cm`
  - **Default**: `2.0`

- **COMT**: Summary rule for identical texts when **REPR DTXT** is active.
  - **Description**: “if REPR DTXT is switch on: YES/NO”
  - **Unit**: `LIT`
  - **Default**: `NO` (do not combine/summarize by default)

- **TOTTT**: Provides the texts of the sum (cut/line labeling aggregation).
  - **Description**: “see record NODE TOTT”
  - **Unit**: `LIT`
  - **Default**: `DEFA` (use default text set)

- **PUNT**: Texts used for “punching” output (punch reinforcement/status labels).
  - **Description**: provides submodes:
    - **DEFA**: use all texts
    - **N**: node number only
    - **V**: force only
    - **B**: eccentricity factor β only
  - **Unit**: `LIT`
  - **Default**: `DEFA`

**Data interpretation for RAG**
When indexing this table for retrieval, treat each “Item” as a configuration key for graphical post-processing: several parameters are **text placement/labeling controls** (OFFZ, CDIS, COMT, TOTT*, PUNT), while REPR and AVER control **how results are represented and smoothed** (representation mode and boundary averaging). Obsolete fields (DANG, LEGX, LEGY) should be mapped to their replacement record references during query-time normalization.

sections: 3.44 QUAD – Single Results of QUAD Elements

content:
The table documents a set of **QUAD “Literals”** (i.e., selectable result/quantity identifiers) used in SOFiSTiK/GRAPHIC to represent **plate/quadrilateral element** results. Each row lists (1) the literal code, (2) a human-readable meaning, and (3) the corresponding unit dimension. The quantities shown are specifically **force and moment resultants** distributed over the element length, given in **kN/m**.

### Structure of the table
- **Column 1: Literal** – short code (e.g., HM, MT, NI) that a user selects as the representation `TYPE` for QUAD results.
- **Column 2: Meaning** – description of what the code represents (e.g., “Principle moments, magnitude and direction”).
- **Column 3: Dim.** – the unit/dimension. In this table, all entries are in **kN/m**, indicating per-unit-length resultants consistent with plate elements (membrane forces and bending moments).

### Result categories covered
The table groups literals implicitly by headers:

#### 1) Bending moments (bending/moment resultants)
- **HM**: Principle (principal) moments, including magnitude and direction.
- **MT**: Principle moment I.
- **MIT**: Principle moment II.
- **BM**: Bending moments in local directions (overall bending).
- **MX**: Bending moment in local x.
- **MY**: Bending moment in local y.
- **MXY**: Twisting moment in local xy.
All are expressed in **kN/m**.

It also indicates special variants after a **cut definition**:
- **MN**: Bending moment along the cut direction.
- **MT**: Bending moment perpendicular to the cut.
- **MNT**: Twisting moment at the cut.
(Units remain **kN/m**.)  
This reflects that some quantities can be transformed into directions defined by an arbitrary cut.

#### 2) Membrane forces (in-plane force resultants)
- **HN**: Principal membrane forces, magnitude and direction.
- **NI**: Principal membrane force n–I.
- **NII**: Principal membrane force n–II.
- **N**: Membrane forces in local directions.
- **NX**: Membrane force in local x.
- **NY**: Membrane force in local y.
- **NXY**: Membrane shear force in local xy.
- **IN1**: Membrane force mean value (1st invariant), defined as **0.5 · (NX + NY)**.
- **IN2**: Membrane force deviator (2nd invariant), defined as **NX · NY − NXY²**.
Again, all are **kN/m**.

After a **cut definition**, additional directional components appear:
- **NN**: Membrane force in cut direction.
- **NT**: Membrane force perpendicular to the cut.
- **NNT**: Membrane shear force at the cut.
Units remain **kN/m**.

#### 3) Shear force resultants (transverse/shear)
- **VR**: Principal shear force (considered with sign).
- **BV**: Shear forces in local directions (sign included).
- **VX**: Shear force in local x (sign included).
- **VY**: Shear force in local y (sign included).
- **AVR**: Principal shear force (absolute value).
Units in the table are **kN/m** (including the absolute variant).

### Key modeling implication
The literal set is intended for graphical plotting of QUAD element resultants where:
- **local coordinate directions** are x/y,
- **principal directions** (I/II) and invariants are available,
- **cut-oriented results** (N/T for along/perpendicular, and similar for moments) are supported when a cut is defined,
- shear literals differentiate between signed and absolute magnitudes.

This table therefore serves as a **mapping index** from compact literal codes to their physical meaning and the unit used for visualization of QUAD output.

sections: 3.44 QUAD – Single Results of QUAD Elements

content:
The table defines **allowed plot/visualization literals (“Litteral”) for QUAD-type results** and, for each literal, provides a short **meaning** and the associated **dimension (Dim.)**. It is intended to be used as a dictionary for interpreting what a particular output quantity represents and in which physical unit it is measured.

### Column structure
- **Litteral**: A short code (e.g., `PTX`, `UX`) identifying the quantity to be represented.
- **Meaning**: Human-readable description of the physical quantity, including whether it is global, local, tangential, per element plane, or relative to a cut definition.
- **Dim. (Dimension)**: The unit used for that quantity (e.g., `kN/m^2`, `kN`, `m`, `kN/m^3`).

### Bedding stress / tangential bedding-related entries
These literals describe **tangential bedding stresses** and related combined scalars:
- `PTX`: Tangential bedding stress in **global X**, unit `kN/m^2`.
- `PTY`: Tangential bedding stress in **global Y**, unit `kN/m^2`.
- `PTZ`: Tangential bedding stress in **global Z**, unit `kN/m^2` (even though “bedding” is often in-plan, the definition explicitly includes Z in this scheme).
- `PTT`: **Total of tangential bedding stresses**, **without direction**, unit `kN/m^2`. The text notes it is “after ASE, DYNA”.
- `PR`: Resulting bedding values (resultant magnitude or combined bedding quantity), unit `kN`.
- `PTR`: Resulting tangential bedding (resultant tangential component), unit `kN`.
- `PEFF`: Effective bedding defined as **Bedding stress / settlement**, unit `kN/m^3`. This combines stiffness-like interpretation by dividing stress by displacement.

### Displacement-related entries (QUAD node quantities)
These literals relate to **displacements of QUAD nodes**:
- `U`: Vector of displacements of QUAD nodes, unit `m`.
- `UX`: Displacement global X at QUAD nodes, unit `m`.
- `UY`: Displacement global Y at QUAD nodes, unit `m`.
- `UZ,W`: Displacement global Z of QUAD nodes, unit `m` (the “W” suffix is likely a component naming convention).

### Local displacement components and cut-related directions
The table also includes **local-direction components**:
- `UXYZ`: Components of displacements of QUAD nodes in **local directions**, unit `m`.
- `UUX`: Displacement local x of QUAD nodes, unit `m`.
- `UUY`: Displacement local y of QUAD nodes, unit `m`.
- `UUZ`: Displacement local z of QUAD nodes, unit `m`.

And it includes geometric projections:
- `UUXY`: Displacement in the **xy plane of the QUAD element**, unit `m`.
- `UUN`: Displacement **in cut direction**, unit `m`. (Requires that a cut definition is active in the larger workflow.)
- `UUT`: Displacement **perpendicular to the cut**, unit `m`.

### Overall role in the QUAD “TYPE/STYP” system
In the broader QUAD result visualization context, these literals represent specific **TYPE keywords** whose values are fetched from the solution and then rendered. Their placement under a consistent “Meaning/Dim” schema makes them suitable for RAG retrieval: users can map a code to what it physically means and how to interpret the numeric values (e.g., distinguish **stress** vs **resultant force** vs **displacement** and **global** vs **local** vs **cut-oriented** components).

content:
The table defines how QUAD-related result quantities are represented for 2D quadrilateral (plate) elements in SOFiSTiK/GRAPHIC, focusing on the **TYPE** literals for stress measures and how they are computed and visualized. Each row specifies a **LITERAL**, its **Meaning**, the underlying formula (where given), and the **Dim.** (dimension/unit).

## Column: Litteral
A short code identifying the specific result variable to plot. In this excerpt, the primary literals are the equivalent-stress family and variants for upper/lower/middle positions and for weld seam evaluation.

## Column: Meaning (with formula)
The table provides engineering definitions:

- **SV**: *Maximum equivalent stress* computed using the “2D equivalent stress” concept  
  \[
  \sigma_{eq,2D}=\sqrt{S_{X}^2+S_{Y}^2-S_X S_Y+3T_{XY}^2}
  \]
  and extended conceptually to 3D:
  \[
  \sigma_{eq,3D}=\sqrt{0.5\big((S_X-S_Y)^2+(S_Y-S_Z)^2+(S_Z-S_X)^2\big)+6(T_{XY}^2+T_{YZ}^2+T_{ZX}^2)}
  \]
  The table indicates **SV** is the *maximum* equivalent stress “in 10 steps over the thickness” and is referenced as a composite result over the plate thickness via \((N/A \pm M/W)\).

- **SVU**: *Upper equivalent stress*  
  \((N/A - M/W)\), unit kN/m². Interpreted as the equivalent stress evaluated at the **top** surface using the sign convention in the thickness formula.

- **SVL**: *Lower equivalent stress*  
  \((N/A + M/W)\), unit kN/m², corresponding to the **bottom** surface.

- **SVM**: *Equivalent stress on middle*  
  Given as \((N/A)\) and computed from stresses with middle-thickness combination:
  \[
  SVM = SV + 3\cdot (PSIGX^2 + PSIGY^2)
  \]
  (as written in the table), unit kN/m².

- **SWNU**: After a cut definition, *Upper equivalent stress weld* computed as a weld-equivalent von-Mises-like measure:
  \[
  \sqrt{STU^2 + TTM^2 + SNTU^2}
  \]
  The table also shows the general upper/lower weld mapping as \((N/A \pm M/W)\) and gives **SWNU** specifically for the **upper** weld position.

- **(Weld equivalent stress weld)**: The table first states an “Equivalent stress weld” form:
  \[
  \sqrt{\sigma_{\perp}^2 + \tau_{\parallel}^2 + \tau_{\parallel}^2}
  \]
  (note: the last term appears duplicated as \(\tau_{\parallel}^2\) in the provided text; the intent is a weld stress invariant including normal and shear contributions). This is then specialized for upper weld stresses (e.g., SWNU).

## Column: TYPE-related context (from the surrounding text)
These literals are consistent with the broader QUAD/type mechanism: GRAPHIC can display results for different **positions through thickness** (upper/lower/middle) and, after defining cuts (REPR DCUT), can transform plate results into **cut/weld seam** stress evaluations (e.g., “weld” variants).

## Column: Dim. (dimension/unit)
All listed stress outputs in this excerpt have dimension **kN/m²** (consistent with stress units used in the QUAD plate stress context).

content:
The table is a fragment of a results/plotting specification for **SOFiSTiK quadrilateral (QUAD) elements**, focused on the **“weld seam stress” / weld equivalent stress** result literals and their mathematical definitions. It appears under a broader context where a user selects an output **TYPE** (what physical quantity to plot) and an **element location / extraction rule** (e.g., center vs. upper/lower, and whether values are taken as “N/A±M/W” combinations relative to the membrane/bending contributions).

## Column structure
1. **Literals (leftmost column):** Short codes (e.g., `SWNL`, `S3NL`) that identify the exact result type to be computed and displayed.
2. **Meaning (middle column):** Human-readable description of the physical quantity, including the formula used for its equivalent stress calculation.
3. **Dim. (right column, sometimes shown per row):** The physical unit of the result, indicated as **kN/m²** (stress units).

## Content and categories
### 1) Weld equivalent stress (overall / middle / upper-lower variants)
- `SWNL` — *Lower equivalent stress weld*  
  Defined using a square-root equivalent-stress formula with the text explicitly showing:  
  **SWNL = √( ST(L)² + … )** expressed as **(N/A + M/W)** style combination:  
  `SWNL` uses **(N/A + M/W)** where the specific split is “lower” (as indicated by the `L` in the literal).  
- `SWNM` — *Equivalent stress weld on middle*  
  Uses a “middle” extraction: **(N/A)** and a formula of the form:  
  **SWNM = √(ST(M)² + … )**, i.e. only the mid-layer/membrane component (per the text: “on middle”).

These literals correspond to equivalent stress measures for a weld seam, computed from underlying stress components and using the **(N/A) vs (M/W)** convention.

### 2) After cut definition: “S3” weld stresses (upper/lower/middle)
The table then states “**After a cut definition**” and introduces a related set for the welded seam stress results derived from cut-transformed plate stress components:
- `S3NU` — *Upper equivalent stress weld*  
  **S3NU = √(STU² + 3*(TTU² + SNTU²))** and the expression is given as **(N/A − M/W)**.
- `S3NL` — *Lower equivalent stress weld*  
  **S3NL = √(STL² + 3*(TTL² + SNTL²))** with **(N/A + M/W)**.
- `S3NM` — *Equivalent stress weld on middle*  
  **S3NM = √(STM² + 3*(TTM² + SNTM²))** using **(N/A)**.

Here `U/L/M` indicate **upper / lower / middle** locations with respect to the cut/plate representation. The factor **3** multiplies the sum of shear-like terms (TT and SNT), consistent with the equivalent stress construction.

### 3) Principal shear stress for weld seam
The table also lists principal shear stress quantities:
- `HTAU` — *Principal shear stress τxy-max* (maximum membrane shear)  
  **HTAU = √( (0.5*(SY − SX))² + TXY² )** (units: kN/m²).
- `HTUU` — *Upper principal shear stress*  
  Provided with the extraction rule **(N/A − M/W)**.
- `HTUL` — *Lower principal shear stress*  
  Provided with the extraction rule **(N/A + M/W)**.
- `HTUM` — *Principal shear stress on middle*  
  Uses **(N/A)**.

These entries indicate shear-stress principal values derived from the in-plane stress components **SX, SY, TXY**, again combined according to the “upper/lower/middle” convention.

## Practical interpretation for RAG
This table should be indexed as: **weld-seam equivalent stress and principal shear stress result literals**, including:
- the **exact literal codes**,
- the **upper/lower/middle selection logic** encoded in the suffix letters (U/L/M),
- the **membrane/bending extraction notation** in parentheses (**N/A**, **M/W**, and signs ±),
- and the **units** (kN/m²),
so retrieval can directly map a requested literal (e.g., `S3NL`) to its definition and physical meaning.

The literals shown are grouped by mechanical interpretation (principal stresses vs. shear stresses). Values are typically produced by plate/shear stress formulations involving principal directions and sign conventions, and are later mapped to graphical representation settings in the surrounding QUAD/GRAPHIC configuration.

### Columns
- **Literal**: A short code used in input records to select the result quantity.
- **Meaning**: Human-readable description of what physical quantity is displayed and how it relates to underlying N/A = M/W conventions or sign handling.
- **Dim.**: Engineering unit / dimension of the plotted value.

### Principal stress group (kN/m²)
These entries correspond to **principal stresses with N/A ≠ M/W** (i.e., distinguishing between top/middle vs. bottom or N/A vs. M/W evaluation schemes commonly used for slab stresses in plate formulations).

- **SPT** — *Maximum principal tensile stress*; unit **kN/m²**.  
- **SPTX** — *Principal tensile stress in local x direction*; unit **kN/m²**.  
- **SPTY** — *Principal tensile stress in local y direction*; unit **kN/m²**.  
- **SPC** — *Maximum principal compressive stress*; unit **kN/m²**.  
- **SPCX** — *Principal compressive stress in local x direction*; unit **kN/m²**.  
- **SPCY** — *Principal compressive stress in local y direction*; unit **kN/m²**.

Interpretation guidance implied by the wording: “local x/y” indicates that, rather than selecting only the scalar maximum/minimum principal stress, the stress is reported resolved along local element axes; N/A vs. M/W indicates whether the stress is taken at a specific slab location/evaluation scheme.

### Linear principal slab shear stress group (kN/m² and kN/m)
This subsection covers **principal slab shear stress** (with a formulation described as *1.5·V/b·h*) and also shear stresses derived from principal shear forces or local shear force components.

- **SSIG** — *Linear principal slab shear stress with 1.5·V/b·h, considered with sign*; unit **kN/m²**.  
- **ASSG** — *Same principal shear quantity as SSIG, but absolute value*; unit **kN/m²**.

Next, the table lists shear stresses in different ways:
- **HTM** — *Middle shear stress with V/A*; unit **kN/m**. Also described as “considered with sign”.  
- **NTM** — *Shear stress from shear forces in local directions (sign)*; unit **kN/m**.  
- **TXM** — *Shear stress from shear force in local x (considered with sign)*; unit **kN/m**.  
- **TYM** — *Shear stress from shear force in local y (considered with sign)*; unit **kN/m**.

Overall, the table acts as a lookup for result selection: users choose a **Literal** to instruct the graphics module which stress/shear measure (principal tensile/compressive, signed or absolute shear, resolved direction components) to compute and display, along with the expected **dimensional scale** (kN/m² for stress, kN/m for line-like shear output).

content:
The table documents a set of **GRAPHIC/SoFiSTiK QUAD result literals** that can be displayed for **plate/quad (area) elements**. It maps each **Literal** to its **Meaning** and the corresponding **Dimension (Dim.)**, focusing mainly on **shear stresses** and **in-plane/plane principal stresses**. Units are given for each result type, enabling consistent interpretation in graphical output and post-processing.

## Overall structure
Each row contains:
- **Literal**: short code used in input/output (e.g., `ANTM`).
- **Meaning**: descriptive explanation including whether values are in **local axes**, **cut coordinates**, or specific **averaging locations** (e.g., cut position vs. element center).
- **Dim.**: physical unit.

The table is organized into sections by context:
1. **General local stress/shear quantities** (no cut reference).
2. **After a cut definition** (values transformed to **cut direction** coordinates).
3. **Special stress components at the “middle” of N/A ± M/W representation** (upper stresses).

## Shear stresses from membrane/plate shear forces
For shear stress quantities with local directions, the table lists:
- `AHTM`: shear stress from **principal shear force (absolute)**, unit **kN/m**
- `ANTM`: shear stress from **absolute shear forces in local directions**, unit **kN/m**
- `ATXM`: shear stress from shear force magnitude **|v-x|** (local x), unit **kN/m**
- `ATYM`: shear stress from shear force magnitude **|v-y|** (local y), unit **kN/m**

These correspond to shear-related results typically derived from the plate’s local shear components (often denoted by velocity/force-like terms `v-x`, `v-y` depending on formulation).

## Shear stresses after a cut definition
When a **cut definition** is active, two directional shear stresses are available in **cut coordinates**:
- `TNM`: shear stress **in the cut direction**, unit **kN/m**
- `TTM`: shear stress **perpendicular to the cut**, unit **kN/m**
- `SNTM`: “membrane shear stress at the cut”, unit **kN/m²**

This indicates that, unlike the earlier kN/m shear stresses (line-like/force-per-length type), the cut-location shear stress can be reported as a stress quantity with **area-based unit kN/m²**, consistent with membrane stress reporting.

## Plane principal stresses (N/A±M/W middle)
The table then provides plane principal stresses (stresses in the plate plane) typically associated with a “middle” representation labeled **N/A**:
- `HSM`: plane principal stresses, unit **kN/m²**
- `SIM`: plane principal stress I, unit **kN/m²**
- `SIIM`: plane principal stress II, unit **kN/m²`

It also includes local-direction stresses and membrane shear stress:
- `NSM`: stresses in local directions, unit **kN/m²**
- `SXM`: stress in local x, unit **kN/m²**
- `SYM`: stress in local y, unit **kN/m²**
- `TXYM`: membrane shear stress in **xy** plane, unit **kN/m²**

Then invariant-based measures:
- `ISIM`: stress mean value (1st invariant), unit **kN/m²**  
  Formula shown: `ISIM = 0.5·(SXM + SYM)`
- `IS2M`: stress deviator (2nd invariant), unit **kN/m²**  
  Formula shown: `IS2M = SXM·SYM − TXYM²`

## Principal/upper stresses after cut and upper layers
A cut definition section for stresses in cut coordinates includes:
- `SNM`: stress **in the cut direction**, unit **kN/m²**
- `STM`: stress **perpendicular to the cut**, unit **kN/m²**
- `SNTM`: membrane shear stress at the cut, unit **kN/m²**

Finally, the “upper stresses with N/A – M/W” section introduces upper-plane principal stresses and corresponding components:
- `HSU`: upper plane principal stresses, unit **kN/m²**
- `SIU`: upper plane stress I, unit **kN/m²**
- `SIIMU`: upper plane stress II, unit **kN/m²** (shown as `SIIU` in the image section)
- `NSU`: upper stresses in local directions, unit **kN/m²**
- `SXU`: upper stress in local x, unit **kN/m²**
- `SYU`: upper stress in local y, unit **kN/m²**

In summary, the table defines how to interpret QUAD output literals for **shear** and **plane principal stress** quantities, including how their meaning changes when results are reported **along a cut** or for **upper layer (N/A − M/W)** stress states.

content:
This table enumerates **GRAPHIC/analysis result “literals”** (data keys) related to QUAD-type display quantities for reinforced concrete and composite/layered materials. Each row provides: **(1) Literal** identifier, **(2) Meaning** (what physical quantity is plotted/printed), and **(3) Dim.** giving the expected **unit or scaling format**.

## Structure of the table
- **Literal**: short code (e.g., `EPNL`) used as the `TYPE` value to select a result channel.
- **Meaning**: human-readable description of the quantity.
- **Dim.**: expected dimension for the output.
  - Many strain quantities use **`0/00`**, indicating a strain output typically expressed in **per mille / percent-style scaling** (exact convention is encoded elsewhere in the system).
  - Stress quantities use **`kN/m²`** (shown in the lower section), matching pressure/stress units for material layers and nonlinear stress results.

## Content groups and semantics
### 1) Strains in cut-aligned directions (top/bottom; parallel/perpendicular to cut)
These quantities are defined relative to a **cut direction** (within a cut definition context):
- `EPNu`: total **top strain** in **cut direction**  
- `EPTu`: total **top strain** **perpendicular to cut**
- `EPNL`: total **bottom strain** in **cut direction**
- `EPTL`: total **bottom strain** perpendicular to cut  
All use dimension **`0/00`** (strain scaling).

### 2) Concrete strain extrema / minimum-maximum strain states
- `ECON`: **maximum concrete compression strain** (`0/00`)
- `EREC`: **minimum averaged reinforcement strain**, including **(pre)strains** from temperature and creep per applicable work law (`0/00`)
- `ERET`: **maximum averaged reinforcement strain**, including temperature/creep prestrains (`0/00`)
- `EPSR`: **maximum reinforcement strain in the crack** (`0/00`)

These emphasize reinforcement strain evaluation with time-dependent effects.

### 3) Non-linear reinforcement stresses (top/bottom and maxima)
All stress results are in **`kN/m²`**:
- `SMU`: nonlinear **top reinforcement stress**
- `SML`: nonlinear **bottom reinforcement stress**
- `SMIUM`: nonlinear **top maximum reinforcement stress**
- `SMLM`: nonlinear **bottom maximum reinforcement stress**

### 4) Averaged steel strain extrema including prestrains
- `EPSC`: **minimum averaged steel strain**, including (pre)strains from temperature and strain loads per work law (`0/00`)
- `EPST`: **maximum averaged steel strain**, including (pre)strains from temperature and strain loads (`0/00`)

### 5) “Wrinkle” strains and layered material strains
These describe failure/imperfection modes and layered composites:
- `WRK1`: wrinkle **compression strain** in **1st direction**, displayed across to compression (`0/00`)
- `WRK2`: wrinkle **compression strain** in **2nd direction** (`0/00`)
- `FLSD`: minimum strain of **layered material** in **compression** (`0/00`)
- `FLSZ`: maximum strain of layered material in **tension** (`0/00`)
- `FLYC`: maximum compression stress of layered material (`kN/m²`)
- `FLYT`: maximum tensile stress of layered material (`kN/m²`)

### 6) Non-linear top stress components (local axes)
Non-linear top stress outputs in local coordinate system:
- `S2UN`: nonlinear **top stress** (`kN/m²`)
- `S2UX`: nonlinear top stress in **local x** (`kN/m²`)
- `S2UY`: nonlinear top stress in **local y** (`kN/m²`)
- `S2UT`: nonlinear top **shear stress xy** (`kN/m²`)

## How to use this table in a RAG context
Treat the rows as a **mapping vocabulary** from `TYPE`-literal → **result quantity description** → **expected unit class**. For search, the most discriminative fields are the literal itself and whether the quantity is:
- **strain vs stress**,
- **top vs bottom**,
- **cut-parallel vs cut-perpendicular**,
- **linear vs non-linear**,
- **global vs local axis** (x/y, shear xy),
- and whether **prestrains** (temperature/creep/work law) are included.

- `S2TL`: *Non-linear bottom stress perpendicular to cut*
- `S2SL`: *Non-linear bottom membrane shear stress in cut direction*
All have dimension **kN/m²** and are meaningful only when a **cut definition** is used, where the system distinguishes the **cut direction** vs **perpendicular direction** in the element plane (as described in the surrounding text about cuts).

### Material state / constitutive model variables (mostly dimensionless)
The remainder lists non-linear material response indicators and damage/crack/voiding variables, typically with dimension **“-”** (dimensionless) except where explicitly given:
- Yield/damage/plasticity surfaces:
  - `YIEL`: *Value of yield function (after TALPA)*
  - `YIEK`: *Value of yield function (after ASE)*
- Plasticization depths (units **mm**):
  - `PLDU`: *Upper plastification depth* (mm)
  - `PLDL`: *Lower plastification depth* (mm)
- Hardening/strain variables:
  - `YIE2`: *Deviatoric hardening variable*
  - `YIE3`: *Swelling strain – volumetric increment*
  - `YIE4`: *Volumetric hardening variable*
  - `YIE5`: *Isotropic preconsolidation stress*
- Damage, voiding, friction/utility indicators (dimensionless):
  - `VRAT`: *Void ratio*
  - `DVTE`: *Damage variable tension*
  - `DVCO`: *Damage variable compression*
  - `MOFA`: *Mobilized friction angle*
  - `UTIL`: *Utilisation level*
  - `ACCU`: *Accuracy indicator*
  - `MODA`: *Mobilized dilatancy angle*
- Crack/damage state:
  - `BPDS`: *Bit pattern for damage state (1 = active crack)* (dimensionless flag/pattern)
  - `CRAC`: *Current crack opening* (mm)

### Overall interpretation
This table serves as a **lookup dictionary** for interpreting QUAD result “TYPE” codes—especially **non-linear plate stress components** (top/bottom, principal/equivalent, and cut-direction variants) and **non-linear material state variables** (yield function values, plasticization depths, hardening variables, void ratio, tensile/compressive damage, mobilized friction/dilatancy, damage bit pattern, and crack opening). These literals can be used by the plotting system to request the correct field output and display it with the appropriate unit scaling.

sections: 3.44 QUAD – Single Results of QUAD Elements

content:
The table defines a mapping between **literals** (short code strings) and their **meaning** for stress/crack/hydration/material-state quantities used in QUAD-based result visualizations (e.g., in SOFiSTiK/WING). It has three columns: **Literal**, **Meaning**, and **Dim.** (dimension/unit). Each row specifies a distinct result parameter that can be selected as a QUAD “TYPE” value in the graphics/representation workflow.

### 1) Crack opening and damage-related state variables
- **CCR3** = “Current crack opening fault 3” with dimension **mm**.  
This indicates a crack opening displacement associated with fault/crack model component number 3.

- **STV1 … STV10** = “State variable 1 … 10” with dimension **–** (unitless/unspecified).  
These represent generic internal variables produced by nonlinear/damage/material models (e.g., hardening, damage evolution, or other constitutive states). Their exact semantics depend on the underlying material law and computation.

### 2) Hydration-related material parameters
- **HYFS** = “Hydration stiffness” (unit **MPa**)  
- **HYFT** = “Hydration tensile strength” (**MPa**)  
- **HYFC** = “Hydration compressive strength” (**MPa**)  
- **HYFK** = “Hydration factor” (**–**) (dimensionless)  
- **HYRT** = “Utilisation factor hydration tensile strength” (**–**)  
- **HYRC** = “Utilisation factor hydration compressive strength” (**–**)  

Together these rows describe stiffness/strength evolution and the degree to which tensile or compressive hydration strength is mobilized (utilisation factors). Hydration factor and utilisation factors are unitless.

### 3) Crack direction and maximum crack widths
- **WRU** = “Upper crack direction” (**–**)  
- **WRL** = “Lower crack direction” (**–**)  
These likely encode the local orientation (e.g., angle or directional indicator) of cracking for the upper and lower layers.

- **WUMX** = “Maximum upper crack width” (**mm**)  
- **WLMX** = “Maximum lower crack width” (**mm**)  
These provide scalar crack width maxima for upper and lower crack zones.

### 4) Compression depth measures (local directions/pressed states)
- **CDX** = “Minimum compression depth in local x” (**m**)  
- **CDY** = “Minimum compression depth in local y” (**m**)  
- **CD1** = “Minimum compression depth at least pressed uniaxial” (**m**)  
- **CD2** = “Minimum compression depth pressed biaxial” (**m**)  

These values quantify the smallest effective compression zone depth in local coordinate directions and under uniaxial/biaxial pressing conditions.

### 5) Concrete stress extrema in layers
- **SIGC** = “Maximum concrete compression stress” (**kN/m²**)  
- **SIGT** (visible next row) = “Maximum concrete tension in the concrete layers” (**kN/m²**)  

These represent extremal concrete stresses: the maximum compressive stress and maximum tensile stress over the modeled concrete layers.

### How to use for RAG indexing
Store each literal as a key phrase linked to its meaning and unit. For retrieval, emphasize that **the “Literal” column corresponds to selectable QUAD “TYPE” identifiers**, and the **Dim. column provides the expected measurement unit**, aiding disambiguation between similarly named quantities (e.g., crack width vs. crack direction; compression depth vs. stress).

sections: 3.44 QUAD – Single Results of QUAD Elements

content:
The input table is a legend/lookup for **QUAD result “TYPE” literals** used in SOFiSTiK/GRAPHIC-style plotting for **quadrilateral (plate/shell) elements**. It lists short codes in the first column (“Literal”), their engineering meaning in the second column (“Meaning”), and the associated physical dimension/unit in the third column (“Dim.”). The codes refer to stress state components and invariants typically produced by linear and/or non-linear analysis, and may also be re-mapped to **cut directions** when cuts are defined.

The section visible in the table comprises two groups:

1) **General (local) planar stress quantities (local directions):**
- **SII**: *Plane principal stress II (without part σ–z)* with unit **kN/m²**. This indicates the second principal stress in the plane of the element, explicitly excluding the out-of-plane component σ–z.
- **NS**: *Stress in local directions* with unit **kN/m²**. This is a generic label indicating that the stress field is resolved along local coordinate directions.
- **SX**: *Stress in local x* with unit **kN/m²**.
- **SY**: *Stress in local y* with unit **kN/m²**.
- **SZ**: *Stress in local z* with unit **kN/m²** (out-of-plane component).
- **TXY**: *Membrane shear stress xy* with unit **kN/m²**. This is the in-plane shear component on the x–y plane.
- **IS1**: *Stress mean value (1st invariant)* with unit **kN/m²**.
- **IS2**: *Stress deviator (2nd invariant)* with unit **kN/m²**. Together, IS1 and IS2 represent invariant-based descriptors of the stress state.
- **SIGV**: *Equivalent stress* with unit **kN/m²**. This represents a scalar equivalent (often von-Mises or similar depending on the program definition) used for failure/limit checks.

2) **Stresses after a cut definition (directional decomposition along the cut):**
When a cut is defined, stress quantities can be transformed into directions aligned with the **cut coordinate system**:
- **SN**: *Stress in cut direction* with unit **kN/m²** (N direction along the cutting line).
- **ST**: *Stress perpendicular to the cut* with unit **kN/m²** (T direction within the element plane but normal to the cut line).
- **SNT**: *Membrane shear stress n t at the cut* with unit **kN/m²**. This denotes the membrane shear component resolved in the (n,t) cut coordinate system.

Across the table, all displayed quantities use consistent stress units (**kN/m²**). In the broader context given (QUAD rendering options), these “TYPE” literals determine **what numeric result** GRAPHIC/visualization routines extract from the analysis for quad element plots, isolines, and cut status lines. Additionally, the meaning of some codes (e.g., SN/ST/SNT) depends on whether a **cut definition** is present, because the stresses are then expressed in cut-aligned directions rather than local x/y axes.

sections: 3.44 QUAD – Single Results of QUAD Elements

content:
The table defines **reinforcement- and design-related output literals** (likely for graphical or design checks in SOFiSTiK/related post-processing). Each row maps a **literal code** to its **meaning** and provides the associated **dimension/unit**. The structure is hierarchical: the first block is for **Multilayer design**, followed by **Baumann design**, with common reinforcement quantities expressed as either reinforcement areas per meter or indices/stresses.

### Columns
1. **Literal**: Short identifier (e.g., `MAS`, `MWK`, `ASUQ`) used as a selectable TYPE/result key in the software.
2. **Meaning**: Human-readable description of what the quantity represents.
3. **Dim. (Unit/Dimension)**: Engineering unit of the literal.

### Multilayer design block
- `MAS` **Reinforcement** (unit: `cm²/m`): Represents the reinforcement amount for multilayer design as an areal density along the member length.
- `MASS` **Stirrup reinforcement** (unit: `cm²/m²`): Stirrup content expressed per area, consistent with typical two-dimensional stirrup representation in plates or slabs.
- `MWK` **Crack width** (unit: `mm`): Crack opening width derived from multilayer/SL S (strain-based) assessment.
- `MSR` **Stress range** (unit: `N/mm²`): Difference or range of stress relevant for fatigue or SLS design contexts.
- `MSMA` **Maximum SLS design steel stress** (unit: `N/mm²`): Upper steel stress from SLS design.
- `MSMI` **Minimum SLS design steel stress** (unit: `N/mm²`): Lower steel stress from SLS design.

### Baumann design block
This block provides reinforcement components separated into upper/lower layers and principal/transverse directions:
- Upper side:
  - `ASU` **Upper reinforcement** (`cm²/m`)
  - `ASUH` **Upper principal reinforcement** (`cm²/m`)
  - `ASUQ` **Upper transverse reinforcement** (`cm²/m`)
  - `ASUI` **Upper 3rd reinforcement layer** (`cm²/m`)
  - `ASUM` **Upper maximum reinforcement** (`cm²/m`)
  - `ASUR` **Ratio upper principal/transverse reinforcement** (unit: `-`)
  - `ASUX` **Upper reinforcement index per element (netto, without constructive parts)** (unit: `kg`)
- Lower side:
  - `ASL` **Lower reinforcement** (`cm²/m`)
  - `ASLH` **Lower principal reinforcement** (`cm²/m`)
  - `ASLQ` **Lower transverse reinforcement** (`cm²/m`)
  - `ASLI` **Lower 3rd reinforcement layer** (`cm²/m`)

### Usage implications for RAG
These literals are **not geometry descriptions** but **semantic keys for design results** (reinforcement area densities, stress/crack outputs, and reinforcement ratios/indices). When indexing for retrieval, treat the literal as the primary join key to the unit/type of design output, and preserve the design category context (“Multilayer design” vs “Baumann design”) because the same themes (reinforcement, SLS limits) appear under different design methodologies.

sections: 3.44 QUAD – Single Results of QUAD Elements

content:
The table defines a mapping between **short “literal” codes** (left column) and their **meaning** plus the **unit/dimension** (right column). These literals represent **different result types for reinforced concrete design and punching/shear/fatigue checks**, typically used in the SOFiSTiK graphical output (e.g., in QUAD-based representations). The table does not contain numerical results themselves; it is a **dictionary** that tells consumers of RAG/documentation what each code stands for when configuring or interpreting output.

### Columns
1. **Literal**: an abbreviated identifier (e.g., `ASLM`, `ASQ`) used as a TYPE/option value in output settings.
2. **Meaning**: the descriptive explanation of what the quantity represents (e.g., “Lower maximum reinforcement”).
3. **Dim.**: the dimension/unit shown for that quantity (e.g., `cm2/m`, `N/mm2`, `kN`). A dash (`-`) indicates a dimensionless ratio/index.

### Literal groups and semantics
- **Reinforcement disks / reinforcement indices (bending design)**  
  Many codes start with `AS...` and represent **reinforcement per meter** in different roles:
  - `ASLM`, `ASLM`: lower maximum reinforcement (`cm2/m`)
  - `ASLQ`, `ASL...` style entries here focus on “lower” or “ratio/principal/transverse” interpretations:
  - Total/principal/transverse/3rd layer/max:  
    `AS` (Total reinforcement disks), `ASH` (principal disks), `ASQ` (transverse disks), `ASI` (3rd layer disks), `ASM` (maximum disks), all with unit `cm2/m`.
  - Ratios:  
    `ASV` (principal/transverse reinforcement disks ratio, dimensionless `-`).
  - Indices:  
    `ASX` and `ASLX` are reinforcement indices per element (dimension reported as `kg` in the table) and represent a kind of “index” rather than area.

- **Stirrups and punching-related reinforcement**
  - `ASSB`: stirrup reinforcement (`cm2/m2`)
  - Punching:
    - `PUNC`: punching (`-`)
    - `ASPS`: punching and stirrup reinforcement (`cm2/m2`)
  - Stirrup per element:
    - `ASSE`: stirrup reinforcement/element (`cm2`)
    - `ASSX`: stirrup reinforcement index per element (`kg`)

- **Error in design with BEMESS**
  - `ASER`: “Error in the design with program BEMESS” (`-`), indicating a status/error measure used for interpretation of BEMESS-based design checks.

- **Concrete shear/decompression/fatigue/utilization and shear checks**
  - `TAU0`: design shear stress tau (= V/(b·z) or V/(b·d)) (`N/mm2`)
  - `ZMİN`: minimum lever arm (`m`)
  - `VEDR`: `max.VED / VRdmax` utilization-like ratio (`-`)
  - `UTIC`: maximum utilization fatigue check concrete (`-`)
  - `VSD`: maximum design shear force VSD (`kN`)
  - `COTT`: maximum cot-theta (`-`)
  - `HVMW` / `HVMO`: shift rule values with respect to reinforcement consideration (`m`)

- **Tendon decompression strain**
  - `DCSA`: decompression strain direction above the tendons (`0/00` style indicates strain in per-mille format)
  - `DCSB`: decompression strain direction below the tendons (`0/00`)

### Overall interpretation
The table serves as a **controlled vocabulary** for interpreting SOFiSTiK output/design result codes. When a configuration specifies one of these literals, the system (or user) should interpret the produced quantity according to the given meaning and associated unit. This is critical for RAG retrieval because the code-to-meaning mapping is often needed to explain plots, isolines/cuts legends, or reinforcement/punching/shear/fatigue check results in technical documentation.

content:
The table documents **possible reinforcement-related “literals” (codes) for the QUAD TYPE parameter** used in SOFiSTiK graphical output (e.g., WING). Each entry maps a short code to a **meaning** and a **display unit**. All listed values are **reinforcement quantities expressed as reinforcement disks per unit length**, indicating they are intended for **reinforcement design drawings**, particularly where reinforcement is represented as “disks” or “mats” with different layers and orientations (lower/upper, principal/transverse, and 3rd layer).

### Column structure
- **Literal**: a short symbolic identifier (e.g., `ABL`, `ABUH`) that selects the data series to be represented.
- **Meaning**: human-readable description of what is being plotted.
- **Dim.**: the associated dimension/unit; in this table, all reinforcement entries use:
  - **`cm²/m`** (area of reinforcement per meter), consistent with reinforcement disk densities.

### Listed literals and their grouped intent
The entries are organized by logical categories:

1. **Lower reinforcement (baseline / “ABL…” group)**
   - `ABL` – Lower reinforcement (`cm²/m`)
   - `ABLH` – Lower principal reinforcement (`cm²/m`)
   - `ABLQ` – Lower transverse reinforcement (`cm²/m`)
   - `ABLI` – Lower 3rd reinforcement layer (`cm²/m`)
   - `ABLM` – Lower maximum reinforcement (`cm²/m`)

   These codes distinguish whether the plotted quantity is **total**, **principal direction**, **transverse direction**, **third layer**, or the **maximum** reinforcement for the lower zone.

2. **Reinforcement bending design information only (AB… group)**
   - `AB` – Total reinforcement disks (`cm²/m`)
   - `ABH` – Principal reinforcement disks (`cm²/m`)
   - `ABQ` – Transverse reinforcement disks (`cm²/m`)
   - `ABI` – 3rd reinforcement layer disks (`cm²/m`)
   - `ABM` – Maximum reinforcement disks (`cm²/m`)

   This subgroup is explicitly labeled “Info reinforcement bending design only,” indicating these literals are relevant when the underlying calculation includes/outputs reinforcement bending design data.

3. **Reinforcement due to shear (A…IU… group for upper zone)**
   - `AIU` – Upper reinforcement (`cm²/m`)
   - `AIUH` – Upper principal reinforcement (`cm²/m`)
   - `AIUQ` – Upper transverse reinforcement (`cm²/m`)
   - `AIUI` – Upper 3rd reinforcement layer (`cm²/m`)
   - `AIUM` – Upper maximum reinforcement (`cm²/m`)

   These are “info reinforcement if increased due to shear,” focusing on the **upper** side and again splitting into total/principal/transverse/third-layer/maximum forms.

4. **Reinforcement due to shear (A…IL… group for lower zone)**
   - `AIL` – Lower reinforcement (`cm²/m`)
   - `AILH` – Lower principal reinforcement (`cm²/m`)
   - `AILQ` – Lower transverse reinforcement (`cm²/m`)
   - `AILI` – Lower 3rd reinforcement layer (`cm²/m`)
   - `AILM` – Lower maximum reinforcement (`cm²/m`)

5. **Reinforcement due to shear (AI… group, combined total)**
   - `AI` – Total reinforcement disks (`cm²/m`)
   - `AIH` – Principal reinforcement disks (`cm²/m`)
   - `AIQ` – Transverse reinforcement disks (`cm²/m`)
   - `AII` – 3rd reinforcement layer disks (`cm²/m`)

### Contextual meaning for RAG retrieval
Overall, the table provides **a controlled vocabulary** of QUAD-type literals for **reinforcement plotting**. It encodes:
- **Position**: lower (`AB*L`), upper (`AIU*`), or combined/total (`AB*`, `AI`)
- **Orientation**: principal (`*H`), transverse (`*Q`)
- **Layer**: third layer (`*I`)
- **Design selection**: maximum reinforcement (`*M`)
- **Quantity type**: reinforcement “disks” used for bending/shear design outputs

All entries share the same unit (**cm²/m**), so the key differentiation for usage is the **literal code**, not the unit.

sections: 3.44 QUAD – Single Results of QUAD Elements

content:
The table defines a mapping between **SOFiSTiK GRAPHIC output “literals”** and their **meaning** and **physical dimension** (unit). Each row contains three fields: **Literal**, **Meaning**, and **Dim.** The literals are short codes used to select which stress/strain-related quantity is represented for a given graphical result.

## 1) Stress results after an elastic stress calculation (theory of elasticity)
Rows in this block specify stresses with **dimensions in N/mm²** (i.e., MPa). The prefixes indicate stress location and extrema:

- **SMIU**: *Upper minimum stresses* — **N/mm²**
- **SMAU**: *Upper maximum stresses* — **N/mm²**
- **SMIL**: *Lower minimum stresses* — **N/mm²**
- **SMAL**: *Lower maximum stresses* — **N/mm²**

Additional shear/stress combination measures:

- **TAUM**: *Minimum shear stresses* — **N/mm²**
- **VSMA**: *Maximum v. Mises stress* — **N/mm²**
- **VSMU**: *Upper v. Mises stress* — **N/mm²**
- **VSML**: *Lower v. Mises stress* — **N/mm²**

Overall, this block is for **elastic (linear) stress outputs**, distinguishing **upper vs. lower** results (typically top/bottom of plate layers or element faces) and **minimum vs. maximum** envelopes.

## 2) Stress ranges of material (e.g., fatigue-relevant range quantities)
The second block labels outputs for a **stress range** concept, also given in **N/mm²**. “Upper” and “Lower” are used as bounds within a directional or temporal range definition, and an additional directional variant is provided:

- **SDU**: *Upper stress range* — **N/mm²**
- **SDL**: *Lower stress range* — **N/mm²**
- **SDUI**: *Upper minimum stress in direction of stress range* — **N/mm²**
- **SDLI**: *Lower minimum stress in direction of stress range* — **N/mm²**
- **SDUA**: *Upper maximum stress in direction of stress range* — **N/mm²**
- **SDLA**: *Lower maximum stress in direction of stress range* — **N/mm²**
- **SDPU**: *Upper permanent stress in direction of stress range* — **N/mm²**
- **SDPL**: *Lower permanent stress in direction of stress range* — **N/mm²**

Hence, the literals encode whether the result is an **envelope** component (**upper/lower**, **min/max**) or a **permanent** component, and whether it is expressed **in the direction associated with the stress range**.

## 3) Crack width design values after a strain calculation (SLS)
The third block shifts from stresses to **crack width design** after an **SLS strain calculation**, with units in **mm**. It distinguishes **maximum** crack width and **layer-specific** crack widths for top and bottom reinforcement/layers:

Top crack widths:
- **WKUM**: *Maximum top crack width design* — **mm**
- **WKU1**: *Top crack width design 1st layer* — **mm**
- **WKU2**: *Top crack width design 2nd layer* — **mm**
- **WKU3**: *Top crack width design third layer* — **mm**

Bottom crack widths:
- **WKLmM** (shown as **WKLM**): *Maximum bottom crack width design* — **mm**
- **WKL1**: *Bottom crack width design 1st layer* — **mm**
- **WKL2**: *Bottom crack width design 2nd layer* — **mm**
- **WKL3**: *Bottom crack width design third layer* — **mm**

Crack width design “disks” (distribution representation):
- **WKM**: *Maximum crack width design disks* — **mm**
- **WK1**: *Crack width design 1st layer disks* — **mm**
(Additional disk/layer variants may continue beyond the visible table.)

### Key interpretation for RAG
When ingesting this table for retrieval, treat it as a **codebook**: each literal is a selector for a particular **result type** (elastic extremal stresses, stress-range components, or crack width design outputs), and the dimension column is essential for disambiguation and for validating result types during query-time.

sections: 3.44 QUAD – Single Results of QUAD Elements

content:
The table defines **material/structural response types related to stiffness** and specifies (1) the **literal name** used in the system and (2) its **meaning** and **dimension**.

## Table schema
- **Literal**: a short code (e.g., `SH0`) that selects what quantity is represented.
- **Meaning**: a German/engineering description of the physical quantity.
- **Dim.**: the unit/dimension of the represented value.

## Rows and interpretation
1. **`SH0` — “Stiffness on halfspace surface”**  
   - **Meaning**: stiffness evaluated **at the interface surface** of the half-space (i.e., the ground/elastic half-space model surface).  
   - **Dim.**: **MPa** (megapascal), indicating stress-like stiffness magnitude.

2. **`SH1` — “Stiffness 1 m below the halfspace surface”**  
   - **Meaning**: stiffness evaluated at a depth of **1 meter below** the half-space surface.  
   - **Dim.**: **MPa**.

3. **`SH2` — “Stiffness 2 m below the halfspace surface”**  
   - **Meaning**: stiffness evaluated at a depth of **2 meters below** the half-space surface.  
   - **Dim.**: **MPa**.

## Overall use in analysis/graphics
These literals are specialized **stiffness** outputs tied to the **depth in a half-space** model. Selecting `SH0`, `SH1`, or `SH2` changes only the **evaluation depth** (surface, 1 m, or 2 m), while the **unit remains MPa**. This is consistent with the broader context where QUAD/element result types can vary by what is sampled (e.g., center vs. nodes vs. Gauss points) and by whether results come from linear/non-linear calculations; here, the table specifically governs **depth-dependent stiffness values** for the half-space.

sections: 3.44 QUAD – Single Results of QUAD Elements

content:
The table is a legend/lookup for **SOFiSTiK “QUAD” result types** used in graphical post-processing (e.g., in WING/GRAPHIC). It specifies a set of **literals** that select different **stiffness-related values in a half-space** at various depths below the half-space surface. The relevant columns are:

- **LITERAL**: Short code that identifies the quantity to be plotted.
- **MEANING**: Human-readable description of what the code represents.
- **DIM.**: Measurement unit/dimension for the plotted value.

### Rows (stiffness of half-space at depth)
Each row indicates the **stiffness at a specific depth** beneath the half-space surface, measured in **MPa**:

1. **SH3** — *Stiffness 3 m below the halfspace surface* — **MPa**
2. **SH5** — *Stiffness 5 m below the halfspace surface* — **MPa**
3. **SH10** — *Stiffness 10 m below the halfspace surface* — **MPa**
4. **SH15** — *Stiffness 15 m below the halfspace surface* — **MPa**
5. **SH20** — *Stiffness 20 m below the halfspace surface* — **MPa**
6. **SH30** — *Stiffness 30 m below the halfspace surface* — **MPa**

### Interpretation for RAG/use in queries
When a user asks for “QUAD stiffness at depth” or “half-space stiffness SH10/SH20…”, the correct matches are these literals and descriptions. The key takeaway is that the codes differ only by depth (**3, 5, 10, 15, 20, 30 m**), and **all share the same unit: MPa**. This makes the table suitable for answering both: (a) which literal to use for a desired depth and (b) what quantity a given literal corresponds to.

### Relationship to surrounding context
In the broader QUAD documentation, **QUAD TYPE** determines what result field is represented. While the shown snippet specifically covers **SH* stiffness values**, it fits the same mechanism: selecting a TYPE/literal controls the plotted quantity and its physical unit. The table’s entries are therefore concrete “TYPE literals” for half-space stiffness output at predefined depths.

sections: 3.44 QUAD – Single Results of QUAD Elements

content:
The QUAD table defines **how single-valued results are represented for quadrilateral (plate) elements** in graphical output (e.g., WING/SOFISTiK). The table is structured as a mapping from a **LITERAL** (code used by the software) to a **Meaning** and its **physical dimension (Dim.)**. These literals typically correspond to result quantities computed by different analysis modules (e.g., thermal/fluid or FE programs) and then displayed either on nodes, element centres, Gauss points, or as derived quantities.

### Literal meanings shown in the table (with units)
**Temperature / thermal head**
- **TEMP**: Temperature (**K**)
- **TMPK**: Temperature (**°C**)
- **H**: Potential (**m**)  
- **HF**: Potential with free surface (**m**)  
- **PH**: Piezometric height (**m**)  

**Pressure-related quantities**
- **PRES**: Pressure (**kN/m²**)  
- **PREX**: Resulting pressure on an area in global X (**kN/m²**)  
- **PREY**: Resulting pressure on an area in global Y (**kN/m²**)  
- **PREZ**: Resulting pressure on an area in global Z (**kN/m²**)  
- **PS**: Pressure of saturation of steam (from temperature) (**Pa**)  

### Fluid-velocity fields (from different programs)
The table distinguishes whether velocities are obtained from **DOLFYN** or **HYDRA** and whether they are reported as **vector components** or full **magnitudes**.

**From DOLFYN**
- **NFL (nodes)**: Fluid velocity in nodes (**m/sec**)  
- **NFLK**: Fluid velocities in nodes in components (**m/sec**)  
- **NFLX**: Fluid velocity in nodes in global X (**m/sec**)  
- **NFLY**: Fluid velocity in nodes in global Y (**m/sec**)  
- **NFLZ**: Fluid velocity in nodes in global Z (**m/sec**)  

**From HYDRA**
- **FL (field result)**: Fluid velocity (**m/sec**)  
- **FLKO**: Fluid velocities in components (**m/sec**)  
- **FLX**: Fluid velocity in X (**m/sec**)  
- **FLY**: Fluid velocity in Y (**m/sec**)  
- **FLZ**: Fluid velocity in Z (**m/sec**)  

### Particle velocity and heat flux
**Particle velocity**
- **PA**: Particle velocity (**m/sec**)  
- **PAKO**: Particle velocities in components (**m/sec**)  
- **PAX**: Particle velocity in X (**m/sec**)  
- **PAY**: Particle velocity in Y (**m/sec**)  
- **PAZ**: Particle velocity in Z (**m/sec**)  

**Heat**
- **HT**: Heat flux (**m/sec** in the table)  
- **HTKO**: Heat flux in components (**m/sec** in the table)  

### Important context for RAG usage
Although this particular snippet lists only **LITERAL → meaning → unit**, it belongs to the broader QUAD definition where the system also supports:
- choosing where values are taken from (**centre of QUAD, Gauss points, nodes, BRIC points, error estimates**) via a separate QUAD-type mechanism (e.g., “STYP …” in the surrounding documentation),
- representing values as vectors/lines or scalar fields,
- and computing cut/isolines from nodal values derived from Gauss-point distributions.

So, for retrieval: interpret these literals as **thermo-fluid quantities on QUAD-based results**, while the **actual spatial sampling location and representation style** are controlled elsewhere (by QUAD-type selection and representation settings, not by the literal alone).

sections: 3.44 QUAD – Single Results of QUAD Elements

content:
This table defines a set of **literals (item codes)** used by SOFiSTiK/GRAPHIC (as part of a visualization/representation system) to label physical result quantities. Each row maps a **code** to its **meaning** (“Meaning”) and provides the corresponding **dimension/unit** (“Dim.”). The quantities largely pertain to **heat transfer and fluid/flow-related results**, likely from thermo-hydraulic or CFD-like analyses that include both heat flux and mass/energy transport terms.

### Columns
1. **Literal**
   - A short identifier (e.g., `HTX`, `Q`, `MUE*T`) that selects a specific result component in output/graphical rendering.
2. **Meaning**
   - Human-readable description of what the selected quantity represents.
3. **Dim.**
   - The physical unit/dimension associated with the literal.

### Defined literals and interpretation
- **Heat flux components**
  - `HTX`: Heat flux in X, unit **m/sec** (as given in the table)
  - `HTY`: Heat flux in Y, unit **m/sec**
  - `HTZ`: Heat flux in Z, unit **m/sec**
  These suggest directional heat transport across coordinate axes.

- **Flow / volumetric or mass flow quantities**
  - `Q`: Flow quantities, unit **1/sec**
  - `ON`: Flow quantities in nodes, unit **1/sec**
  These indicate flow rates globally (`Q`) and discretized at nodes (`QN` would be the analogous notion; here `ON` is used).

- **Heat quantities**
  - `HEAT`: Heat quantities in nodes, unit **W**
  - `TOHT`: Total flux, unit **W**
  These relate to thermal accumulation and total transferred energy flux.

- **Liquid fraction and turbulence-related variables**
  - `LFR`: Liquid fraction, unit **-** (dimensionless)
  - `MUET`: Turbulent viscosity, unit **kNsec/m²**
  - `TE`: Turbulent kinetic energy, unit **m²/sec²**
  - `TDN`: Turbulent dissipation rate, unit **m²/sec³**
  These are typical turbulence-model outputs and phase/mixture information.

- **Boundary layer and age**
  - `HO(P)T`: Boundary layer, unit **m**
  - `AGE`: Effective Age, unit **h**
  These characterize a boundary-layer metric and a time-like “age” variable (e.g., curing/maturation/effective age in materials).

- **Smoke-related concentration**
  - `SMOK`: Smoke concentration, unit **g/m³**
  This is a scalar concentration variable for smoke/particulates.

### Relation to broader context (QUAD/TYPE/STYP)
While this specific table is a **literal-to-quantity mapping** (used to choose what to visualize or report), the surrounding context in the provided text describes how QUAD element results are represented with different **TYPE** and **STYP** options (e.g., values at element centres, Gauss points, nodes; stress components; etc.). In that framework, these literals would typically be used as **TYPE-like selectors** for which field is drawn or output, while **STYP/REPR** control where/how the value is sampled (centre vs. Gauss vs. node) and the visualization style (vectors, isolines, cuts, etc.).

Note: The listed units for heat flux (`HTX/HTY/HTZ`) appear as **m/sec** in the table, which is atypical for heat flux (normally power per area). For RAG, treat the unit text as authoritative as provided, even if it seems physically inconsistent.

 The quadrilateral elements in SOFiSTiK includes five Gauss points. Four points are located near the corners and one point in the middle of element.
 The point in the middle corresponds to the value ’Centre of QUAD elements’ (STYP QUAD). For some non-linear results, it is possible to printout with ’Gauss points’ (STYP GAUS) the values of the four Gauss points which are located near the corners.

metadata.sections: 3.44 QUAD – Single Results of QUAD Elements

content:
Four points are located near the corners and one point in the middle of element.. The point in the middle corresponds to the value ’Centre of QUAD elements’ (STYP QUAD). For some non-linear results, it is possible to printout with ’Gauss points’ (STYP GAUS) the values of the four Gauss points which are located near the corners..
 In order to get a smoothed distribution of these values of the four Gauss points which are lo- cated near the corners, WING is able to calculate an averaged value of all Gauss points in the node which is important for cuts or isolines. This value is called ’Averaging node values, read from Gauss points’ (STYP G2N).
 The programs for the analysis (eg. ASE) calculate the nodal values using an extrapolation of the values of the four Gauss points into the nodes and average them about all adjacent ele- ments. In WING it is value ’Nodes of QUAD elements’ (STYP NODE).
 Sometimes the programs do not determine values in the nodes, e.g. in the case of a superpo- sition only for ’ETYP QUAD’ in program MAXIMA and missing input ’ETYP QNOD’ for values in the nodes although these nodal values are necessary for the graphical presentation of isolines or cuts. In such cases it makes sense to calculate temporarily the nodal values of the ’Centre of QUAD elements’ by shifting the value of the centre into the nodes. Subsequently, this value is averaged about all adjacent elements. This value is called ’Averaging node values, read from element centre’ (STYP E2N).
 The programs of the analysis are able to calculate error estimates in the centre of the elements. These values are the ’Error estimates in centre’ (STYP ERIN).
 However, since no error estimates are calculated in the nodes by the programs during analy- sis, WING can determine them similarly to the STYP E2N. This corresponds to the ’averaging node values, read from error estimates’ (STYP EE2N).
 The volume elements are correspondingly used, however, they can have up to eight Gauss points.
 The point in the middle of the volume element corresponds to the value ’Centre of BRIC ele- ments’ (STYP BRIC).
