 The nodal values of the BRIC elements which are calculated with the programs of the analysis are output with ’Nodes of BRIC elements’ (STYP BRIK).
 Representation as Tensor / Vector (REPR DVEC,DARE,DREP,DTXT):
 • A line in the corresponding length is drawn in its real size in the two projected directions (see record VIEW) for TYPE HM, HN, HS, BM, NS, N, HSU, HSL, EPSU, EPSL, SIIU, SIIL, S2U, S2L, WU, WL, WRU, WRL as well as ASL, ASU. Negative values get short limit lines for the differentiation. The value is measurable as long as the effect direction is not perpendicular to the drawing sheet.
 • The vector of the flow velocities is drawn in its projected direction for TYPE FL, PA and Q.
 • All other (single) values are drawn in their effective direction. Also isolines, cuts and fill area are possible here.
 • An error estimate can be printed with STYP ERIN for TYPE HM, MX, MY, MXY, BV, VX, VY, HN, NX, NY, NS, SX, SY, SZ, TXY and OPTG, if it was requested for the calculation.
 The punching results (TYPE PUNC, ASPS) use the colour C14 (record COLO) for the text, the colour C4 for the drawing of the column cross section or the enlarged column head and the colour C13 for the punching circle. An input for a minimum value (record SCH2 item MIN1) which should be represented is compared with the support reaction.
 Representation at Isolines (REPR DISO)
 The isolines are calculated one element at a time from the nodal values and drawn. The isolines are defined within each element with a hyperbola. The lines are straight, if the part of the hyperbola is small.

metadata.sections: 3.44 QUAD – Single Results of QUAD Elements

content:
An input for a minimum value (record SCH2 item MIN1) which should be represented is compared with the support reaction.. Representation at Isolines (REPR DISO). The isolines are calculated one element at a time from the nodal values and drawn. The isolines are defined within each element with a hyperbola. The lines are straight, if the part of the hyperbola is small..
 The designation of the isolines occurs in such a way that the text is readable so called uphill. A designation must be input explicitly with SCHH, if more than 50 isoline values are active.
 The isolines may be designated in intervals (DTXT). GRAPHIC searches for favourable posi- tions within subareas whose size has to be defined via CDIS. The program does not search for closed lines to designate the isolines. CDIS acts only to the designation of the isolines with the same value. An overwriting can not be prevented always in the case of a different level.
 The TYPE FLIE is only possible after a non-linear calculation (programs TALPA, ASE-IV). Usu- ally then the item FROM should be input with zero. In this case only the plasticized areas are represented.
 The types ASUM and ASLM are suitable for reinforcement drawings, if reinforcement mats should be used. For reinforcement mats with transverse reinforcement it is helpful to designate the elements with QUAD ASUR and ASLR additionally, if the transverse reinforcements is larger than 20 percent.
 A reinforcement representation as isolines or in cuts is only reasonable, if the positioning of the reinforcement (direction) is equal in all used elements.
 Either the values of the nodes are directly available or the values are determined from the element values. This may be controlled with an input for STYP.
 Representation at Cuts (REPR DCUT)
 All active DRAW elements with an input for DTYP are cut with the structure (only QUAD elements). The results are represented as status lines along the cuts. The status lines can be marked and/or generated as areas. If only one fill pattern was defined, the colours C13 and C14 and this fill pattern are used.
 Some values can be transformed into the directions of the cut. In this case N is the direction of the cutting line and T is the direction in the element plane perpendicular to the cut.
 After a cut definition, weld seam stresses are also available (TYPE SWNU, SWNL, SWNM, S3NU, S3NL, S3NM).

metadata.sections: 3.44 QUAD – Single Results of QUAD Elements

content:
Some values can be transformed into the directions of the cut. In this case N is the direction of the cutting line and T is the direction in the element plane perpendicular to the cut.. After a cut definition, weld seam stresses are also available (TYPE SWNU, SWNL, SWNM, S3NU, S3NL, S3NM)..
 As GRAPHIC does not know the exact geometry of the weld seam, the required values are approximated from the plate on which the cut lies. The following assumptions are made:
 • Thickness of weld seam = Thickness of the cut plate (area A = t ∗ 1m)
 σ⊥ = Normal stress in the plate that acts perpendicular to the cut (perpendicular to the weld seam)
 •
 τ∥ = Shear stress that lies in the plane of the plate, acting in the direction of the cut
 τ⊥ = Shear stress resulting from the shear forces V and Vy, acting in the cutting direction
 GRAPHIC calculates the stresses of the QUAD elements (plate) via N/A±M/W. In this context, middle (TYPE SWNM, S3NM) means that only the part N/A (slab centre) is used.

content:
This table defines the parameters for an **ISOL** element, i.e., an isolation/labeling construct that produces text-based output (notably controlled by a “TYPE” concept). It appears to act as a configuration block where some fields reference other records to supply additional layout and styling values.

**Columns**
- **Item**: Short mnemonic for a parameter.
- **Description**: Meaning and any special rules.
- **Unit**: Measurement unit or literal/data type indicator.
- **Default**: Default value used if not explicitly set (often `*` meaning “unspecified/derived elsewhere”).

**Key parameters**

1. **TYPE (Unit: LIT, Default: `*`)**
   - “Type which is supposed to be represented.”
   - The description states that **DSGN sets only input values and does not draw anything**.
   - It also specifies that “further literals” are taken from the **record QUAD TYPE**, meaning TYPE in this record likely maps to a literal/formatting definition stored in QUAD TYPE.
   - This parameter is therefore a selector for what will be represented and how related literals are interpreted.

2. **FROM / TO / INC (Source selection and iteration over isolates)**
   - **FROM** (Unit: `*`, Default: `*`): Indicates the starting value; it references **FILL ISOL FROM**.
   - **TO** (Unit: `*`, Default: `*`): Ending value; references **FILL ISOL TO**.
   - **INC** (Unit: `*`, Default: `*`): Increment step; references **FILL ISOL INC**.
   - Together these fields define a range and spacing used to determine which isolines/isolations (or designations) are generated.

3. **SCHH (Text height)**
   - **SCHH**: “Text height.”
   - **Unit**: `cm/LIT` (suggesting a scaling by literal type).
   - **Default**: `H6`.
   - Value is sourced via **record STRU**, implying font/structure conventions are centralized in STRU.

4. **STYP (Element type)**
   - **STYP**: “Element type.”
   - **Unit**: `LIT`.
   - **Default**: `NODE`.
   - Defined by referencing **record QUAD STYP**. This likely selects the graphical/text rendering class for the element.

5. **CINC (Increment of the designation)**
   - **CINC** (Unit: `*`, Default: `-1`):
   - Rules:
     - `< 0`: “Every n-th isoline” (uses the absolute magnitude to skip isolines).
     - `> 0`: “Increment in the dimension of TYPE” (ties step behavior to TYPE indexing rather than isoline count).

6. **CDIS (Minimum distance threshold between designations)**
   - **CDIS**: “Minimum distance of two designations with the same value.”
   - **Unit**: `cm`.
   - **Default**: `5.0`.
   - Interpretation: prevents label overlap by enforcing a minimum spacing rule.
   - It also states that this is based on “number of decimal points after comma,” suggesting formatting/rounding consistency matters.

7. **ND (Number of decimal points after comma)**
   - **ND** (Unit: `–/LIT`, Default: `*`):
   - Specifies decimal precision for numeric formatting.

This table serves as a **lookup reference** for interpreting result “literals” as specific measurable quantities with units and (often) computational provenance. In a retrieval system, queries about a literal (e.g., “What does `HTX` mean?” or “Unit for `PRES`?”) can be answered directly from the mapping, including the axis/component semantics and the source solver (DOL­FYN vs HYDRA).

The input table is a reference mapping that defines **literals** used in a visualization/representation system to indicate *what specific calculated quantity or design result should be plotted*, along with the **physical meaning** and its **dimension/unit**.

## Overall structure
The table has three columns:

1. **Literal** – a short code (e.g., `AS`, `DC`, `SR1`) used by the program/user to select the plotted quantity.
2. **Meaning** – a human-readable description of the quantity represented by that literal.
3. **Dim.** – the associated dimension/unit (or “-” if dimensionless).

## Reinforcement-related quantities (AS / AS1 / AS2 / AS3)
The first block lists reinforcement values in **three directions**:

- `AS`: Reinforcement in **3 directions**, unit **cm²/m**
- `AS1`: Reinforcement in **1st direction**, unit **cm²/m**
- `AS2`: Reinforcement in **2nd direction**, unit **cm²/m**
- `AS3`: Reinforcement in **3rd direction**, unit **cm²/m**

This suggests the system can display reinforcement density separated by directional components.

## Decisive design check block (DC / DC1 / DC2 / DC3)
A second block defines “decisive design check” outputs, again split by the same three directions:

- `DC`: Decisive design check → Reinforcement in **3 directions**, unit **-** (dimensionless)
- `DC1`: Decisive design check → Reinforcement in **1st direction**, unit **-**
- `DC2`: Decisive design check → Reinforcement in **2nd direction**, unit **-**
- `DC3`: Decisive design check → Reinforcement in **3rd direction**, unit **-**

Here, the dimension is given as “-”, indicating the result is likely a check factor, utilization, or boolean-like design metric rather than a physical density.

## Strain-life / SLS block (SRM / SR / SR1 / SR2 / SR3 / CPM)
A third block is explicitly “After a strain calculation (SLS)”. It covers stress range outputs and an additional design pressure quantity:

- `SRM`: Maximum stress range, unit **N/mm²**
- `SR`: Stress range in **3 directions**, unit **N/mm²**
- `SR1`: Stress range in **1st direction**, unit **N/mm²**
- `SR2`: Stress range in **2nd direction**, unit **N/mm²**
- `SR3`: Stress range in **3rd direction**, unit **N/mm²**
- `CPM`: Maximum SLS design concrete pressure, unit **N/mm²**

This block indicates that after an SLS (serviceability limit state) strain/stress evaluation, the system can plot fatigue-related or range-based stress metrics and corresponding concrete pressure design results.

The table is a schema/overview describing how configuration “SET” records and their parameters (“PAR1…PARn”) are organized. It contains three columns: **Item**, **Description**, and **Unit/Default** (the screenshot shows a “Unit” and a “Default” column; for this overview they are often marked with “–” or “*” because the actual meaning depends on the specific SET and parameter).

## Structure and meaning
- **Item (first column)**: Identifies the record type and the specific parameter index.
  - **SET**: A top-level record that groups related switches/properties. The table lists which “SET numbers” exist in this configuration.
  - **PAR1, PAR9, PAR10, …, PAR27**: Individual parameters inside a given SET. Their meaning and units depend on the parent SET and on which interaction phase the program is in (interactive input vs. later execution).

- **Description (second column)**: Explains what the item represents and, for **SET**, provides a mapping of SET subranges to functional areas.

- **Unit and Default (right columns)**:
  - For **SET**, the table shows “–” because “SET” is a summary container rather than a single value with a consistent unit/default.
  - For **PAR*** entries, the table uses “*” to indicate that units/defaults are not uniform across parameters; they must be interpreted per the detailed SET definition.

## SET summary (from the Description field)
The table states:
- **SET = Summary of switches**, with sub-items:
  - **0**: Current sheet / picture / layer
  - **1…7**: Interactive switch sets
  - **8**: Properties of the current printer
  - **9**: Precision of values (decimal places)
  - **11**: Properties of QUAD cuts
  - **12**: Properties of the cutting pattern (geodetic lines)
  - **13**: Properties of the additional lines
  - **14**: Properties of additional text
  - **15**: Properties of axes
  - **101**: Tolerances for the line representation
  - **102**: Further tolerances for line representation
  - **103**: Tolerances for the area representation

This indicates that the program’s configuration is modular: each SET number controls a distinct category (display, interaction, printing, geometry/cutting pattern behavior, or numerical tolerances).

## Parameter placeholders (PAR1…PAR27)
The table then lists parameter indices:
- **PAR1**: “Switch of different meaning according to the input for SET” (i.e., PAR1 is not universal; its semantics change depending on SET).
- **PAR9, PAR10, …, PAR27**: Additional parameters inside the selected SET definition (again, their meaning is SET-dependent).

## RAG usage implication
For retrieval, this table functions as an **index/dispatch map**: it tells you which SET blocks exist and that **PAR parameters are context-sensitive**. When embedding, the most useful facts are:
1) the catalog of SET categories (0, 1…7, 8, 9, 11–15, 101–103), and  
2) that PAR indices (e.g., PAR1, PAR9, PAR10, PAR27) must be resolved using the corresponding SET block definition rather than treated as having fixed units/default meanings.
